title: Wontui Tangkhul
subject: Literature
notes: Tangkhul literature textbook for Class II. Catalogued in Bharatavani textbook repository.

front_matter.preface: This textbook, Wontui Tangkhul (Class II), was formulated under the auspices of the Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS), Manipur (2022). It provides a structured, standardized curriculum from Chapter 1 to the concluding chapter, cultivating mother-tongue literacy, cultural values, grammar mastery, and creative expression for students in Class II.

chapters.title: Tuitam Khare: Iram Ukhrul (Homeland & Heritage)
chapters.summary: Introduction to the ancestral land of Ukhrul, scenic mountains, and community pride.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Iram Ukhrul hi kaphung kashungli kazei ram thotna. Wontui Tangkhul wui tuitam khareli ithum iramwui maran kala kaphana otbingli themkhapei. Shirui Kashong kaphungli Kashongwon wonri; Phangrei phungli mayarnaomayana laa shakda mathapamei.
chapters.english_translation: Our homeland Ukhrul is nestled high amidst the mountain ridges. In Chapter 1 of Wontui Tangkhul, we learn of the beauty, geography, and ancestral heritage of our hills. On Mount Shirui, the famed Shirui Lily blooms, and across Phangrei peak, youth sing songs of celebration.
grammar_points: Locative marker -li with geographical names: Ukhrul-li, Shirui-li.
Possessive compound: iram (i + ram = our land).
comprehension_questions: Which renowned rare flower blooms on Mount Shirui?
Describe the geographic landscape of Ukhrul in Tangkhul.

chapters.title: Khararchan: Tangkhul Folktales & Ancestral Lore
chapters.summary: Traditional legends including the tragic romance of Shimreishang and Maitonphi.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Shimreishang kala Maitonphi wui khararchan hi Tangkhul ngachaili leishat kachak wari thotna. Phungcham ramli kapam Maitonphi kachihi ramwui won kapha thotna; Shimreishangna awui ningli leikashi pamei. Kha shiyan khangatei eina thot kakhara kachang leiyi.
chapters.english_translation: The folktale of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most celebrated romance in Tangkhul oral tradition. Living in Phungcham village, Maitonphi was the fairest blossom of the land; Shimreishang loved her dearly. Yet clan custom and fateful trials intervened.
grammar_points: Narrative past tense marked with -yi and -thotna.
Adjectival clause modification of character names.
comprehension_questions: In which historic village did Maitonphi reside?
What moral values does the legend of Shimreishang and Maitonphi convey?

chapters.title: Paotam: Proverbs, Idioms & Elder Wisdom
chapters.summary: Proverbs transmitting customary ethics, diligence, honor, and community solidarity.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Paotam: 'Hanna hannui shaiphamei, tuiva arartui phamei.' 'Ot masa kakhana kachak mashamana.' 'Mayarnaona phasa mathada shiyan mashikha ramwui khangayung kakaso phamei.' Tuikashak arartuili Tangkhul ngashan kachak lei.
chapters.english_translation: Tangkhul Proverbs: 'Tender greens are savory, but elder counsel is sweeter.' 'One who does not labor shall not partake of harvest grain.' 'When young men uphold righteous conduct, the foundation of the community is honored.' These proverbial maxims encode ancestral philosophy.
grammar_points: Proverbs commonly use parallel couplet structures.
Comparative suffix -phamei conveys preferential moral superiority.
comprehension_questions: Explain the proverb 'Hanna hannui shaiphamei, tuiva arartui phamei'.
How do Tangkhul proverbs guide adolescent character formation?

chapters.title: Tangkhul Shiyan: Orthography & Phonetics
chapters.summary: Standard spellings, macron usage, aspirated consonants, and glottal tone marks.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS) na shiyan kashak shiyan: Sairik shiyan kashungli vowels khangashan ā, ē, ī, ō, ū shiyan mashungda kapi shiyan. Kakhalat kashak: 'sa' (to do) vs 'sā' (animal/meat); 'sha' (to hear) vs 'shā' (hundred).
chapters.english_translation: TLS orthographic standardization: Strict adherence to vowel length markings (ā, ē, ī, ō, ū). Minimal pairs demonstrate phonemic vowel length: 'sa' (to do) versus 'sā' (animal/flesh); 'sha' (to hear) versus 'shā' (hundred).
grammar_points: Minimal vowel length contrasts distinguish lexical meanings.
Capitalization conventions in written Tangkhul.
comprehension_questions: Illustrate three minimal word pairs distinguished by vowel length.
Why is standardized orthography essential for textbooks?

chapters.title: Tuiwon kala Tuikashak: Grammar & Parts of Speech
chapters.summary: Nouns, pronouns, verbs, case markers (-na, -li, -wui, -eina), and sentence syntax.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tuiwon kasak: Nouns take case suffixes: mayarnaona (subject), ali (object), shimwui (genitive). Verbs take aspect suffixes: sai (present), sada (past), sara (future). Clause syntax: Subject + Object + Verb (SOV).
chapters.english_translation: Grammatical structures: Nouns inflect for syntactic roles: agentive (-na), accusative (-li), possessive (-wui). Verbs mark tense and aspect: present (-i), past (-da), future (-ra). Canonical word order is Subject-Object-Verb.
grammar_points: Postpositional clitics attach to noun phrase boundaries.
Verb agreement is aspectual rather than person-concordant.
comprehension_questions: Identify the subject, object, and verb in: 'Mayarnaona lairik pari.'
List the past tense suffixes in modern Tangkhul.

chapters.title: Iram Ukhrul wui Phanit: Seasonal Festivals
chapters.summary: Cultural rituals and community celebrations: Luira (Seed Sowing), Mangkhap, and Chumpha.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Luira Phanit hi Tangkhul wui phanit kaphamei thotna. Luira tharan iram kaphungli laa shakda Haora kachon khonseri. Chumpha phanitli kachak kashak shimli ungkazip mathaser; Mangkhap tharan kaphung shungli ngashan shiyan mathathotna.
chapters.english_translation: The Luira seed-sowing festival is the premier seasonal observance of the Tangkhuls. Villagers sing ancestral melodies adorned in traditional Haora shawls. At Chumpha festival, newly harvested grain is consecrated, and during Mangkhap, community feasting strengthens communal bonds.
grammar_points: Temporal case suffix -tharan indicates 'during / at the time of'.
Cultural compound nouns (Luira Phanit, Haora Kachon).
comprehension_questions: What is the agricultural significance of the Luira festival?
Which traditional shawl is worn during seasonal celebrations?

chapters.title: Meila Won: Poetic Selections & Traditional Haola
chapters.summary: Classical and modern Tangkhul verses celebrating love, courage, nature, and longing.
chapters.tangkhul_text:
Laa tuitam: 'Phungreitangli meila won kapha wonri,
Zingsho kaphungli leishat laa shakri.
Iram Ukhrul ram wui thot mathamei,
Mayarnaomayana ningkachon pamei.'
Haola tuihi Tangkhul wui akhara shiyan thotna.
chapters.english_translation:
Poetic verse: 'On Phungreitang hill, lovely blossoms unfurl,
Across the eastern ridge, melodies of love arise.
Our Ukhrul homeland generation thrives,
In the hearts of our youth, true devotion endures.'
The Haola poetic genre encapsulates Tangkhul lyricism.
grammar_points: Rhyme and assonance in Tangkhul four-line poetic stanzas.
Repetition of floral and geographical metaphors.
comprehension_questions: What natural imagery is employed in the opening stanza of Meila Won?
Define the oral literary significance of Haola.

chapters.title: Kahaotui: Composition, Writing & Review Exercises
chapters.summary: Practical writing skills, letter composition, paragraph formulation, and chapter reviews.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Kapi shiyan: Lairik kapi, shiyan ngashitda chithi kapi. 'Izeishinaoli chithi: Izeinao kaphā, nali khamorwi kahang, ithumwui shimli ungkazip mathalu.' Tuikashak khangachan: Vowels shiyan mashunglu, tuiwon bingli case suffixes sanglu.
chapters.english_translation: Composition exercises: Essay writing and letter composition. 'Letter to a friend: Dear friend, I send you heartfelt greetings and invite you to join us at our home.' Review drills: Verify vowel markings and affix appropriate case suffixes.
grammar_points: Formal salutations in Tangkhul letter writing.
Syntactic coordination of compound sentences using 'kala' (and) and 'kha' (but).
comprehension_questions: Draft a five-sentence letter in Tangkhul inviting a friend to Luira festival.
Complete the grammatical review exercises on nominal cases.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 1: Tuitam Khare: Iram Ukhrul (Homeland & Heritage)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Iram Ukhrul hi kaphung kashungli kazei ram thotna. Wontui Tangkhul wui tuitam khareli ithum iramwui maran kala kaphana otbingli themkhapei. Shirui Kashong kaphungli Kashongwon wonri; Phangrei phungli mayarnaomayana laa shakda mathapamei.
excerpts.translation_en: Our homeland Ukhrul is nestled high amidst the mountain ridges. In Chapter 1 of Wontui Tangkhul, we learn of the beauty, geography, and ancestral heritage of our hills. On Mount Shirui, the famed Shirui Lily blooms, and across Phangrei peak, youth sing songs of celebration.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 2: Khararchan: Tangkhul Folktales & Ancestral Lore
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Shimreishang kala Maitonphi wui khararchan hi Tangkhul ngachaili leishat kachak wari thotna. Phungcham ramli kapam Maitonphi kachihi ramwui won kapha thotna; Shimreishangna awui ningli leikashi pamei. Kha shiyan khangatei eina thot kakhara kachang leiyi.
excerpts.translation_en: The folktale of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most celebrated romance in Tangkhul oral tradition. Living in Phungcham village, Maitonphi was the fairest blossom of the land; Shimreishang loved her dearly. Yet clan custom and fateful trials intervened.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 3: Paotam: Proverbs, Idioms & Elder Wisdom
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Paotam: 'Hanna hannui shaiphamei, tuiva arartui phamei.' 'Ot masa kakhana kachak mashamana.' 'Mayarnaona phasa mathada shiyan mashikha ramwui khangayung kakaso phamei.' Tuikashak arartuili Tangkhul ngashan kachak lei.
excerpts.translation_en: Tangkhul Proverbs: 'Tender greens are savory, but elder counsel is sweeter.' 'One who does not labor shall not partake of harvest grain.' 'When young men uphold righteous conduct, the foundation of the community is honored.' These proverbial maxims encode ancestral philosophy.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 4: Tangkhul Shiyan: Orthography & Phonetics
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS) na shiyan kashak shiyan: Sairik shiyan kashungli vowels khangashan ā, ē, ī, ō, ū shiyan mashungda kapi shiyan. Kakhalat kashak: 'sa' (to do) vs 'sā' (animal/meat); 'sha' (to hear) vs 'shā' (hundred).
excerpts.translation_en: TLS orthographic standardization: Strict adherence to vowel length markings (ā, ē, ī, ō, ū). Minimal pairs demonstrate phonemic vowel length: 'sa' (to do) versus 'sā' (animal/flesh); 'sha' (to hear) versus 'shā' (hundred).

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 5: Tuiwon kala Tuikashak: Grammar & Parts of Speech
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tuiwon kasak: Nouns take case suffixes: mayarnaona (subject), ali (object), shimwui (genitive). Verbs take aspect suffixes: sai (present), sada (past), sara (future). Clause syntax: Subject + Object + Verb (SOV).
excerpts.translation_en: Grammatical structures: Nouns inflect for syntactic roles: agentive (-na), accusative (-li), possessive (-wui). Verbs mark tense and aspect: present (-i), past (-da), future (-ra). Canonical word order is Subject-Object-Verb.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 6: Iram Ukhrul wui Phanit: Seasonal Festivals
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Luira Phanit hi Tangkhul wui phanit kaphamei thotna. Luira tharan iram kaphungli laa shakda Haora kachon khonseri. Chumpha phanitli kachak kashak shimli ungkazip mathaser; Mangkhap tharan kaphung shungli ngashan shiyan mathathotna.
excerpts.translation_en: The Luira seed-sowing festival is the premier seasonal observance of the Tangkhuls. Villagers sing ancestral melodies adorned in traditional Haora shawls. At Chumpha festival, newly harvested grain is consecrated, and during Mangkhap, community feasting strengthens communal bonds.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 7: Meila Won: Poetic Selections & Traditional Haola
excerpts.tangkhul_text:
Laa tuitam: 'Phungreitangli meila won kapha wonri,
Zingsho kaphungli leishat laa shakri.
Iram Ukhrul ram wui thot mathamei,
Mayarnaomayana ningkachon pamei.'
Haola tuihi Tangkhul wui akhara shiyan thotna.
excerpts.translation_en:
Poetic verse: 'On Phungreitang hill, lovely blossoms unfurl,
Across the eastern ridge, melodies of love arise.
Our Ukhrul homeland generation thrives,
In the hearts of our youth, true devotion endures.'
The Haola poetic genre encapsulates Tangkhul lyricism.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 8: Kahaotui: Composition, Writing & Review Exercises
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Kapi shiyan: Lairik kapi, shiyan ngashitda chithi kapi. 'Izeishinaoli chithi: Izeinao kaphā, nali khamorwi kahang, ithumwui shimli ungkazip mathalu.' Tuikashak khangachan: Vowels shiyan mashunglu, tuiwon bingli case suffixes sanglu.
excerpts.translation_en: Composition exercises: Essay writing and letter composition. 'Letter to a friend: Dear friend, I send you heartfelt greetings and invite you to join us at our home.' Review drills: Verify vowel markings and affix appropriate case suffixes.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 1: Tuitam Khare: Iram Ukhrul (Homeland & Heritage)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Iram Ukhrul hi kaphung kashungli kazei ram thotna. Zingyar Tangkhul wui tuitam khareli ithum iramwui maran kala kaphana otbingli themkhapei. Shirui Kashong kaphungli Kashongwon wonri; Phangrei phungli mayarnaomayana laa shakda mathapamei.
excerpts.translation_en: Our homeland Ukhrul is nestled high amidst the mountain ridges. In Chapter 1 of Zingyar Tangkhul, we learn of the beauty, geography, and ancestral heritage of our hills. On Mount Shirui, the famed Shirui Lily blooms, and across Phangrei peak, youth sing songs of celebration.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 2: Khararchan: Tangkhul Folktales & Ancestral Lore
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Shimreishang kala Maitonphi wui khararchan hi Tangkhul ngachaili leishat kachak wari thotna. Phungcham ramli kapam Maitonphi kachihi ramwui won kapha thotna; Shimreishangna awui ningli leikashi pamei. Kha shiyan khangatei eina thot kakhara kachang leiyi.
excerpts.translation_en: The folktale of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most celebrated romance in Tangkhul oral tradition. Living in Phungcham village, Maitonphi was the fairest blossom of the land; Shimreishang loved her dearly. Yet clan custom and fateful trials intervened.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 3: Paotam: Proverbs, Idioms & Elder Wisdom
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Paotam: 'Hanna hannui shaiphamei, tuiva arartui phamei.' 'Ot masa kakhana kachak mashamana.' 'Mayarnaona phasa mathada shiyan mashikha ramwui khangayung kakaso phamei.' Tuikashak arartuili Tangkhul ngashan kachak lei.
excerpts.translation_en: Tangkhul Proverbs: 'Tender greens are savory, but elder counsel is sweeter.' 'One who does not labor shall not partake of harvest grain.' 'When young men uphold righteous conduct, the foundation of the community is honored.' These proverbial maxims encode ancestral philosophy.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 4: Tangkhul Shiyan: Orthography & Phonetics
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS) na shiyan kashak shiyan: Sairik shiyan kashungli vowels khangashan ā, ē, ī, ō, ū shiyan mashungda kapi shiyan. Kakhalat kashak: 'sa' (to do) vs 'sā' (animal/meat); 'sha' (to hear) vs 'shā' (hundred).
excerpts.translation_en: TLS orthographic standardization: Strict adherence to vowel length markings (ā, ē, ī, ō, ū). Minimal pairs demonstrate phonemic vowel length: 'sa' (to do) versus 'sā' (animal/flesh); 'sha' (to hear) versus 'shā' (hundred).

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 5: Tuiwon kala Tuikashak: Grammar & Parts of Speech
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tuiwon kasak: Nouns take case suffixes: mayarnaona (subject), ali (object), shimwui (genitive). Verbs take aspect suffixes: sai (present), sada (past), sara (future). Clause syntax: Subject + Object + Verb (SOV).
excerpts.translation_en: Grammatical structures: Nouns inflect for syntactic roles: agentive (-na), accusative (-li), possessive (-wui). Verbs mark tense and aspect: present (-i), past (-da), future (-ra). Canonical word order is Subject-Object-Verb.

subject: Literature
notes: Tangkhul literature textbook for Class VI (Katharuka = Sixth). Catalogued in Bharatavani textbook repository.

front_matter.preface: This textbook, Zingshan Tangkhul Katharuka (Class VI), was formulated under the auspices of the Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS), Manipur (2021). It provides a structured, standardized curriculum from Chapter 1 to the concluding chapter, cultivating mother-tongue literacy, cultural values, grammar mastery, and creative expression for students in Class VI.

pages.header: Chapter 2: Khararchan: Tangkhul Folktales & Ancestral Lore (Page 6)
pages.title: Chapter 2: Khararchan: Tangkhul Folktales & Ancestral Lore
lines: CHAPTER 2: KHARARCHAN: TANGKHUL FOLKTALES & ANCESTRAL LORE
Summary: Traditional legends including the tragic romance of Shimreishang and Maitonphi.
Shimreishang kala Maitonphi wui khararchan hi Tangkhul ngachaili leishat
kachak wari thotna. Phungcham ramli kapam Maitonphi kachihi ramwui won
kapha thotna; Shimreishangna awui ningli leikashi pamei. Kha shiyan
khangatei eina thot kakhara kachang leiyi.
The folktale of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most celebrated
romance in Tangkhul oral tradition. Living in Phungcham village,
Maitonphi was the fairest blossom of the land; Shimreishang loved her
dearly. Yet clan custom and fateful trials intervened.

title: Zingshan Tangkhul Kashine
subject: Literature
notes: Tangkhul literature textbook for Class VII (Kashine = Seventh). Catalogued in Bharatavani textbook repository.

front_matter.preface: This textbook, Zingshan Tangkhul Kashine (Class VII), was formulated under the auspices of the Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS), Manipur (2019). It provides a structured, standardized curriculum from Chapter 1 to the concluding chapter, cultivating mother-tongue literacy, cultural values, grammar mastery, and creative expression for students in Class VII.

chapters.title: Tuitam Khare: Iram Ukhrul (Homeland & Heritage)
chapters.summary: Introduction to the ancestral land of Ukhrul, scenic mountains, and community pride.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Iram Ukhrul hi kaphung kashungli kazei ram thotna. Zingshan Tangkhul Kashine wui tuitam khareli ithum iramwui maran kala kaphana otbingli themkhapei. Shirui Kashong kaphungli Kashongwon wonri; Phangrei phungli mayarnaomayana laa shakda mathapamei.
chapters.english_translation: Our homeland Ukhrul is nestled high amidst the mountain ridges. In Chapter 1 of Zingshan Tangkhul Kashine, we learn of the beauty, geography, and ancestral heritage of our hills. On Mount Shirui, the famed Shirui Lily blooms, and across Phangrei peak, youth sing songs of celebration.
grammar_points: Locative marker -li with geographical names: Ukhrul-li, Shirui-li.
Possessive compound: iram (i + ram = our land).
comprehension_questions: Which renowned rare flower blooms on Mount Shirui?
Describe the geographic landscape of Ukhrul in Tangkhul.

chapters.title: Khararchan: Tangkhul Folktales & Ancestral Lore
chapters.summary: Traditional legends including the tragic romance of Shimreishang and Maitonphi.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Shimreishang kala Maitonphi wui khararchan hi Tangkhul ngachaili leishat kachak wari thotna. Phungcham ramli kapam Maitonphi kachihi ramwui won kapha thotna; Shimreishangna awui ningli leikashi pamei. Kha shiyan khangatei eina thot kakhara kachang leiyi.
chapters.english_translation: The folktale of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most celebrated romance in Tangkhul oral tradition. Living in Phungcham village, Maitonphi was the fairest blossom of the land; Shimreishang loved her dearly. Yet clan custom and fateful trials intervened.
grammar_points: Narrative past tense marked with -yi and -thotna.
Adjectival clause modification of character names.
comprehension_questions: In which historic village did Maitonphi reside?
What moral values does the legend of Shimreishang and Maitonphi convey?

chapters.title: Paotam: Proverbs, Idioms & Elder Wisdom
chapters.summary: Proverbs transmitting customary ethics, diligence, honor, and community solidarity.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Paotam: 'Hanna hannui shaiphamei, tuiva arartui phamei.' 'Ot masa kakhana kachak mashamana.' 'Mayarnaona phasa mathada shiyan mashikha ramwui khangayung kakaso phamei.' Tuikashak arartuili Tangkhul ngashan kachak lei.
chapters.english_translation: Tangkhul Proverbs: 'Tender greens are savory, but elder counsel is sweeter.' 'One who does not labor shall not partake of harvest grain.' 'When young men uphold righteous conduct, the foundation of the community is honored.' These proverbial maxims encode ancestral philosophy.
grammar_points: Proverbs commonly use parallel couplet structures.
Comparative suffix -phamei conveys preferential moral superiority.
comprehension_questions: Explain the proverb 'Hanna hannui shaiphamei, tuiva arartui phamei'.
How do Tangkhul proverbs guide adolescent character formation?

chapters.title: Tangkhul Shiyan: Orthography & Phonetics
chapters.summary: Standard spellings, macron usage, aspirated consonants, and glottal tone marks.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS) na shiyan kashak shiyan: Sairik shiyan kashungli vowels khangashan ā, ē, ī, ō, ū shiyan mashungda kapi shiyan. Kakhalat kashak: 'sa' (to do) vs 'sā' (animal/meat); 'sha' (to hear) vs 'shā' (hundred).
chapters.english_translation: TLS orthographic standardization: Strict adherence to vowel length markings (ā, ē, ī, ō, ū). Minimal pairs demonstrate phonemic vowel length: 'sa' (to do) versus 'sā' (animal/flesh); 'sha' (to hear) versus 'shā' (hundred).
grammar_points: Minimal vowel length contrasts distinguish lexical meanings.
Capitalization conventions in written Tangkhul.
comprehension_questions: Illustrate three minimal word pairs distinguished by vowel length.
Why is standardized orthography essential for textbooks?

chapters.title: Tuiwon kala Tuikashak: Grammar & Parts of Speech
chapters.summary: Nouns, pronouns, verbs, case markers (-na, -li, -wui, -eina), and sentence syntax.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tuiwon kasak: Nouns take case suffixes: mayarnaona (subject), ali (object), shimwui (genitive). Verbs take aspect suffixes: sai (present), sada (past), sara (future). Clause syntax: Subject + Object + Verb (SOV).
chapters.english_translation: Grammatical structures: Nouns inflect for syntactic roles: agentive (-na), accusative (-li), possessive (-wui). Verbs mark tense and aspect: present (-i), past (-da), future (-ra). Canonical word order is Subject-Object-Verb.
grammar_points: Postpositional clitics attach to noun phrase boundaries.
Verb agreement is aspectual rather than person-concordant.
comprehension_questions: Identify the subject, object, and verb in: 'Mayarnaona lairik pari.'
List the past tense suffixes in modern Tangkhul.

chapters.title: Iram Ukhrul wui Phanit: Seasonal Festivals
chapters.summary: Cultural rituals and community celebrations: Luira (Seed Sowing), Mangkhap, and Chumpha.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Luira Phanit hi Tangkhul wui phanit kaphamei thotna. Luira tharan iram kaphungli laa shakda Haora kachon khonseri. Chumpha phanitli kachak kashak shimli ungkazip mathaser; Mangkhap tharan kaphung shungli ngashan shiyan mathathotna.
chapters.english_translation: The Luira seed-sowing festival is the premier seasonal observance of the Tangkhuls. Villagers sing ancestral melodies adorned in traditional Haora shawls. At Chumpha festival, newly harvested grain is consecrated, and during Mangkhap, community feasting strengthens communal bonds.
grammar_points: Temporal case suffix -tharan indicates 'during / at the time of'.
Cultural compound nouns (Luira Phanit, Haora Kachon).
comprehension_questions: What is the agricultural significance of the Luira festival?
Which traditional shawl is worn during seasonal celebrations?

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 1: Tuitam Khare: Iram Ukhrul (Homeland & Heritage)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Iram Ukhrul hi kaphung kashungli kazei ram thotna. Zingshan Tangkhul Kashine wui tuitam khareli ithum iramwui maran kala kaphana otbingli themkhapei. Shirui Kashong kaphungli Kashongwon wonri; Phangrei phungli mayarnaomayana laa shakda mathapamei.
excerpts.translation_en: Our homeland Ukhrul is nestled high amidst the mountain ridges. In Chapter 1 of Zingshan Tangkhul Kashine, we learn of the beauty, geography, and ancestral heritage of our hills. On Mount Shirui, the famed Shirui Lily blooms, and across Phangrei peak, youth sing songs of celebration.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 2: Khararchan: Tangkhul Folktales & Ancestral Lore
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Shimreishang kala Maitonphi wui khararchan hi Tangkhul ngachaili leishat kachak wari thotna. Phungcham ramli kapam Maitonphi kachihi ramwui won kapha thotna; Shimreishangna awui ningli leikashi pamei. Kha shiyan khangatei eina thot kakhara kachang leiyi.
excerpts.translation_en: The folktale of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most celebrated romance in Tangkhul oral tradition. Living in Phungcham village, Maitonphi was the fairest blossom of the land; Shimreishang loved her dearly. Yet clan custom and fateful trials intervened.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 3: Paotam: Proverbs, Idioms & Elder Wisdom
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Paotam: 'Hanna hannui shaiphamei, tuiva arartui phamei.' 'Ot masa kakhana kachak mashamana.' 'Mayarnaona phasa mathada shiyan mashikha ramwui khangayung kakaso phamei.' Tuikashak arartuili Tangkhul ngashan kachak lei.
excerpts.translation_en: Tangkhul Proverbs: 'Tender greens are savory, but elder counsel is sweeter.' 'One who does not labor shall not partake of harvest grain.' 'When young men uphold righteous conduct, the foundation of the community is honored.' These proverbial maxims encode ancestral philosophy.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 4: Tangkhul Shiyan: Orthography & Phonetics
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS) na shiyan kashak shiyan: Sairik shiyan kashungli vowels khangashan ā, ē, ī, ō, ū shiyan mashungda kapi shiyan. Kakhalat kashak: 'sa' (to do) vs 'sā' (animal/meat); 'sha' (to hear) vs 'shā' (hundred).
excerpts.translation_en: TLS orthographic standardization: Strict adherence to vowel length markings (ā, ē, ī, ō, ū). Minimal pairs demonstrate phonemic vowel length: 'sa' (to do) versus 'sā' (animal/flesh); 'sha' (to hear) versus 'shā' (hundred).

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 5: Tuiwon kala Tuikashak: Grammar & Parts of Speech
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tuiwon kasak: Nouns take case suffixes: mayarnaona (subject), ali (object), shimwui (genitive). Verbs take aspect suffixes: sai (present), sada (past), sara (future). Clause syntax: Subject + Object + Verb (SOV).
excerpts.translation_en: Grammatical structures: Nouns inflect for syntactic roles: agentive (-na), accusative (-li), possessive (-wui). Verbs mark tense and aspect: present (-i), past (-da), future (-ra). Canonical word order is Subject-Object-Verb.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 6: Iram Ukhrul wui Phanit: Seasonal Festivals
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Luira Phanit hi Tangkhul wui phanit kaphamei thotna. Luira tharan iram kaphungli laa shakda Haora kachon khonseri. Chumpha phanitli kachak kashak shimli ungkazip mathaser; Mangkhap tharan kaphung shungli ngashan shiyan mathathotna.
excerpts.translation_en: The Luira seed-sowing festival is the premier seasonal observance of the Tangkhuls. Villagers sing ancestral melodies adorned in traditional Haora shawls. At Chumpha festival, newly harvested grain is consecrated, and during Mangkhap, community feasting strengthens communal bonds.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 7: Meila Won: Poetic Selections & Traditional Haola
excerpts.tangkhul_text:
Laa tuitam: 'Phungreitangli meila won kapha wonri,
Zingsho kaphungli leishat laa shakri.
Iram Ukhrul ram wui thot mathamei,
Mayarnaomayana ningkachon pamei.'
Haola tuihi Tangkhul wui akhara shiyan thotna.
excerpts.translation_en:
Poetic verse: 'On Phungreitang hill, lovely blossoms unfurl,
Across the eastern ridge, melodies of love arise.
Our Ukhrul homeland generation thrives,
In the hearts of our youth, true devotion endures.'
The Haola poetic genre encapsulates Tangkhul lyricism.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 1: Tuitam Khare: Iram Ukhrul (Homeland & Heritage)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Iram Ukhrul hi kaphung kashungli kazei ram thotna. Zingshan Tangkhul Kachishata wui tuitam khareli ithum iramwui maran kala kaphana otbingli themkhapei. Shirui Kashong kaphungli Kashongwon wonri; Phangrei phungli mayarnaomayana laa shakda mathapamei.
excerpts.translation_en: Our homeland Ukhrul is nestled high amidst the mountain ridges. In Chapter 1 of Zingshan Tangkhul Kachishata, we learn of the beauty, geography, and ancestral heritage of our hills. On Mount Shirui, the famed Shirui Lily blooms, and across Phangrei peak, youth sing songs of celebration.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 2: Khararchan: Tangkhul Folktales & Ancestral Lore
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Shimreishang kala Maitonphi wui khararchan hi Tangkhul ngachaili leishat kachak wari thotna. Phungcham ramli kapam Maitonphi kachihi ramwui won kapha thotna; Shimreishangna awui ningli leikashi pamei. Kha shiyan khangatei eina thot kakhara kachang leiyi.
excerpts.translation_en: The folktale of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most celebrated romance in Tangkhul oral tradition. Living in Phungcham village, Maitonphi was the fairest blossom of the land; Shimreishang loved her dearly. Yet clan custom and fateful trials intervened.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 3: Paotam: Proverbs, Idioms & Elder Wisdom
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Paotam: 'Hanna hannui shaiphamei, tuiva arartui phamei.' 'Ot masa kakhana kachak mashamana.' 'Mayarnaona phasa mathada shiyan mashikha ramwui khangayung kakaso phamei.' Tuikashak arartuili Tangkhul ngashan kachak lei.
excerpts.translation_en: Tangkhul Proverbs: 'Tender greens are savory, but elder counsel is sweeter.' 'One who does not labor shall not partake of harvest grain.' 'When young men uphold righteous conduct, the foundation of the community is honored.' These proverbial maxims encode ancestral philosophy.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 4: Tangkhul Shiyan: Orthography & Phonetics
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS) na shiyan kashak shiyan: Sairik shiyan kashungli vowels khangashan ā, ē, ī, ō, ū shiyan mashungda kapi shiyan. Kakhalat kashak: 'sa' (to do) vs 'sā' (animal/meat); 'sha' (to hear) vs 'shā' (hundred).
excerpts.translation_en: TLS orthographic standardization: Strict adherence to vowel length markings (ā, ē, ī, ō, ū). Minimal pairs demonstrate phonemic vowel length: 'sa' (to do) versus 'sā' (animal/flesh); 'sha' (to hear) versus 'shā' (hundred).

subject: Literature
notes: Tangkhul literature textbook for Class IX (Kachiko = Ninth). Catalogued in Bharatavani textbook repository.

front_matter.preface: This textbook, Tangkhul Tuitam Kachiko (Class IX), was formulated under the auspices of the Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS), Manipur (2000). It provides a structured, standardized curriculum from Chapter 1 to the concluding chapter, cultivating mother-tongue literacy, cultural values, grammar mastery, and creative expression for students in Class IX.

lines: CHAPTER 6: IRAM UKHRUL WUI PHANIT: SEASONAL FESTIVALS
Summary: Cultural rituals and community celebrations: Luira (Seed Sowing), Mangkhap, and Chumpha.
Luira Phanit hi Tangkhul wui phanit kaphamei thotna. Luira tharan iram
kaphungli laa shakda Haora kachon khonseri. Chumpha phanitli kachak
kashak shimli ungkazip mathaser; Mangkhap tharan kaphung shungli ngashan
The Luira seed-sowing festival is the premier seasonal observance of the
Tangkhuls. Villagers sing ancestral melodies adorned in traditional
Haora shawls. At Chumpha festival, newly harvested grain is consecrated,
and during Mangkhap, community feasting strengthens communal bonds.

front_matter.preface: This textbook, Tuitam Kathara (Class X), was formulated under the auspices of the Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS), Manipur (2021). lines: CHAPTER 1: TUITAM KHARE: IRAM UKHRUL (HOMELAND & HERITAGE)
Summary: Introduction to the ancestral land of Ukhrul, scenic mountains, and community pride.
Iram Ukhrul hi kaphung kashungli kazei ram thotna. Tuitam Kathara wui
tuitam khareli ithum iramwui maran kala kaphana otbingli themkhapei.
Shirui Kashong kaphungli Kashongwon wonri; Phangrei phungli
Our homeland Ukhrul is nestled high amidst the mountain ridges. In
Chapter 1 of Tuitam Kathara, we learn of the beauty, geography, and
ancestral heritage of our hills. On Mount Shirui, the famed Shirui Lily
blooms, and across Phangrei peak, youth sing songs of celebration.

pages.header: Chapter 2: Khararchan: Tangkhul Folktales & Ancestral Lore (Page 6)
pages.title: Chapter 2: Khararchan: Tangkhul Folktales & Ancestral Lore
lines: CHAPTER 2: KHARARCHAN: TANGKHUL FOLKTALES & ANCESTRAL LORE
Summary: Traditional legends including the tragic romance of Shimreishang and Maitonphi.
Shimreishang kala Maitonphi wui khararchan hi Tangkhul ngachaili leishat
kachak wari thotna. Phungcham ramli kapam Maitonphi kachihi ramwui won
kapha thotna; Shimreishangna awui ningli leikashi pamei. Kha shiyan
khangatei eina thot kakhara kachang leiyi.
The folktale of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most celebrated
romance in Tangkhul oral tradition. Living in Phungcham village,
Maitonphi was the fairest blossom of the land; Shimreishang loved her
dearly. Yet clan custom and fateful trials intervened.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 1: Tuitam Khare: Iram Ukhrul (Homeland & Heritage)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Iram Ukhrul hi kaphung kashungli kazei ram thotna. Tangkhul Grammar wui tuitam khareli ithum iramwui maran kala kaphana otbingli themkhapei. Shirui Kashong kaphungli Kashongwon wonri; Phangrei phungli mayarnaomayana laa shakda mathapamei.
excerpts.translation_en: Our homeland Ukhrul is nestled high amidst the mountain ridges. In Chapter 1 of Tangkhul Grammar, we learn of the beauty, geography, and ancestral heritage of our hills. On Mount Shirui, the famed Shirui Lily blooms, and across Phangrei peak, youth sing songs of celebration.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 2: Khararchan: Tangkhul Folktales & Ancestral Lore
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Shimreishang kala Maitonphi wui khararchan hi Tangkhul ngachaili leishat kachak wari thotna. Phungcham ramli kapam Maitonphi kachihi ramwui won kapha thotna; Shimreishangna awui ningli leikashi pamei. Kha shiyan khangatei eina thot kakhara kachang leiyi.
excerpts.translation_en: The folktale of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most celebrated romance in Tangkhul oral tradition. Living in Phungcham village, Maitonphi was the fairest blossom of the land; Shimreishang loved her dearly. Yet clan custom and fateful trials intervened.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 3: Paotam: Proverbs, Idioms & Elder Wisdom
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Paotam: 'Hanna hannui shaiphamei, tuiva arartui phamei.' 'Ot masa kakhana kachak mashamana.' 'Mayarnaona phasa mathada shiyan mashikha ramwui khangayung kakaso phamei.' Tuikashak arartuili Tangkhul ngashan kachak lei.
excerpts.translation_en: Tangkhul Proverbs: 'Tender greens are savory, but elder counsel is sweeter.' 'One who does not labor shall not partake of harvest grain.' 'When young men uphold righteous conduct, the foundation of the community is honored.' These proverbial maxims encode ancestral philosophy.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 4: Tangkhul Shiyan: Orthography & Phonetics
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS) na shiyan kashak shiyan: Sairik shiyan kashungli vowels khangashan ā, ē, ī, ō, ū shiyan mashungda kapi shiyan. Kakhalat kashak: 'sa' (to do) vs 'sā' (animal/meat); 'sha' (to hear) vs 'shā' (hundred).
excerpts.translation_en: TLS orthographic standardization: Strict adherence to vowel length markings (ā, ē, ī, ō, ū). Minimal pairs demonstrate phonemic vowel length: 'sa' (to do) versus 'sā' (animal/flesh); 'sha' (to hear) versus 'shā' (hundred).

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 5: Tuiwon kala Tuikashak: Grammar & Parts of Speech
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tuiwon kasak: Nouns take case suffixes: mayarnaona (subject), ali (object), shimwui (genitive). Verbs take aspect suffixes: sai (present), sada (past), sara (future). Clause syntax: Subject + Object + Verb (SOV).
excerpts.translation_en: Grammatical structures: Nouns inflect for syntactic roles: agentive (-na), accusative (-li), possessive (-wui). Verbs mark tense and aspect: present (-i), past (-da), future (-ra). Canonical word order is Subject-Object-Verb.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 6: Iram Ukhrul wui Phanit: Seasonal Festivals
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Luira Phanit hi Tangkhul wui phanit kaphamei thotna. Luira tharan iram kaphungli laa shakda Haora kachon khonseri. Chumpha phanitli kachak kashak shimli ungkazip mathaser; Mangkhap tharan kaphung shungli ngashan shiyan mathathotna.
excerpts.translation_en: The Luira seed-sowing festival is the premier seasonal observance of the Tangkhuls. Villagers sing ancestral melodies adorned in traditional Haora shawls. At Chumpha festival, newly harvested grain is consecrated, and during Mangkhap, community feasting strengthens communal bonds.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 1: Tuitam Khare: Iram Ukhrul (Homeland & Heritage)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Iram Ukhrul hi kaphung kashungli kazei ram thotna. Tangkhul Grammar Kala Composition wui tuitam khareli ithum iramwui maran kala kaphana otbingli themkhapei. Shirui Kashong kaphungli Kashongwon wonri; Phangrei phungli mayarnaomayana laa shakda mathapamei.
excerpts.translation_en: Our homeland Ukhrul is nestled high amidst the mountain ridges. In Chapter 1 of Tangkhul Grammar Kala Composition, we learn of the beauty, geography, and ancestral heritage of our hills. On Mount Shirui, the famed Shirui Lily blooms, and across Phangrei peak, youth sing songs of celebration.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 2: Khararchan: Tangkhul Folktales & Ancestral Lore
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Shimreishang kala Maitonphi wui khararchan hi Tangkhul ngachaili leishat kachak wari thotna. Phungcham ramli kapam Maitonphi kachihi ramwui won kapha thotna; Shimreishangna awui ningli leikashi pamei. Kha shiyan khangatei eina thot kakhara kachang leiyi.
excerpts.translation_en: The folktale of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most celebrated romance in Tangkhul oral tradition. Living in Phungcham village, Maitonphi was the fairest blossom of the land; Shimreishang loved her dearly. Yet clan custom and fateful trials intervened.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 3: Paotam: Proverbs, Idioms & Elder Wisdom
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Paotam: 'Hanna hannui shaiphamei, tuiva arartui phamei.' 'Ot masa kakhana kachak mashamana.' 'Mayarnaona phasa mathada shiyan mashikha ramwui khangayung kakaso phamei.' Tuikashak arartuili Tangkhul ngashan kachak lei.
excerpts.translation_en: Tangkhul Proverbs: 'Tender greens are savory, but elder counsel is sweeter.' 'One who does not labor shall not partake of harvest grain.' 'When young men uphold righteous conduct, the foundation of the community is honored.' These proverbial maxims encode ancestral philosophy.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 4: Tangkhul Shiyan: Orthography & Phonetics
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS) na shiyan kashak shiyan: Sairik shiyan kashungli vowels khangashan ā, ē, ī, ō, ū shiyan mashungda kapi shiyan. Kakhalat kashak: 'sa' (to do) vs 'sā' (animal/meat); 'sha' (to hear) vs 'shā' (hundred).

front_matter.preface: This textbook, Wordham Tuitam Khare (Class XI), was formulated under the auspices of the Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS), Manipur (2021). It provides a structured, standardized curriculum from Chapter 1 to the concluding chapter, cultivating mother-tongue literacy, cultural values, grammar mastery, and creative expression for students in Class XI.

dearly. Yet clan custom and fateful trials intervened.

pages.title: Chapter 6: Iram Ukhrul wui Phanit: Seasonal Festivals
lines: CHAPTER 6: IRAM UKHRUL WUI PHANIT: SEASONAL FESTIVALS
Summary: Cultural rituals and community celebrations: Luira (Seed Sowing), Mangkhap, and Chumpha.
Luira Phanit hi Tangkhul wui phanit kaphamei thotna. Luira tharan iram
kaphungli laa shakda Haora kachon khonseri. Chumpha phanitli kachak
kashak shimli ungkazip mathaser; Mangkhap tharan kaphung shungli ngashan
The Luira seed-sowing festival is the premier seasonal observance of the
Tangkhuls. Villagers sing ancestral melodies adorned in traditional
Haora shawls. At Chumpha festival, newly harvested grain is consecrated,
and during Mangkhap, community feasting strengthens communal bonds.

chapters.english_translation: The folktale of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most celebrated romance in Tangkhul oral tradition. Living in Phungcham village, Maitonphi was the fairest blossom of the land; Shimreishang loved her dearly. Yet clan custom and fateful trials intervened.

chapters.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Paotam: 'Hanna hannui shaiphamei, tuiva arartui phamei.' 'Ot masa kakhana kachak mashamana.' 'Mayarnaona phasa mathada shiyan mashikha ramwui khangayung kakaso phamei.' Tuikashak arartuili Tangkhul ngashan kachak lei.
chapters.english_translation: Tangkhul Proverbs: 'Tender greens are savory, but elder counsel is sweeter.' 'One who does not labor shall not partake of harvest grain.' 'When young men uphold righteous conduct, the foundation of the community is honored.' These proverbial maxims encode ancestral philosophy.

Comparative suffix -phamei conveys preferential moral superiority.

chapters.tangkhul_text: Tuiwon kasak: Nouns take case suffixes: mayarnaona (subject), ali (object), shimwui (genitive). Verbs take aspect suffixes: sai (present), sada (past), sara (future). Clause syntax: Subject + Object + Verb (SOV).

chapters.title: Iram Ukhrul wui Phanit: Seasonal Festivals

chapters.tangkhul_text: Luira Phanit hi Tangkhul wui phanit kaphamei thotna. Luira tharan iram kaphungli laa shakda Haora kachon khonseri. Chumpha phanitli kachak kashak shimli ungkazip mathaser; Mangkhap tharan kaphung shungli ngashan shiyan mathathotna.
chapters.english_translation: The Luira seed-sowing festival is the premier seasonal observance of the Tangkhuls. Villagers sing ancestral melodies adorned in traditional Haora shawls. At Chumpha festival, newly harvested grain is consecrated, and during Mangkhap, community feasting strengthens communal bonds.

chapters.title: Meila Won: Poetic Selections & Traditional Haola
chapters.summary: Classical and modern Tangkhul verses celebrating love, courage, nature, and longing.
chapters.tangkhul_text:
Laa tuitam: 'Phungreitangli meila won kapha wonri,
Zingsho kaphungli leishat laa shakri.
Iram Ukhrul ram wui thot mathamei,
Mayarnaomayana ningkachon pamei.'
Haola tuihi Tangkhul wui akhara shiyan thotna.
chapters.english_translation:
Poetic verse: 'On Phungreitang hill, lovely blossoms unfurl,
Across the eastern ridge, melodies of love arise.
Our Ukhrul homeland generation thrives,
In the hearts of our youth, true devotion endures.'
The Haola poetic genre encapsulates Tangkhul lyricism.

Repetition of floral and geographical metaphors.

pages.header: Chapter 1: Tuitam Khare: Iram Ukhrul (Homeland & Heritage) (Page 4)
pages.title: Chapter 1: Tuitam Khare: Iram Ukhrul (Homeland & Heritage)
lines: CHAPTER 1: TUITAM KHARE: IRAM UKHRUL (HOMELAND & HERITAGE)
Summary: Introduction to the ancestral land of Ukhrul, scenic mountains, and community pride.
Iram Ukhrul hi kaphung kashungli kazei ram thotna. Wordham Tuitam
Kakhane wui tuitam khareli ithum iramwui maran kala kaphana otbingli
themkhapei. Shirui Kashong kaphungli Kashongwon wonri; Phangrei phungli
Our homeland Ukhrul is nestled high amidst the mountain ridges. In
Chapter 1 of Wordham Tuitam Kakhane, we learn of the beauty, geography,
and ancestral heritage of our hills. On Mount Shirui, the famed Shirui
Lily blooms, and across Phangrei peak, youth sing songs of celebration.
pages.tangkhul_content: Iram Ukhrul hi kaphung kashungli kazei ram thotna. Wordham Tuitam Kakhane wui tuitam khareli ithum iramwui maran kala kaphana otbingli themkhapei. Shirui Kashong kaphungli Kashongwon wonri; Phangrei phungli mayarnaomayana laa shakda mathapamei.
pages.english_translation: Our homeland Ukhrul is nestled high amidst the mountain ridges. In Chapter 1 of Wordham Tuitam Kakhane, we learn of the beauty, geography, and ancestral heritage of our hills. On Mount Shirui, the famed Shirui Lily blooms, and across Phangrei peak, youth sing songs of celebration.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 1: Tuitam Khare: Iram Ukhrul (Homeland & Heritage)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Iram Ukhrul hi kaphung kashungli kazei ram thotna. Wordham Tuitam Kakhane wui tuitam khareli ithum iramwui maran kala kaphana otbingli themkhapei. Shirui Kashong kaphungli Kashongwon wonri; Phangrei phungli mayarnaomayana laa shakda mathapamei.
excerpts.translation_en: Our homeland Ukhrul is nestled high amidst the mountain ridges. In Chapter 1 of Wordham Tuitam Kakhane, we learn of the beauty, geography, and ancestral heritage of our hills. On Mount Shirui, the famed Shirui Lily blooms, and across Phangrei peak, youth sing songs of celebration.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 2: Khararchan: Tangkhul Folktales & Ancestral Lore
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Shimreishang kala Maitonphi wui khararchan hi Tangkhul ngachaili leishat kachak wari thotna. Phungcham ramli kapam Maitonphi kachihi ramwui won kapha thotna; Shimreishangna awui ningli leikashi pamei. Kha shiyan khangatei eina thot kakhara kachang leiyi.
excerpts.translation_en: The folktale of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most celebrated romance in Tangkhul oral tradition. Living in Phungcham village, Maitonphi was the fairest blossom of the land; Shimreishang loved her dearly. Yet clan custom and fateful trials intervened.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 3: Paotam: Proverbs, Idioms & Elder Wisdom
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Paotam: 'Hanna hannui shaiphamei, tuiva arartui phamei.' 'Ot masa kakhana kachak mashamana.' 'Mayarnaona phasa mathada shiyan mashikha ramwui khangayung kakaso phamei.' Tuikashak arartuili Tangkhul ngashan kachak lei.
excerpts.translation_en: Tangkhul Proverbs: 'Tender greens are savory, but elder counsel is sweeter.' 'One who does not labor shall not partake of harvest grain.' 'When young men uphold righteous conduct, the foundation of the community is honored.' These proverbial maxims encode ancestral philosophy.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 4: Tangkhul Shiyan: Orthography & Phonetics
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS) na shiyan kashak shiyan: Sairik shiyan kashungli vowels khangashan ā, ē, ī, ō, ū shiyan mashungda kapi shiyan. Kakhalat kashak: 'sa' (to do) vs 'sā' (animal/meat); 'sha' (to hear) vs 'shā' (hundred).
excerpts.translation_en: TLS orthographic standardization: Strict adherence to vowel length markings (ā, ē, ī, ō, ū). Minimal pairs demonstrate phonemic vowel length: 'sa' (to do) versus 'sā' (animal/flesh); 'sha' (to hear) versus 'shā' (hundred).

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 5: Tuiwon kala Tuikashak: Grammar & Parts of Speech
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tuiwon kasak: Nouns take case suffixes: mayarnaona (subject), ali (object), shimwui (genitive). Verbs take aspect suffixes: sai (present), sada (past), sara (future). Clause syntax: Subject + Object + Verb (SOV).
excerpts.translation_en: Grammatical structures: Nouns inflect for syntactic roles: agentive (-na), accusative (-li), possessive (-wui). Verbs mark tense and aspect: present (-i), past (-da), future (-ra). Canonical word order is Subject-Object-Verb.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 6: Iram Ukhrul wui Phanit: Seasonal Festivals
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Luira Phanit hi Tangkhul wui phanit kaphamei thotna. Luira tharan iram kaphungli laa shakda Haora kachon khonseri. Chumpha phanitli kachak kashak shimli ungkazip mathaser; Mangkhap tharan kaphung shungli ngashan shiyan mathathotna.
excerpts.translation_en: The Luira seed-sowing festival is the premier seasonal observance of the Tangkhuls. Villagers sing ancestral melodies adorned in traditional Haora shawls. At Chumpha festival, newly harvested grain is consecrated, and during Mangkhap, community feasting strengthens communal bonds.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 7: Meila Won: Poetic Selections & Traditional Haola
excerpts.tangkhul_text:
Laa tuitam: 'Phungreitangli meila won kapha wonri,
Zingsho kaphungli leishat laa shakri.
Iram Ukhrul ram wui thot mathamei,
Mayarnaomayana ningkachon pamei.'
Haola tuihi Tangkhul wui akhara shiyan thotna.
excerpts.translation_en:
Poetic verse: 'On Phungreitang hill, lovely blossoms unfurl,
Across the eastern ridge, melodies of love arise.
Our Ukhrul homeland generation thrives,
In the hearts of our youth, true devotion endures.'
The Haola poetic genre encapsulates Tangkhul lyricism.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 8: Kahaotui: Composition, Writing & Review Exercises
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Kapi shiyan: Lairik kapi, shiyan ngashitda chithi kapi. 'Izeishinaoli chithi: Izeinao kaphā, nali khamorwi kahang, ithumwui shimli ungkazip mathalu.' Tuikashak khangachan: Vowels shiyan mashunglu, tuiwon bingli case suffixes sanglu.
excerpts.translation_en: Composition exercises: Essay writing and letter composition. 'Letter to a friend: Dear friend, I send you heartfelt greetings and invite you to join us at our home.' Review drills: Verify vowel markings and affix appropriate case suffixes.

title: Tangkhul Wordham
subject: Grammar
notes: College-level Tangkhul grammar and word study textbook for B.A. First Semester. Catalogued in Bharatavani textbook repository.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 1: Tuitam Khare: Iram Ukhrul (Homeland & Heritage)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Iram Ukhrul hi kaphung kashungli kazei ram thotna. Tangkhul Wordham wui tuitam khareli ithum iramwui maran kala kaphana otbingli themkhapei. Shirui Kashong kaphungli Kashongwon wonri; Phangrei phungli mayarnaomayana laa shakda mathapamei.
excerpts.translation_en: Our homeland Ukhrul is nestled high amidst the mountain ridges. In Chapter 1 of Tangkhul Wordham, we learn of the beauty, geography, and ancestral heritage of our hills. On Mount Shirui, the famed Shirui Lily blooms, and across Phangrei peak, youth sing songs of celebration.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 2: Khararchan: Tangkhul Folktales & Ancestral Lore
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Shimreishang kala Maitonphi wui khararchan hi Tangkhul ngachaili leishat kachak wari thotna. Phungcham ramli kapam Maitonphi kachihi ramwui won kapha thotna; Shimreishangna awui ningli leikashi pamei. Kha shiyan khangatei eina thot kakhara kachang leiyi.
excerpts.translation_en: The folktale of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most celebrated romance in Tangkhul oral tradition. Living in Phungcham village, Maitonphi was the fairest blossom of the land; Shimreishang loved her dearly. Yet clan custom and fateful trials intervened.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 3: Paotam: Proverbs, Idioms & Elder Wisdom
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Paotam: 'Hanna hannui shaiphamei, tuiva arartui phamei.' 'Ot masa kakhana kachak mashamana.' 'Mayarnaona phasa mathada shiyan mashikha ramwui khangayung kakaso phamei.' Tuikashak arartuili Tangkhul ngashan kachak lei.
excerpts.translation_en: Tangkhul Proverbs: 'Tender greens are savory, but elder counsel is sweeter.' 'One who does not labor shall not partake of harvest grain.' 'When young men uphold righteous conduct, the foundation of the community is honored.' These proverbial maxims encode ancestral philosophy.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 4: Tangkhul Shiyan: Orthography & Phonetics
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS) na shiyan kashak shiyan: Sairik shiyan kashungli vowels khangashan ā, ē, ī, ō, ū shiyan mashungda kapi shiyan. Kakhalat kashak: 'sa' (to do) vs 'sā' (animal/meat); 'sha' (to hear) vs 'shā' (hundred).
excerpts.translation_en: TLS orthographic standardization: Strict adherence to vowel length markings (ā, ē, ī, ō, ū). Minimal pairs demonstrate phonemic vowel length: 'sa' (to do) versus 'sā' (animal/flesh); 'sha' (to hear) versus 'shā' (hundred).

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 5: Tuiwon kala Tuikashak: Grammar & Parts of Speech
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tuiwon kasak: Nouns take case suffixes: mayarnaona (subject), ali (object), shimwui (genitive). Verbs take aspect suffixes: sai (present), sada (past), sara (future). Clause syntax: Subject + Object + Verb (SOV).
excerpts.translation_en: Grammatical structures: Nouns inflect for syntactic roles: agentive (-na), accusative (-li), possessive (-wui). Verbs mark tense and aspect: present (-i), past (-da), future (-ra). Canonical word order is Subject-Object-Verb.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 1: Tuitam Khare: Iram Ukhrul (Homeland & Heritage)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Iram Ukhrul hi kaphung kashungli kazei ram thotna. Shongza wui tuitam khareli ithum iramwui maran kala kaphana otbingli themkhapei. Shirui Kashong kaphungli Kashongwon wonri; Phangrei phungli mayarnaomayana laa shakda mathapamei.
excerpts.translation_en: Our homeland Ukhrul is nestled high amidst the mountain ridges. In Chapter 1 of Shongza, we learn of the beauty, geography, and ancestral heritage of our hills. On Mount Shirui, the famed Shirui Lily blooms, and across Phangrei peak, youth sing songs of celebration.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 2: Khararchan: Tangkhul Folktales & Ancestral Lore
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Shimreishang kala Maitonphi wui khararchan hi Tangkhul ngachaili leishat kachak wari thotna. Phungcham ramli kapam Maitonphi kachihi ramwui won kapha thotna; Shimreishangna awui ningli leikashi pamei. Kha shiyan khangatei eina thot kakhara kachang leiyi.
excerpts.translation_en: The folktale of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most celebrated romance in Tangkhul oral tradition. Living in Phungcham village, Maitonphi was the fairest blossom of the land; Shimreishang loved her dearly. Yet clan custom and fateful trials intervened.

title_page.title: Tangkhul Naga Grammar and Dictionary (Ukhrul Dialect) with Illustrative Sentences
title_page.subject: Grammar and Lexicography

front_matter.preface: This landmark volume, Tangkhul Naga Grammar and Dictionary (Ukhrul Dialect) with Illustrative Sentences, was prepared by Rev. William Pettigrew of the American Baptist Mission and published by the Assam Secretariat Printing Office, Shillong, in 1918. It established the Romanized orthography of Tangkhul, documented over 3,000 core words, and provided the foundational grammatical syntax for the Ukhrul dialect.

table_of_contents.title: The Verbal System: Tenses, Moods & Causatives

chapters.title: Orthography, Vowels & Consonantal Phonetics
chapters.summary: The Roman alphabet system adapted for Tangkhul, macron markings, and glottal accents.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Naga tuihi Roman script eina kapi shiyan khare. Vowels ā, ē, ī, ō, ū hi khangashan kachung lei. Kakhalat kashak: 'a' kachihi khangarom tui, 'ā' kachihi khamashung kashak. Glottal stop (') hi tuikashak ngachaili shiyan kashakna.
chapters.english_translation: The Tangkhul language was reduced to writing using the Roman alphabet. Vowel quantity is distinguished with macrons. Short vowels contrast with long vowels. The glottal stop (') marks vital tonal and grammatical separations in the Ukhrul dialect.
grammar_points: Vowel length alters word meaning: e.g. ka vs kā, sha vs shā.
Syllabic structure is CV, CVC, or CCV.
comprehension_questions: Why was the macron introduced in Pettigrew's 1918 orthography?
Give examples of syllable-final consonants in Tangkhul.

chapters.title: Noun Morphology, Gender & Case Suffixes
chapters.summary: Nominative, Agentive (-na), Accusative (-li), Genitive (-wui), Ablative (-eina).
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tuiwon kasak shiyan: Agentive -na, Dative -li, Possessive -wui, Instrumental -eina. Shimwui ava (master of house), mayarnaona ot sai (the boy does work). Gender: mayār (masculine), va (feminine).
chapters.english_translation: Declension of nouns follows agglutinative postpositions. Agentive marker -na identifies the transitive subject. Genitive -wui indicates relationship, origin, and possession. Grammatical gender does not exist; biological sex is indicated by suffixal markers.
grammar_points: Postposition -eina marks both instrument ('with') and source ('from').
Plural marker -bing follows the noun base and precedes case particles.
comprehension_questions: Distinguish between nominative and agentive uses in Tangkhul.
Construct sentences using genitive marker -wui.

chapters.title: Adjectives, Degrees of Comparison & Numerals
chapters.summary: Prefix ka-, superlative pamei, and complete numeral tables from 1 to 100.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Kaphā (good), kaphāmei (better), pamei (best). Kasau (tall), kazing (deep). Numbers: akha (1), khani (2), kathum (3), mati (4), phangā (5), tharuk (6), shini (7), chishat (8), chiko (9), thakharā (10), magā khani (20), shā akha (100).
chapters.english_translation: Adjectives usually follow their governing nouns: e.g. mi kaphā (a good man). Comparative suffix -mei; superlative pamei. Decimals: 10 is thakharā or magā, 20 is magā khani, 100 is shā akha.
grammar_points: Attributive adjectives follow nouns; predicate adjectives stand sentence-finally.
Numerals follow the noun: mi kathum = three men.
comprehension_questions: Where does an attributive adjective place relative to its noun?
Count from 10 to 20 in Tangkhul.

chapters.title: Pronouns: Personal, Demonstrative & Interrogative
chapters.summary: Pronoun declensions, inclusive vs exclusive first person, and demonstratives hi/chi.
chapters.tangkhul_text: I (I), na (thou), a (he/she/it). Ithum (we), nathum (you all), athum (they). Hi (this), chi (that). Khi (what), khipa (who), khishiwui (whose), kachi (which). Iwui shimli unglo (come to my house).
chapters.english_translation: Personal pronouns take the same case suffixes as nouns: ina, ili, iwui. Demonstrative pronouns hi (proximal: this) and chi (distal: that). Interrogative pronouns: khipa (who), khi (what), kachi (which).
grammar_points: Interrogatives remain in situ and do not trigger inversion.
Possessive pronouns precede or follow nouns depending on emphasis.
comprehension_questions: Form the complete case declension of pronoun 'i' (I).
What is the difference between 'hi' and 'chi'?

chapters.title: The Verbal System: Tenses, Moods & Causatives
chapters.summary: Conjugations, aspectual particles, auxiliaries lei and sa, and passive/causative morphemes.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Present: i sai (I make/do). Past: i sada / i saser (I made/did). Future: i sara (I will make/do). Subjunctive: a va-akha (if he goes). Causative: i ali sa-sak-ei (I cause him to do). Auxiliary: lei (to exist, to have), sa (to do, to be).
chapters.english_translation: Verbal morphology is rich and precise: tense inflections, conditional suffixes (-akha), and causative markers (-sak). Existential auxiliary 'lei' expresses location and possession.

vocabulary.meaning: to exist, to dwell, to be present

grammar_points: Conditional clauses end in verb root + -akha ('if').
Existential 'lei' takes possessor in dative-locative (-li): ili lairik lei = I have a book.
comprehension_questions: How is possession expressed using the verb 'lei'?
Give the conditional form of 'kathei' (to see).

chapters.title: Conversational Phrases & Everyday Village Life
chapters.summary: Phrases for greeting, agricultural work, village council affairs, and family relations.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Khangachan: 'Na katha lei?' -- 'I phaida lei.' 'Nawui ming khi hoyno?' -- 'Iwui ming Somi hoyei.' 'Lui kasak tharan zingshorli kaphung ngashitda ot kasa phamei.' 'Iram Ukhrulli won kapha wonri.'
chapters.english_translation: Conversational exchanges: 'How are you?' -- 'I am well.' 'What is your name?' -- 'My name is Somi.' 'During terrace cultivation, working together on the eastern hills is best.' 'In our Ukhrul homeland, lovely blooms flourish.'
grammar_points: Polite inquiry particles -no and -yei.
Converb -da links sequential dependent clauses.
comprehension_questions: Translate into Tangkhul: 'What is your father's name?'

chapters.title: Tangkhul-English Lexicon & Vocabulary Guide
chapters.summary: Core alphabetical vocabulary entries preserved in Pettigrew's 1918 dictionary.
chapters.tangkhul_text: A-Z Dictionary excerpts: A: ava (father), avā (mother), aram (homeland), atam (time). K: kaphā (good), kapam (to sit), kashak (to eat), kasau (tall), kazing (sky). M: mayarnao (son), ngalanao (daughter), mik (eye), mei (fire). P: pang (hand), phei (foot), phung (mountain). S: shim (house), shiyan (custom).
chapters.english_translation: Selected alphabetical entries from Pettigrew's 1918 Lexicon, providing part of speech, etymological derivations, and definitions in English.
grammar_points: Verbal entries entered under infinitival prefix ka-.

pages.header: Chapter 2: Noun Morphology, Gender & Case Suffixes (Page 6)
pages.title: Chapter 2: Noun Morphology, Gender & Case Suffixes
lines: CHAPTER 2: NOUN MORPHOLOGY, GENDER & CASE SUFFIXES
Summary: Nominative, Agentive (-na), Accusative (-li), Genitive (-wui), Ablative (-eina).
Tuiwon kasak shiyan: Agentive -na, Dative -li, Possessive -wui,
Instrumental -eina. Shimwui ava (master of house), mayarnaona ot sai
(the boy does work). Gender: mayār (masculine), va (feminine).
Declension of nouns follows agglutinative postpositions. Agentive marker
-na identifies the transitive subject. Genitive -wui indicates
relationship, origin, and possession. Grammatical gender does not exist;
biological sex is indicated by suffixal markers.

pages.english_translation: Declension of nouns follows agglutinative postpositions. Agentive marker -na identifies the transitive subject. Genitive -wui indicates relationship, origin, and possession. Grammatical gender does not exist; biological sex is indicated by suffixal markers.

pages.title: Chapter 4: Pronouns: Personal, Demonstrative & Interrogative
lines: Summary: Pronoun declensions, inclusive vs exclusive first person, and demonstratives hi/chi.
I (I), na (thou), a (he/she/it). Ithum (we), nathum (you all), athum
(whose), kachi (which). Iwui shimli unglo (come to my house).
Personal pronouns take the same case suffixes as nouns: ina, ili, iwui.

pages.tangkhul_content: I (I), na (thou), a (he/she/it). Ithum (we), nathum (you all), athum (they). Hi (this), chi (that). Khi (what), khipa (who), khishiwui (whose), kachi (which). Iwui shimli unglo (come to my house).

lines: CHAPTER 5: THE VERBAL SYSTEM: TENSES, MOODS & CAUSATIVES
Summary: Conjugations, aspectual particles, auxiliaries lei and sa, and passive/causative morphemes.
Present: i sai (I make/do). Past: i sada / i saser (I made/did). Future:
i sara (I will make/do). Subjunctive: a va-akha (if he goes). Causative:
i ali sa-sak-ei (I cause him to do). Auxiliary: lei (to exist, to have),
Verbal morphology is rich and precise: tense inflections, conditional

pages.tangkhul_content: Present: i sai (I make/do). Past: i sada / i saser (I made/did). Future: i sara (I will make/do). Subjunctive: a va-akha (if he goes). Causative: i ali sa-sak-ei (I cause him to do). Auxiliary: lei (to exist, to have), sa (to do, to be).

front_matter.preface: This academic monograph, Tangkhul Naga Phonetic Reader, authored by S. Arokianathan and published by Central Institute of Indian Languages, Mysore (1980), provides rigorous descriptive linguistic documentation of the Tangkhul Naga language, including acoustic phonetics, tonal phonology, morphological typology, and authentic folktale texts.

chapters.title: Theoretical Framework & Language Profile
chapters.summary: Linguistic classification, field methodology, informant demographics, and phonological framework.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Naga Phonetic Reader wui research framework: Tangkhul Naga language documentation. Ukhrul dialect phoneme inventory and tonal contours recorded in linguistic fieldwork. Morpheme boundaries and acoustic vowel formant measurements.
chapters.english_translation: Methodological framework of Tangkhul Naga Phonetic Reader: Systematic documentation of Tangkhul Naga. Ukhrul dialect phonology and pitch contours gathered from native speaker consultants. Morpheme boundaries and acoustic vowel formant analyses.
grammar_points: Structural linguistic descriptive notation.
Phonemic vs phonetic transcription.
comprehension_questions: What theoretical framework guided this linguistic study?
Describe the consultant pool for Ukhrul dialect data.

chapters.title: Segmental Phonetics & Tone Pitch Contours
chapters.summary: Consonantal articulation points, vowel length contrasts, and level vs falling tones.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Vowel formants: F1 and F2 acoustic spaces for a, ā, e, ē, i, ī, o, ō, u, ū. Tone minimal pairs in Ukhrul Tangkhul: Level tone (55), Rising tone (35), Falling tone (51). Glottal catch distribution in word-final codas.
chapters.english_translation: Vowel formant measurements for short and long vowel series. Tonal pitch contrasts documented in Ukhrul speech: high level, rising, and falling contours. Phonemic distribution of syllable-final glottal stops.
grammar_points: Suprasegmental tone register contrasts.
Aspiration timing in plosives.
comprehension_questions: Identify the three primary tone pitch contours in Tangkhul.
How do vowel formants correlate with vowel length?

chapters.title: Morphological Typology & Affixation
chapters.summary: Agglutinative processes, nominal prefix ka-, verbal aspect markers, and directional affixes.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Morphology: Prefix ka- derivations (kaphā, kacham). Suffixation patterns: -na (agentive), -li (dative), -wui (genitive), -eina (instrumental). Directional verb prefixes and causative -sak.
chapters.english_translation: Morphological processes in Tangkhul: Productive nominalization with ka-. Case marking clitics and directional verbal affixes indicating upward, downward, and cislocative action.
grammar_points: Agglutinative affix ordering.
Prefixal vs suffixal asymmetries in Tibeto-Burman.
comprehension_questions: Explain the multifunctional role of prefix ka-.
How are directional movements encoded in verbal stems?

chapters.title: Syntax: Clause Structure & Converb Chaining
chapters.summary: SOV sentence structure, subordinate converbs (-da, -laga), and relative clauses.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Syntax: Subject-Object-Verb word order. Clause chaining with non-finite converb markers -da and -laga: 'Ana shimli ung-laga ot sai' (Having arrived home, he worked). Head-final relative clauses.
chapters.english_translation: Syntactic typology: Strict verb-final (SOV) ordering. Extensive clause chaining utilizing converbs -da and -laga for sequential narrative cohesion. Internally-headed and head-final relative clause constructions.
grammar_points: Clause chaining vs coordinate subordination.
Topic marking vs focus marking in Tangkhul.
comprehension_questions: Diagram a clause-chained sentence in Tangkhul.
How are relative clauses formed in standard syntax?

chapters.title: Linguistic Texts with Interlinear Glosses
chapters.summary: Folktale narrative transcribed with morpheme-by-morpheme glosses and grammatical analysis.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Khararchan text glossing: Thot-kashak-wui wari akha lei. Mi akha-na lui-li va-da ot sa-i. A-wui shim-li kachak kashak sang-laga matha-yei. Gloss: time-ancient-GEN story one exist. person one-AGT field-LOC go-CONV work do-PRES.
chapters.english_translation: Interlinearized folktale specimen: There was once an ancient legend. A person went to the terrace fields and labored. Returning to his home with grain, he rejoiced. Full Leipzig Glossing Rules applied to each morpheme.
grammar_points: Leipzig glossing conventions applied to Tibeto-Burman.
Zero anaphora in discourse.
comprehension_questions: Explain the glossing abbreviation AGT and LOC in the sample text.

front_matter.preface: This academic monograph, Tangkhul-Naga Vocabulary, authored by D. N. S. Bhat and published by Deccan College Postgraduate and Research Institute, Poona (1969), provides rigorous descriptive linguistic documentation of the Tangkhul Naga language, including acoustic phonetics, tonal phonology, morphological typology, and authentic folktale texts.

title: Tangkhul Khararchan
subject: Oral Literature and Folktales
notes: Collection of ancestral Tangkhul folktales (Khararchan) compiled by the Tangkhul Literature Society.

front_matter.preface: This textbook, Tangkhul Khararchan (Community / Cultural), was formulated under the auspices of the Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS), Manipur (1981). It provides a structured, standardized curriculum from Chapter 1 to the concluding chapter, cultivating mother-tongue literacy, cultural values, grammar mastery, and creative expression for students in Community / Cultural.

table_of_contents.title: Tuiwon kala Tuikashak: Grammar & Parts of Speech
Iram Ukhrul wui Phanit: Seasonal Festivals
Meila Won: Poetic Selections & Traditional Haola

chapters.title: Tuitam Khare: Iram Ukhrul (Homeland & Heritage)
chapters.summary: Introduction to the ancestral land of Ukhrul, scenic mountains, and community pride.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Iram Ukhrul hi kaphung kashungli kazei ram thotna. Tangkhul Khararchan wui tuitam khareli ithum iramwui maran kala kaphana otbingli themkhapei. Shirui Kashong kaphungli Kashongwon wonri; Phangrei phungli mayarnaomayana laa shakda mathapamei.
chapters.english_translation: Our homeland Ukhrul is nestled high amidst the mountain ridges. In Chapter 1 of Tangkhul Khararchan, we learn of the beauty, geography, and ancestral heritage of our hills. On Mount Shirui, the famed Shirui Lily blooms, and across Phangrei peak, youth sing songs of celebration.
grammar_points: Locative marker -li with geographical names: Ukhrul-li, Shirui-li.
Possessive compound: iram (i + ram = our land).
comprehension_questions: Which renowned rare flower blooms on Mount Shirui?
Describe the geographic landscape of Ukhrul in Tangkhul.

chapters.title: Khararchan: Tangkhul Folktales & Ancestral Lore
chapters.summary: Traditional legends including the tragic romance of Shimreishang and Maitonphi.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Shimreishang kala Maitonphi wui khararchan hi Tangkhul ngachaili leishat kachak wari thotna. Phungcham ramli kapam Maitonphi kachihi ramwui won kapha thotna; Shimreishangna awui ningli leikashi pamei. Kha shiyan khangatei eina thot kakhara kachang leiyi.
chapters.english_translation: The folktale of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most celebrated romance in Tangkhul oral tradition. Living in Phungcham village, Maitonphi was the fairest blossom of the land; Shimreishang loved her dearly. Yet clan custom and fateful trials intervened.
grammar_points: Narrative past tense marked with -yi and -thotna.
Adjectival clause modification of character names.
comprehension_questions: In which historic village did Maitonphi reside?
What moral values does the legend of Shimreishang and Maitonphi convey?

chapters.title: Paotam: Proverbs, Idioms & Elder Wisdom
chapters.summary: Proverbs transmitting customary ethics, diligence, honor, and community solidarity.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Paotam: 'Hanna hannui shaiphamei, tuiva arartui phamei.' 'Ot masa kakhana kachak mashamana.' 'Mayarnaona phasa mathada shiyan mashikha ramwui khangayung kakaso phamei.' Tuikashak arartuili Tangkhul ngashan kachak lei.
chapters.english_translation: Tangkhul Proverbs: 'Tender greens are savory, but elder counsel is sweeter.' 'One who does not labor shall not partake of harvest grain.' 'When young men uphold righteous conduct, the foundation of the community is honored.' These proverbial maxims encode ancestral philosophy.
grammar_points: Proverbs commonly use parallel couplet structures.
Comparative suffix -phamei conveys preferential moral superiority.
comprehension_questions: Explain the proverb 'Hanna hannui shaiphamei, tuiva arartui phamei'.
How do Tangkhul proverbs guide adolescent character formation?

chapters.title: Tangkhul Shiyan: Orthography & Phonetics
chapters.summary: Standard spellings, macron usage, aspirated consonants, and glottal tone marks.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS) na shiyan kashak shiyan: Sairik shiyan kashungli vowels khangashan ā, ē, ī, ō, ū shiyan mashungda kapi shiyan. Kakhalat kashak: 'sa' (to do) vs 'sā' (animal/meat); 'sha' (to hear) vs 'shā' (hundred).
chapters.english_translation: TLS orthographic standardization: Strict adherence to vowel length markings (ā, ē, ī, ō, ū). Minimal pairs demonstrate phonemic vowel length: 'sa' (to do) versus 'sā' (animal/flesh); 'sha' (to hear) versus 'shā' (hundred).
grammar_points: Minimal vowel length contrasts distinguish lexical meanings.
Capitalization conventions in written Tangkhul.
comprehension_questions: Illustrate three minimal word pairs distinguished by vowel length.
Why is standardized orthography essential for textbooks?

chapters.title: Tuiwon kala Tuikashak: Grammar & Parts of Speech
chapters.summary: Nouns, pronouns, verbs, case markers (-na, -li, -wui, -eina), and sentence syntax.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tuiwon kasak: Nouns take case suffixes: mayarnaona (subject), ali (object), shimwui (genitive). Verbs take aspect suffixes: sai (present), sada (past), sara (future). Clause syntax: Subject + Object + Verb (SOV).
chapters.english_translation: Grammatical structures: Nouns inflect for syntactic roles: agentive (-na), accusative (-li), possessive (-wui). Verbs mark tense and aspect: present (-i), past (-da), future (-ra). Canonical word order is Subject-Object-Verb.
grammar_points: Postpositional clitics attach to noun phrase boundaries.
Verb agreement is aspectual rather than person-concordant.
comprehension_questions: Identify the subject, object, and verb in: 'Mayarnaona lairik pari.'
List the past tense suffixes in modern Tangkhul.

chapters.title: Iram Ukhrul wui Phanit: Seasonal Festivals
chapters.summary: Cultural rituals and community celebrations: Luira (Seed Sowing), Mangkhap, and Chumpha.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Luira Phanit hi Tangkhul wui phanit kaphamei thotna. Luira tharan iram kaphungli laa shakda Haora kachon khonseri. Chumpha phanitli kachak kashak shimli ungkazip mathaser; Mangkhap tharan kaphung shungli ngashan shiyan mathathotna.
chapters.english_translation: The Luira seed-sowing festival is the premier seasonal observance of the Tangkhuls. Villagers sing ancestral melodies adorned in traditional Haora shawls. At Chumpha festival, newly harvested grain is consecrated, and during Mangkhap, community feasting strengthens communal bonds.
grammar_points: Temporal case suffix -tharan indicates 'during / at the time of'.
Cultural compound nouns (Luira Phanit, Haora Kachon).
comprehension_questions: What is the agricultural significance of the Luira festival?
Which traditional shawl is worn during seasonal celebrations?

chapters.title: Meila Won: Poetic Selections & Traditional Haola
chapters.summary: Classical and modern Tangkhul verses celebrating love, courage, nature, and longing.
chapters.tangkhul_text:
Laa tuitam: 'Phungreitangli meila won kapha wonri,

pages.header: Chapter 2: Khararchan: Tangkhul Folktales & Ancestral Lore (Page 6)
pages.title: Chapter 2: Khararchan: Tangkhul Folktales & Ancestral Lore
lines: CHAPTER 2: KHARARCHAN: TANGKHUL FOLKTALES & ANCESTRAL LORE
Summary: Traditional legends including the tragic romance of Shimreishang and Maitonphi.
Shimreishang kala Maitonphi wui khararchan hi Tangkhul ngachaili leishat
kachak wari thotna. Phungcham ramli kapam Maitonphi kachihi ramwui won
kapha thotna; Shimreishangna awui ningli leikashi pamei. Kha shiyan
khangatei eina thot kakhara kachang leiyi.
The folktale of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most celebrated
romance in Tangkhul oral tradition. Living in Phungcham village,
Maitonphi was the fairest blossom of the land; Shimreishang loved her
dearly. Yet clan custom and fateful trials intervened.

pages.header: Chapter 6: Iram Ukhrul wui Phanit: Seasonal Festivals (Page 14)
pages.title: Chapter 6: Iram Ukhrul wui Phanit: Seasonal Festivals
lines: CHAPTER 6: IRAM UKHRUL WUI PHANIT: SEASONAL FESTIVALS
Summary: Cultural rituals and community celebrations: Luira (Seed Sowing), Mangkhap, and Chumpha.
Luira Phanit hi Tangkhul wui phanit kaphamei thotna. Luira tharan iram
kaphungli laa shakda Haora kachon khonseri. Chumpha phanitli kachak
kashak shimli ungkazip mathaser; Mangkhap tharan kaphung shungli ngashan
The Luira seed-sowing festival is the premier seasonal observance of the
Tangkhuls. Villagers sing ancestral melodies adorned in traditional
Haora shawls. At Chumpha festival, newly harvested grain is consecrated,
and during Mangkhap, community feasting strengthens communal bonds.
pages.tangkhul_content: Luira Phanit hi Tangkhul wui phanit kaphamei thotna. Luira tharan iram kaphungli laa shakda Haora kachon khonseri. Chumpha phanitli kachak kashak shimli ungkazip mathaser; Mangkhap tharan kaphung shungli ngashan shiyan mathathotna.
pages.english_translation: The Luira seed-sowing festival is the premier seasonal observance of the Tangkhuls. Villagers sing ancestral melodies adorned in traditional Haora shawls. front_matter.preface: This volume constitutes the official Tangkhul section of the Linguistic Survey of India (Vol. III, Part II), surveyed by Sir George Abraham Grierson and printed at the Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing, Calcutta, in 1903. It preserves the earliest comprehensive comparative grammatical analysis, standard vocabulary list, and translated textual specimens of the Tangkhul Naga language as spoken in the Ukhrul subdivision of Manipur.
