chapters.title: Introduction & Dialectal Classification
chapters.summary: Geographical distribution, tribal divisions, and linguistic position in the Tibeto-Burman family.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Naga hi Manipur ramwui kaphung zanshorli kapam tui thotna. Ukhrul kaphung hi Tangkhul tuiwui phungreitang thada shiyan kashakna. Tui hi Tibeto-Burman wui Naga-Kuki tui ngachaili shangserna.
chapters.english_translation: The Tangkhul Nagas inhabit the eastern hill tracts of Manipur State. The village of Ukhrul serves as the central cultural and linguistic standard. The language belongs to the Naga-Bodo / Tibeto-Burman linguistic stock.
grammar_points: Tangkhul exhibits SOV (Subject - Object - Verb) word order.
Agglutinative prefixation (ka-) and suffixation dominate inflection.
comprehension_questions: Where is the dialectal center of the Tangkhul language located?
What major language family does Tangkhul belong to?

chapters.title: Phonology and the Roman Alphabet
chapters.summary: Vowels, consonants, diphthongs, and glottal tone stops introduced by W. Pettigrew.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Vowels: a, ā, e, ē, i, ī, o, ō, u, ū. Consonants: k, kh, ng, ch, chh, j, t, th, n, p, ph, m, y, r, l, w, s, sh, h. Kakhalat kashak shiyan eina tui khangatei kachung lei.
chapters.english_translation: Vowel inventory with phonemic length distinctions: short and long vowels. Consonantal series with aspirated stops (kh, th, ph, chh). Syllable-final consonants and tonal inflections alter word significations.
grammar_points: Macron diacritic marks long vowel quantity (ā, ē, ī, ō, ū).
Aspiration contrasts phonemically in initial plosives: k vs kh, t vs th, p vs ph.
comprehension_questions: Name the five vowel pairs with length distinctions in Tangkhul.
How are aspirated consonants represented in the Roman orthography?

chapters.title: The Noun System & Case Inflections
chapters.summary: Natural gender indicators, plural formations, and postpositional case endings.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tuiwon bing: mayarnaona (nominative), mayarnaoli (accusative/dative), mayarnaowui (genitive), mayarnaoeina (instrumental/ablative). Chitharan shiyan kakhane: si (dog), siva (bitch), simayār (male dog).
chapters.english_translation: Case suffixes attached to nominal stems: -na (nominative/agentive), -li (dative/objective), -wui (genitive/possessive), -eina (instrumental/ablative). Gender markers: -va (female) and -mayār (male).
grammar_points: Agentive suffix -na is obligatory for subjects of transitive verbs.
Plurality is formed by adding -bing or -binda to nominal bases.
comprehension_questions: Identify the four primary case suffixes in Tangkhul nominal syntax.
How is natural gender differentiated in animal nouns?

chapters.title: Adjectives, Numerals & Pronouns
chapters.summary: Adjectival prefix ka-, degrees of comparison, cardinal numerals, and pronoun paradigms.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Kaphā (good), kakhui (bitter), kacham (poor). Comparison: kaphāmei (better), pamei (best). Numerals: akha (1), khani (2), kathum (3), mati (4), phangā (5), tharuk (6), shini (7), chishat (8), chiko (9), thakharā / magā (10). Pronouns: i (I), na (thou), a (he/she).
chapters.english_translation: Descriptive adjectives are derived using prefix ka-. Comparison is marked with -mei. Cardinal numerals from 1 to 10. Personal pronouns: 1st person 'i', 2nd person 'na', 3rd person 'a'; plurals: ithum, nathum, athum.
grammar_points: Prefix ka- nominalizes or adjectivizes verbal roots.
Dual and plural pronouns are formed with suffix -thum (ithum = we).
comprehension_questions: List the Tangkhul numerals from one to five.
Explain how personal pronouns form possessives in Tangkhul.

chapters.title: Verb Conjugation, Tenses & Moods
chapters.summary: Verbal roots, tense inflections (-ei, -ser, -ra), imperative (-lu), and negative prefixes.
chapters.tangkhul_text: I sai (I do, present), i sada / i theiser (past), i sara (future). Imperative: salu (do!), theilu (see!). Negative: masa-mana (does not do), mathei-mana (does not see). Causative: -sak (sasaku).
chapters.english_translation: Verbs conjugate through tense suffixes: present -ei/-i, past -ser/-da, future -ra. Imperative forms take suffix -lu. Negation frames the verbal root with prefix ma- and suffix -mana. Causation is expressed with -sak.

vocabulary.meaning: to do, to make, to create

grammar_points: Discontinuous negative morpheme: ma- [root] -mana.
Aspectual suffix -ser indicates completive or collective action.
comprehension_questions: Conjugate the verb root 'sa' in present, past, and future.
How is a negative declarative sentence constructed in Tangkhul?

chapters.title: Specimen I: The Parable of the Prodigal Son (Complete)
chapters.summary: Authentic full-text translation of Luke 15:11-32 in Tangkhul Naga with verse-by-verse gloss.
chapters.tangkhul_text:
11. Mi akhali mayarnaowon khani leiyi.
12. Kakhani chiwui ngachaili kakhanao china aishavaali kahang, 'Ava, ramwui kashikhavai ngashan iwui khavai thali ili milu.' Chiwui vang aishavana aram athum khaniwui ngachaili ngashanserie.
13. Zingkum kachung mathaloikhalang kakhanao china aishapup sanglaga kashak ramli vashitserie, chitharan aphasa kakhano awui vang phasa ngalung khayai eina khamatai thotna.
14. Ana atam sashidaran ram chithuili haora kapha thotna; chitharan a kacham thotna.
15. Chiwui vang a vashitlaga chiwui ramwui mi akhali phungphada leiyi; ana ali awui lili hok kashukhavai ngasikseriya.
16. Chitharan ana hokna shakhavai theichon chieina phasa vashikhavai ningkachon leiyi; chalieikha mi akhana ali mimana.
17. Kha ana awui ning kazil chitharan ana kahang, 'Iva wui ngavaia mi kachungkhana kachak mathaloikhalang thari, kha i hiwui phasa ngalung kazata eina thiyei!'
18. 'I ngakhokda iva wui lili vara, ana ali hangra: Ava, Kazingramli kala na makhaingalina i yor kasa mi thotna.'
19. 'Chiwui vang nawui nao kachi tui shiyan katha mavana; ili nawui ngavaia mi akha gaka thada sanglu.'
20. Chithālaga a ngakhokda aishava wui lili vayi. Kha a kashakli leitharan aishavana ali theilaga kachan pamei, chithālaga ngathimlaga akukli chukda kachamseriya.
21. Nao china ali kahang, 'Ava, Kazingramli kala na makhaingalina i yor kasa mi thotna; nawui nao kachi tui shiyan katha mavana.'
22. Kha aishavana awui ngavaia mi bingli kahang, 'Kaphāmei kachon sanglalu, ali khonlu; kala awui pangyali chap sanglu, awui pheili khokhop sanglu.'
23. 'Kala se phapharo shithalu, ngasotlu; ithum sashilaga mathaseru.'
24. 'Iwui nao hi thida leikha kazing thotna, themda leikha theikhuiraser.' Chitharan athum mathapameiser.
25. Chitharan awui mayarnaowon kakhara a lili leiyi; a ngateilaga shim mathatungda leikhara laa khavai kala ngakhum kaphei khangazip tharan a kashana.
26. Ana ngavaia mi akhali hoklaga, 'Hi khi thotno?' da ngahangyei.
27. Ana ali kahang, 'Nawui nanao vashungser, nawui avana se phapharo shithiser, ana phasa katha theikhuira tharan.'
28. Chiwui vang a kachuk thotna, a shimli ungkhavai ningkachon maleimana; chiwui vang aishava vashitlaga ali kahangyei.
29. Ana ngashitda aishavaali kahang, 'Theilu, kum hiya thada i nali ngavaiyei, nawui tui kachikha mamatai-mana; chithakha iwui azeishinao bingli ngasotda sashikhavai senao akha gaka ili mimana.'
30. 'Kha nawui nao khamatai thotna ngalanao bingli nawui ram shiser china vang se phapharo shithimina!'
31. Ana ali kahang, 'Nao, na i eina kapam thotna, iwui ot phasa shishapup nawuina.'
32. 'Kha mathada ngasotkhavai shiyan phamei; nanao hi thida leikha kazing thotna, themda leikha theikhuiraser.'
chapters.english_translation:
11. A certain man had two sons:
12. And the younger of them said to his father, 'Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me.' And he divided unto them his living.
13. And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living.
14. And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that land; and he began to be in want.
15. And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine.
16. And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him.
17. And when he came to himself, he said, 'How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!'
18. 'I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee,'
19. 'And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.'
20. And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
21. And the son said unto him, 'Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son.'
22. But the father said to his servants, 'Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:'
23. 'And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:'
24. 'For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found.' And they began to be merry.
25. Now his elder son was in the field: and as he came and drew nigh to the house, he heard music and dancing.
26. And he called one of the servants, and asked what these things meant.
27. And he said unto him, 'Thy brother is come; and thy father hath killed the fatted calf, because he hath received him safe and sound.'
28. And he was angry, and would not go in: therefore came his father out, and intreated him.
29. And he answering said to his father, 'Lo, these many years do I serve thee, neither transgressed I at any time thy commandment: and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends:'
30. 'But as soon as this thy son was come, which hath devoured thy living with harlots, thou hast killed for him the fatted calf.'
31. And he said unto him, 'Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine.'
32. 'It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.'
grammar_points: Direct speech framing with quotative postposition 'da'.
Honorific and intimate kinship terms (ava, nanao, azeishinao).
comprehension_questions: What did the younger son ask of his father?
How did the father respond when the younger son returned?

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 1: Introduction & Dialectal Classification
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Naga hi Manipur ramwui kaphung zanshorli kapam tui thotna. Ukhrul kaphung hi Tangkhul tuiwui phungreitang thada shiyan kashakna. Tui hi Tibeto-Burman wui Naga-Kuki tui ngachaili shangserna.
excerpts.translation_en: The Tangkhul Nagas inhabit the eastern hill tracts of Manipur State. The village of Ukhrul serves as the central cultural and linguistic standard. The language belongs to the Naga-Bodo / Tibeto-Burman linguistic stock.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 2: Phonology and the Roman Alphabet
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Vowels: a, ā, e, ē, i, ī, o, ō, u, ū. Consonants: k, kh, ng, ch, chh, j, t, th, n, p, ph, m, y, r, l, w, s, sh, h. Kakhalat kashak shiyan eina tui khangatei kachung lei.
excerpts.translation_en: Vowel inventory with phonemic length distinctions: short and long vowels. Consonantal series with aspirated stops (kh, th, ph, chh). Syllable-final consonants and tonal inflections alter word significations.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 3: The Noun System & Case Inflections
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tuiwon bing: mayarnaona (nominative), mayarnaoli (accusative/dative), mayarnaowui (genitive), mayarnaoeina (instrumental/ablative). Chitharan shiyan kakhane: si (dog), siva (bitch), simayār (male dog).
excerpts.translation_en: Case suffixes attached to nominal stems: -na (nominative/agentive), -li (dative/objective), -wui (genitive/possessive), -eina (instrumental/ablative). Gender markers: -va (female) and -mayār (male).

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 4: Adjectives, Numerals & Pronouns
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Kaphā (good), kakhui (bitter), kacham (poor). Comparison: kaphāmei (better), pamei (best). Numerals: akha (1), khani (2), kathum (3), mati (4), phangā (5), tharuk (6), shini (7), chishat (8), chiko (9), thakharā / magā (10). Pronouns: i (I), na (thou), a (he/she).
excerpts.translation_en: Descriptive adjectives are derived using prefix ka-. Comparison is marked with -mei. Cardinal numerals from 1 to 10. Personal pronouns: 1st person 'i', 2nd person 'na', 3rd person 'a'; plurals: ithum, nathum, athum.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 5: Verb Conjugation, Tenses & Moods
excerpts.tangkhul_text: I sai (I do, present), i sada / i theiser (past), i sara (future). Imperative: salu (do!), theilu (see!). Negative: masa-mana (does not do), mathei-mana (does not see). Causative: -sak (sasaku).
excerpts.translation_en: Verbs conjugate through tense suffixes: present -ei/-i, past -ser/-da, future -ra. Imperative forms take suffix -lu. Negation frames the verbal root with prefix ma- and suffix -mana. Causation is expressed with -sak.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 6: Specimen I: The Parable of the Prodigal Son (Complete)
excerpts.tangkhul_text:
11. Mi akhali mayarnaowon khani leiyi.
12. Kakhani chiwui ngachaili kakhanao china aishavaali kahang, 'Ava, ramwui kashikhavai ngashan iwui khavai thali ili milu.' Chiwui vang aishavana aram athum khaniwui ngachaili ngashanserie.
13. Zingkum kachung mathaloikhalang kakhanao china aishapup sanglaga kashak ramli vashitserie, chitharan aphasa kakhano awui vang phasa ngalung khayai eina khamatai thotna.
14. Ana atam sashidaran ram chithuili haora kapha thotna; chitharan a kacham thotna.
15. Chiwui vang a vashitlaga chiwui ramwui mi akhali phungphada leiyi; ana ali awui lili hok kashukhavai ngasikseriya.
16. Chitharan ana hokna shakhavai theichon chieina phasa vashikhavai ningkachon leiyi; chalieikha mi akhana ali mimana.
17. Kha ana awui ning kazil chitharan ana kahang, 'Iva wui ngavaia mi kachungkhana kachak mathaloikhalang thari, kha i hiwui phasa ngalung kazata eina thiyei!'
18. 'I ngakhokda iva wui lili vara, ana ali hangra: Ava, Kazingramli kala na makhaingalina i yor kasa mi thotna.'
19. 'Chiwui vang nawui nao kachi tui shiyan katha mavana; ili nawui ngavaia mi akha gaka thada sanglu.'
20. Chithālaga a ngakhokda aishava wui lili vayi. Kha a kashakli leitharan aishavana ali theilaga kachan pamei, chithālaga ngathimlaga akukli chukda kachamseriya.
21. Nao china ali kahang, 'Ava, Kazingramli kala na makhaingalina i yor kasa mi thotna; nawui nao kachi tui shiyan katha mavana.'
22. Kha aishavana awui ngavaia mi bingli kahang, 'Kaphāmei kachon sanglalu, ali khonlu; kala awui pangyali chap sanglu, awui pheili khokhop sanglu.'
23. 'Kala se phapharo shithalu, ngasotlu; ithum sashilaga mathaseru.'
24. 'Iwui nao hi thida leikha kazing thotna, themda leikha theikhuiraser.' Chitharan athum mathapameiser.
25. Chitharan awui mayarnaowon kakhara a lili leiyi; a ngateilaga shim mathatungda leikhara laa khavai kala ngakhum kaphei khangazip tharan a kashana.
26. Ana ngavaia mi akhali hoklaga, 'Hi khi thotno?' da ngahangyei.
27. Ana ali kahang, 'Nawui nanao vashungser, nawui avana se phapharo shithiser, ana phasa katha theikhuira tharan.'
28. Chiwui vang a kachuk thotna, a shimli ungkhavai ningkachon maleimana; chiwui vang aishava vashitlaga ali kahangyei.
29. Ana ngashitda aishavaali kahang, 'Theilu, kum hiya thada i nali ngavaiyei, nawui tui kachikha mamatai-mana; chithakha iwui azeishinao bingli ngasotda sashikhavai senao akha gaka ili mimana.'
30. 'Kha nawui nao khamatai thotna ngalanao bingli nawui ram shiser china vang se phapharo shithimina!'
31. Ana ali kahang, 'Nao, na i eina kapam thotna, iwui ot phasa shishapup nawuina.'
32. 'Kha mathada ngasotkhavai shiyan phamei; nanao hi thida leikha kazing thotna, themda leikha theikhuiraser.'
excerpts.translation_en:
11. A certain man had two sons:
12. And the younger of them said to his father, 'Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me.' And he divided unto them his living.
13. And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living.
14. And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that land; and he began to be in want.
15. And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine.
16. And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him.
17. And when he came to himself, he said, 'How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!'
18. 'I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee,'
19. 'And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.'
20. And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
21. And the son said unto him, 'Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son.'
22. But the father said to his servants, 'Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:'
23. 'And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:'
24. 'For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found.' And they began to be merry.
25. Now his elder son was in the field: and as he came and drew nigh to the house, he heard music and dancing.
26. And he called one of the servants, and asked what these things meant.
27. And he said unto him, 'Thy brother is come; and thy father hath killed the fatted calf, because he hath received him safe and sound.'
28. And he was angry, and would not go in: therefore came his father out, and intreated him.
29. And he answering said to his father, 'Lo, these many years do I serve thee, neither transgressed I at any time thy commandment: and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends:'
30. 'But as soon as this thy son was come, which hath devoured thy living with harlots, thou hast killed for him the fatted calf.'
31. And he said unto him, 'Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine.'
32. 'It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.'

front_matter.preface: This textbook, Tangkhul Folk Songs and Cultural Lore (Cultural / Archival), was formulated under the auspices of the Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS), Manipur (2021). It provides a structured, standardized curriculum from Chapter 1 to the concluding chapter, cultivating mother-tongue literacy, cultural values, grammar mastery, and creative expression for students in Cultural / Archival.

chapters.title: Tuitam Khare: Iram Ukhrul (Homeland & Heritage)
chapters.summary: Introduction to the ancestral land of Ukhrul, scenic mountains, and community pride.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Iram Ukhrul hi kaphung kashungli kazei ram thotna. Tangkhul Folk Songs and Cultural Lore wui tuitam khareli ithum iramwui maran kala kaphana otbingli themkhapei. Shirui Kashong kaphungli Kashongwon wonri; Phangrei phungli mayarnaomayana laa shakda mathapamei.
chapters.english_translation: Our homeland Ukhrul is nestled high amidst the mountain ridges. In Chapter 1 of Tangkhul Folk Songs and Cultural Lore, we learn of the beauty, geography, and ancestral heritage of our hills. On Mount Shirui, the famed Shirui Lily blooms, and across Phangrei peak, youth sing songs of celebration.
grammar_points: Locative marker -li with geographical names: Ukhrul-li, Shirui-li.
Possessive compound: iram (i + ram = our land).
comprehension_questions: Which renowned rare flower blooms on Mount Shirui?
Describe the geographic landscape of Ukhrul in Tangkhul.

chapters.title: Khararchan: Tangkhul Folktales & Ancestral Lore
chapters.summary: Traditional legends including the tragic romance of Shimreishang and Maitonphi.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Shimreishang kala Maitonphi wui khararchan hi Tangkhul ngachaili leishat kachak wari thotna. Phungcham ramli kapam Maitonphi kachihi ramwui won kapha thotna; Shimreishangna awui ningli leikashi pamei. Kha shiyan khangatei eina thot kakhara kachang leiyi.
chapters.english_translation: The folktale of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most celebrated romance in Tangkhul oral tradition. Living in Phungcham village, Maitonphi was the fairest blossom of the land; Shimreishang loved her dearly. Yet clan custom and fateful trials intervened.
grammar_points: Narrative past tense marked with -yi and -thotna.
Adjectival clause modification of character names.
comprehension_questions: In which historic village did Maitonphi reside?
What moral values does the legend of Shimreishang and Maitonphi convey?

chapters.title: Paotam: Proverbs, Idioms & Elder Wisdom
chapters.summary: Proverbs transmitting customary ethics, diligence, honor, and community solidarity.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Paotam: 'Hanna hannui shaiphamei, tuiva arartui phamei.' 'Ot masa kakhana kachak mashamana.' 'Mayarnaona phasa mathada shiyan mashikha ramwui khangayung kakaso phamei.' Tuikashak arartuili Tangkhul ngashan kachak lei.
chapters.english_translation: Tangkhul Proverbs: 'Tender greens are savory, but elder counsel is sweeter.' 'One who does not labor shall not partake of harvest grain.' 'When young men uphold righteous conduct, the foundation of the community is honored.' These proverbial maxims encode ancestral philosophy.
grammar_points: Proverbs commonly use parallel couplet structures.
Comparative suffix -phamei conveys preferential moral superiority.
comprehension_questions: Explain the proverb 'Hanna hannui shaiphamei, tuiva arartui phamei'.
How do Tangkhul proverbs guide adolescent character formation?

chapters.title: Tangkhul Shiyan: Orthography & Phonetics
chapters.summary: Standard spellings, macron usage, aspirated consonants, and glottal tone marks.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul Literature Society (TLS) na shiyan kashak shiyan: Sairik shiyan kashungli vowels khangashan ā, ē, ī, ō, ū shiyan mashungda kapi shiyan. Kakhalat kashak: 'sa' (to do) vs 'sā' (animal/meat); 'sha' (to hear) vs 'shā' (hundred).
chapters.english_translation: TLS orthographic standardization: Strict adherence to vowel length markings (ā, ē, ī, ō, ū). Minimal pairs demonstrate phonemic vowel length: 'sa' (to do) versus 'sā' (animal/flesh); 'sha' (to hear) versus 'shā' (hundred).
grammar_points: Minimal vowel length contrasts distinguish lexical meanings.
Capitalization conventions in written Tangkhul.
comprehension_questions: Illustrate three minimal word pairs distinguished by vowel length.
Why is standardized orthography essential for textbooks?

chapters.title: Tuiwon kala Tuikashak: Grammar & Parts of Speech
chapters.summary: Nouns, pronouns, verbs, case markers (-na, -li, -wui, -eina), and sentence syntax.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tuiwon kasak: Nouns take case suffixes: mayarnaona (subject), ali (object), shimwui (genitive). Verbs take aspect suffixes: sai (present), sada (past), sara (future). Clause syntax: Subject + Object + Verb (SOV).
chapters.english_translation: Grammatical structures: Nouns inflect for syntactic roles: agentive (-na), accusative (-li), possessive (-wui). Verbs mark tense and aspect: present (-i), past (-da), future (-ra). Canonical word order is Subject-Object-Verb.
grammar_points: Postpositional clitics attach to noun phrase boundaries.
Verb agreement is aspectual rather than person-concordant.
comprehension_questions: Identify the subject, object, and verb in: 'Mayarnaona lairik pari.'
List the past tense suffixes in modern Tangkhul.

chapters.title: Iram Ukhrul wui Phanit: Seasonal Festivals
chapters.summary: Cultural rituals and community celebrations: Luira (Seed Sowing), Mangkhap, and Chumpha.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Luira Phanit hi Tangkhul wui phanit kaphamei thotna. Luira tharan iram kaphungli laa shakda Haora kachon khonseri. Chumpha phanitli kachak kashak shimli ungkazip mathaser; Mangkhap tharan kaphung shungli ngashan shiyan mathathotna.
chapters.english_translation: The Luira seed-sowing festival is the premier seasonal observance of the Tangkhuls. Villagers sing ancestral melodies adorned in traditional Haora shawls. At Chumpha festival, newly harvested grain is consecrated, and during Mangkhap, community feasting strengthens communal bonds.
grammar_points: Temporal case suffix -tharan indicates 'during / at the time of'.
Cultural compound nouns (Luira Phanit, Haora Kachon).
comprehension_questions: What is the agricultural significance of the Luira festival?
Which traditional shawl is worn during seasonal celebrations?

chapters.title: Meila Won: Poetic Selections & Traditional Haola
chapters.summary: Classical and modern Tangkhul verses celebrating love, courage, nature, and longing.
chapters.tangkhul_text:
Laa tuitam: 'Phungreitangli meila won kapha wonri,
Zingsho kaphungli leishat laa shakri.
Iram Ukhrul ram wui thot mathamei,
Mayarnaomayana ningkachon pamei.'
Haola tuihi Tangkhul wui akhara shiyan thotna.
chapters.english_translation:
Poetic verse: 'On Phungreitang hill, lovely blossoms unfurl,
Across the eastern ridge, melodies of love arise.
Our Ukhrul homeland generation thrives,
In the hearts of our youth, true devotion endures.'
The Haola poetic genre encapsulates Tangkhul lyricism.
grammar_points: Rhyme and assonance in Tangkhul four-line poetic stanzas.
Repetition of floral and geographical metaphors.
comprehension_questions: What natural imagery is employed in the opening stanza of Meila Won?
Define the oral literary significance of Haola.

chapters.title: Kahaotui: Composition, Writing & Review Exercises
chapters.summary: Practical writing skills, letter composition, paragraph formulation, and chapter reviews.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Kapi shiyan: Lairik kapi, shiyan ngashitda chithi kapi. 'Izeishinaoli chithi: Izeinao kaphā, nali khamorwi kahang, ithumwui shimli ungkazip mathalu.' Tuikashak khangachan: Vowels shiyan mashunglu, tuiwon bingli case suffixes sanglu.
chapters.english_translation: Composition exercises: Essay writing and letter composition. 'Letter to a friend: Dear friend, I send you heartfelt greetings and invite you to join us at our home.' Review drills: Verify vowel markings and affix appropriate case suffixes.
grammar_points: Formal salutations in Tangkhul letter writing.
Syntactic coordination of compound sentences using 'kala' (and) and 'kha' (but).
comprehension_questions: Draft a five-sentence letter in Tangkhul inviting a friend to Luira festival.
Complete the grammatical review exercises on nominal cases.

pages.title: Chapter 6: Iram Ukhrul wui Phanit: Seasonal Festivals
lines: CHAPTER 6: IRAM UKHRUL WUI PHANIT: SEASONAL FESTIVALS
Summary: Cultural rituals and community celebrations: Luira (Seed Sowing), Mangkhap, and Chumpha.
Luira Phanit hi Tangkhul wui phanit kaphamei thotna. Luira tharan iram
kaphungli laa shakda Haora kachon khonseri. Chumpha phanitli kachak
kashak shimli ungkazip mathaser; Mangkhap tharan kaphung shungli ngashan
The Luira seed-sowing festival is the premier seasonal observance of the
Tangkhuls. Villagers sing ancestral melodies adorned in traditional
Haora shawls. At Chumpha festival, newly harvested grain is consecrated,
and during Mangkhap, community feasting strengthens communal bonds.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 1: Tuitam Khare: Iram Ukhrul (Homeland & Heritage)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Iram Ukhrul hi kaphung kashungli kazei ram thotna. Tangkhul Folk Songs and Cultural Lore wui tuitam khareli ithum iramwui maran kala kaphana otbingli themkhapei. Shirui Kashong kaphungli Kashongwon wonri; Phangrei phungli mayarnaomayana laa shakda mathapamei.
excerpts.translation_en: Our homeland Ukhrul is nestled high amidst the mountain ridges. In Chapter 1 of Tangkhul Folk Songs and Cultural Lore, we learn of the beauty, geography, and ancestral heritage of our hills. On Mount Shirui, the famed Shirui Lily blooms, and across Phangrei peak, youth sing songs of celebration.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 2: Khararchan: Tangkhul Folktales & Ancestral Lore
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Shimreishang kala Maitonphi wui khararchan hi Tangkhul ngachaili leishat kachak wari thotna. Phungcham ramli kapam Maitonphi kachihi ramwui won kapha thotna; Shimreishangna awui ningli leikashi pamei. Kha shiyan khangatei eina thot kakhara kachang leiyi.
excerpts.translation_en: The folktale of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most celebrated romance in Tangkhul oral tradition. Living in Phungcham village, Maitonphi was the fairest blossom of the land; Shimreishang loved her dearly. Yet clan custom and fateful trials intervened.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 3: Paotam: Proverbs, Idioms & Elder Wisdom

'When young men uphold righteous conduct, the foundation of the community is honored.' These proverbial maxims encode ancestral philosophy.

front_matter.preface: Jesuwui La: Hymns in Tangkhul Naga, compiled and translated by Rev. William Pettigrew (American Baptist Mission House, Ukhrul, Manipur, Assam, 1907, 2nd Edition; printed at Baptist Mission Press, Calcutta). Preserves the earliest published Christian hymnal and devotional poetry in the Ukhrul dialect of Tangkhul Naga.

table_of_contents.title: Hymns of the Kingdom & Eternal Life

chapters.title: Early Devotional Hymns
chapters.summary: Classic devotional hymns including 'Jesus Loves Me' (Hi Jesuna Laishi).
chapters.tangkhul_text: 1. Hi Jesuna laishi, khikala jila, in a Vare chiwui lairikli, palaga I shitsanga. Ma, ili laishi! Ma, ili laishi! Ma, ili laishi! Lairikli iya. 2. Hi Jesuna laishi, A mangla chihomihai; Varina kaching khamaug shomida changmilakra. 3. Ili Jesuna laishi, noshino awui nona; athum masathukmana, Ana kamakangvana. 4. Hi Jesuna laishi, iwui moral pheomira; khikala jila awui Mangla chihomihaira.
chapters.english_translation: 1. Jesus loves me, this I know, for the Bible tells me so; little ones to Him belong, they are weak but He is strong. Yes, Jesus loves me! The Bible tells me so. 2. Jesus loves me, He who died heaven's gate to open wide; He will wash away my sin. 3. Jesus loves me, loves me still, though I'm very weak and ill; from His shining throne on high. 4. Jesus loves me, He will stay close beside me all the way; He has washed away my sin.
grammar_points: Early orthography feature: 'ai' diphthong where TLS standardizes to 'ei'.
Future tense inflection -ra in 'pheomira' (will cleanse).
comprehension_questions: How is divine love expressed in early Pettigrew Tangkhul hymnody?
What orthographic differences distinguish the 1907 text from modern TLS spelling?

chapters.title: Hymns of Divine Grace & Love
chapters.summary: Grace and security in faith: 'Safe in the Arms of Jesus' (He Jesuwui Makali).
chapters.tangkhul_text: 1. He Jesuwui makali, eingphalaka; siwui ngahan ngaida romhai, phasa kakhanang rai. Kachingwui chan nganalu, iwui la sada laili, Jesuna nani mashitta, hangda la kasana. 2. He Jesuwui makali, kangachee malaimana; I moral maphungmara, chiaina makhanangmara. Wukli kakhanang malaita, ringkapha apamna, mikumo awui okkathui ringkapha kashungna.
chapters.english_translation: 1. Safe in the arms of Jesus, safe on His gentle breast; there by His love o'ershaded, sweetly my soul shall rest. Hark! 'tis the voice of angels, borne in a song to me. 2. Safe in the arms of Jesus, safe from corroding care; safe from the world's temptations, sin cannot harm me there. Free from the blight of sorrow, free from my doubts and fears.
grammar_points: Negative particle malaimana indicating complete absence.
Postpositional phrase attachment with genitive -wui.
comprehension_questions: What metaphor is used to express spiritual peace in Chapter 2?
Identify the negative verbal constructions in the stanzas.

chapters.title: Penitential & Supplication Hymns
chapters.summary: Supplication and fellowship: 'What a Friend We Have in Jesus' (Jesuli Ithum Kaphā Temi).
chapters.tangkhul_text: 1. Jesuli ithum kaphā temi akha leiyi, ithumwui moral kala kakhanang saikora phungmiya. Khorum-ngacheida Varili kachiphun mathaloikhalang, ningkhamayung tarakha ithum khamatai thotna. 2. Khipana kakhanang kala ningkachuk phunga? Jesuwui lili vashitlaga khorumlu. Ana khipakha matheikhui-mana malei, ningchang lak eina temkhamishi phapharomei.
chapters.english_translation: 1. What a friend we have in Jesus, all our sins and griefs to bear! What a privilege to carry everything to God in prayer! O what peace we often forfeit, O what needless pain we bear. 2. Have we trials and temptations? Is there trouble anywhere? We should never be discouraged; take it to the Lord in prayer. In His arms He'll take and shield thee; thou wilt find a solace there.
grammar_points: Dative case marker -li in personal relations ('Jesuli', 'Varili').
Rhetorical interrogation marker with 'khipana'.
comprehension_questions: What is the Tangkhul equivalent for 'prayer' in Pettigrew's text?
Translate into Tangkhul: 'Jesus is our faithful friend.'

chapters.title: Pilgrim & Faith Hymns
chapters.summary: Unshakable refuge: 'Rock of Ages' (Aching Lungrei Makatha).
chapters.tangkhul_text: 1. Aching lungrei iwui vang kakhayei, nawui khamangli ili kaphumpam milu. Nawui azing eina kathur tara kala ashi china iwui moral shiman ngasaku. 2. Iwui pang eina kasa otna nawui shiyan makhararthukmana; kachara zangzang shoklala nawui akhavawuina. Na vathot iwui kachiphun, nawui crossli i panglakha ngaranmida leiyi.
chapters.english_translation: 1. Rock of Ages, cleft for me, let me hide myself in Thee; let the water and the blood, from Thy wounded side which flowed, be of sin the double cure, save from wrath and make me pure. 2. Not the labors of my hands can fulfill Thy law's demands; could my zeal no respite know, could my tears forever flow, all for sin could not atone; Thou must save, and Thou alone.
grammar_points: Causative suffix -sak in 'shiman ngasaku' (cause to disappear).
Instrumental/ablative clitic -eina in 'pang eina'.
comprehension_questions: Explain the geological metaphor of 'Aching lungrei' in Tangkhul hymnody.
Identify the causative verbs in Chapter 4.

chapters.title: Hymns of the Kingdom & Eternal Life
chapters.summary: The heavenly river: 'Shall We Gather at the River' (Kongreili Ithum Ngazipra).
chapters.tangkhul_text: 1. Kaching Kazingramwui kongreili, Varewui khamatha apamli, ithum saikora ngazipra? Ma, ithum ngazipra kong kaphali, kong kaphali, Varewui kuiram ngachaili ngazipsera. 2. Kongrei chihui ngashilakna, thikahai maleimana; Vare eina A Naochina karing khangarum ramli.
chapters.english_translation: 1. Shall we gather at the river, where bright angel feet have trod, with its crystal tide forever flowing by the throne of God? Yes, we'll gather at the river, the beautiful river. 2. On the margin of the river, washing up its silver spray, we will walk and worship ever, all the happy golden day.
grammar_points: Future marker -sera denoting collective completion.
Repetition of nouns for poetic emphasis: 'kong kaphali, kong kaphali'.
comprehension_questions: What celestial imagery is depicted in the hymn?
How is collective gathering expressed morphologically?

chapters.title: Morning, Evening & Daily Life Hymns
chapters.summary: Evening meditation: 'Abide With Me' (I Eina Pamchinglu).
chapters.tangkhul_text: 1. Zimik tunhaira, ngaya kaching chuiye; Kazing khayingli i eina pamchinglu. Katei ngashunkhami kacham chitharanli, khangachamwui Ava, i eina pamchinglu. 2. Okkathui mirin hi thakta kanthuiseri; kuipham, ngashan saikora themthuira. Khamatei malei nawui ngachaili pamlu; Makangateipa, i eina pamchinglu.
chapters.english_translation: 1. Abide with me: fast falls the eventide; the darkness deepens; Lord, with me abide. When other helpers fail and comforts flee, Help of the helpless, O abide with me. 2. pages.header: Chapter 2: Hymns of Divine Grace & Love (Page 6)
pages.title: Chapter 2: Hymns of Divine Grace & Love
lines: CHAPTER 2: HYMNS OF DIVINE GRACE & LOVE
Summary: Grace and security in faith: 'Safe in the Arms of Jesus' (He Jesuwui Makali).
1. He Jesuwui makali, eingphalaka; siwui ngahan ngaida romhai, phasa
kakhanang rai. Kachingwui chan nganalu, iwui la sada laili, Jesuna nani
mashitta, hangda la kasana. 2. He Jesuwui makali, kangachee malaimana; I
moral maphungmara, chiaina makhanangmara. Wukli kakhanang malaita,
ringkapha apamna, mikumo awui okkathui ringkapha kashungna.
1. Safe in the arms of Jesus, safe on His gentle breast; there by His
love o'ershaded, sweetly my soul shall rest. Hark! 'tis the voice of
angels, borne in a song to me. 2. Safe in the arms of Jesus, safe from
corroding care; safe from the world's temptations, sin cannot harm me
there. Free from the blight of sorrow, free from my doubts and fears.

pages.title: Chapter 3: Penitential & Supplication Hymns
lines: Summary: Supplication and fellowship: 'What a Friend We Have in Jesus' (Jesuli Ithum Kaphā Temi).
1. Jesuli ithum kaphā temi akha leiyi, ithumwui moral kala kakhanang
saikora phungmiya. Khorum-ngacheida Varili kachiphun mathaloikhalang,
ningkhamayung tarakha ithum khamatai thotna. 2. Khipana kakhanang kala
ningkachuk phunga? Jesuwui lili vashitlaga khorumlu. Ana khipakha
matheikhui-mana malei, ningchang lak eina temkhamishi phapharomei.
1. What a friend we have in Jesus, all our sins and griefs to bear! What
a privilege to carry everything to God in prayer! O what peace we often
forfeit, O what needless pain we bear. 2. Have we trials and
temptations? Is there trouble anywhere? We should never be discouraged;
take it to the Lord in prayer. In His arms He'll take and shield thee;
thou wilt find a solace there.

Ana khipakha matheikhui-mana malei, ningchang lak eina temkhamishi phapharomei.

lines: Summary: Unshakable refuge: 'Rock of Ages' (Aching Lungrei Makatha).

milu. Nawui azing eina kathur tara kala ashi china iwui moral shiman

nawui crossli i panglakha ngaranmida leiyi.

and the blood, from Thy wounded side which flowed, be of sin the double
cure, save from wrath and make me pure. 2. Not the labors of my hands

tears forever flow, all for sin could not atone; Thou must save, and

excerpts.translation_en: 1. Safe in the arms of Jesus, safe on His gentle breast; there by His love o'ershaded, sweetly my soul shall rest. Hark! 'tis the voice of angels, borne in a song to me. 2. Safe in the arms of Jesus, safe from corroding care; safe from the world's temptations, sin cannot harm me there. Free from the blight of sorrow, free from my doubts and fears.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 3: Penitential & Supplication Hymns
excerpts.tangkhul_text: 1. Jesuli ithum kaphā temi akha leiyi, ithumwui moral kala kakhanang saikora phungmiya. Khorum-ngacheida Varili kachiphun mathaloikhalang, ningkhamayung tarakha ithum khamatai thotna. 2. Khipana kakhanang kala ningkachuk phunga? Jesuwui lili vashitlaga khorumlu. Ana khipakha matheikhui-mana malei, ningchang lak eina temkhamishi phapharomei.
excerpts.translation_en: 1. What a friend we have in Jesus, all our sins and griefs to bear! What a privilege to carry everything to God in prayer! O what peace we often forfeit, O what needless pain we bear. 2. Have we trials and temptations? Is there trouble anywhere? We should never be discouraged; take it to the Lord in prayer. In His arms He'll take and shield thee; thou wilt find a solace there.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 4: Pilgrim & Faith Hymns
excerpts.tangkhul_text: 1. Aching lungrei iwui vang kakhayei, nawui khamangli ili kaphumpam milu. Nawui azing eina kathur tara kala ashi china iwui moral shiman ngasaku. 2. Iwui pang eina kasa otna nawui shiyan makhararthukmana; kachara zangzang shoklala nawui akhavawuina. Na vathot iwui kachiphun, nawui crossli i panglakha ngaranmida leiyi.
excerpts.translation_en: 1. Rock of Ages, cleft for me, let me hide myself in Thee; let the water and the blood, from Thy wounded side which flowed, be of sin the double cure, save from wrath and make me pure. 2. Not the labors of my hands can fulfill Thy law's demands; could my zeal no respite know, could my tears forever flow, all for sin could not atone; Thou must save, and Thou alone.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 5: Hymns of the Kingdom & Eternal Life
excerpts.tangkhul_text: 1. Kaching Kazingramwui kongreili, Varewui khamatha apamli, ithum saikora ngazipra? Ma, ithum ngazipra kong kaphali, kong kaphali, Varewui kuiram ngachaili ngazipsera. 2. Kongrei chihui ngashilakna, thikahai maleimana; Vare eina A Naochina karing khangarum ramli.
excerpts.translation_en: 1. Shall we gather at the river, where bright angel feet have trod, with its crystal tide forever flowing by the throne of God? Yes, we'll gather at the river, the beautiful river. 2. On the margin of the river, washing up its silver spray, we will walk and worship ever, all the happy golden day.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 6: Morning, Evening & Daily Life Hymns
excerpts.tangkhul_text: 1. Zimik tunhaira, ngaya kaching chuiye; Kazing khayingli i eina pamchinglu. Katei ngashunkhami kacham chitharanli, khangachamwui Ava, i eina pamchinglu. 2. Okkathui mirin hi thakta kanthuiseri; kuipham, ngashan saikora themthuira. Khamatei malei nawui ngachaili pamlu; Makangateipa, i eina pamchinglu.
excerpts.translation_en: 1. Abide with me: fast falls the eventide; the darkness deepens; Lord, with me abide. When other helpers fail and comforts flee, Help of the helpless, O abide with me. 2. Swift to its close ebbs out life's little day; earth's joys grow dim; its glories pass away; change and decay in all around I see; O Thou who changest not, abide with me.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 7: Doxologies, Anthems & Closing Liturgy
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Vare khamatha kashungli, ngalei miyur saikorana matheilu; Kaching Kazingramwui mangla bing, Vare A Mingli mathaseru. Ava, A Nao, kala Mangla Kathara, ngashan kashung kumching-kumching leiyangranu. Amen. Ithumwui Ava Kazingramli kapam, Nawui ming kathara thada kharing sairanu. Nawui ngashan ram raranu. Nawui ning Kazingramli thada ngaleili la ngarunsangranu. Aja ithumwui kasala kashakpei milu. Ithumli kateina kashikhami pheomikahai thada ithumwui moralla pheomilu. Ithumli ngasateikhavaili mathalukhavai masangasaklu, kha kashieina kankhuimilu. Amen.
excerpts.translation_en: Praise God from whom all blessings flow; praise Him all creatures here below; praise Him above, ye heavenly host; praise Father, Son, and Holy Ghost. Amen. Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be Thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For Thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, forever. Amen.

Hodson, late Assistant Political Agent in Manipur and Superintendent of the State (Macmillan and Co., Limited, London, 1911). Presents the authoritative historical and ethnographic documentation of the Tangkhul Nagas, their habitat, social organization, village headmanship, folktales, ballads, and linguistic survey.

chapters.title: Habitat, Geography & Tribal Divisions
chapters.summary: Geographical territory and four subdivisions: Raphei, Kathur, Kamo, and Kharao.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul miyur hi Manipur wui kaphung zanshorli pamda kaphung khangacheo eina ngashitna. Ayur khani eina mati leiyi: Raphei (Northern Tangkhuls), Kathur (Central Tangkhuls around Ukhrul), Kamo (Southern Tangkhuls bordering Maring territory), and Kharao (Western Tangkhuls facing the valley). Ukhrul kaphung hi phungreitang sada kaphung khangateiwui tui ngazekpam thada leiyi.
chapters.english_translation: The Tangkhuls occupy the mountain tracts east of the valley of Manipur. They are grouped into four main territorial sections: Raphei in the north, Kathur in the centre around Ukhrul and Hungpung, Kamo in the south, and Kharao in the west. Ukhrul serves as the recognized linguistic standard among all regional dialects.
grammar_points: Locative case marker -li attached to geographical names.
Directional nominalization: zanshor (east), zantung (west).
comprehension_questions: What are the four historical subdivisions of the Tangkhul territory?
Why was Ukhrul selected as the central standard by early linguists?

chapters.title: Tangkhul Linguistic Classification & Dialects
chapters.summary: Agglutinative morphology, vowel length contrasts, and Tibeto-Burman affiliations.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul language exhibits agglutinative morphology with dominant prefix ka- forming adjectives and infinitives. Case relationships are indicated by postpositional affixes: -na (agentive), -li (dative/locative), -wui (genitive). Vowel length contrasts: 'sa' (to do) vs 'sā' (animal/flesh); 'mik' (eye) vs 'mei' (fire).
chapters.english_translation: Linguistic features of Tangkhul: Extensive use of prefixes and suffixes. Nominal and adjectival derivation through prefix ka-. Case markers function as postpositional clitics. Phonemic vowel length distinguishes essential vocabulary pairs.
grammar_points: Phonemic vowel length contrasts.
Agglutinative affix ordering in verbal complexes.
comprehension_questions: Give two examples of minimal vowel length pairs in Tangkhul.
Which prefix is predominantly used to form infinitives?

chapters.title: Village Organization & The Awunga (Headman)
chapters.summary: Hereditary chieftainship (Awunga), the village council (Hangva), and clan clans (Shangnao).
chapters.tangkhul_text: Khaung kachida Awunga akha leiyi; Awunga hi shimkhurwui mathun eina ngashitna. Hangva council eina ngasoda ram shiyan kashak saikora ngazekseri. Shangnao kachida paman kathana mi akhakhana hangvali zangda khaungwui ot ngazeka.
chapters.english_translation: Every Tangkhul village is an autonomous democratic unit under a hereditary chief called the Awunga. The Awunga rules in consultation with the village council (Hangva), comprised of representatives from each clan (Shangnao), managing village land, disputes, and seasonal festivals.
grammar_points: Honorific register associated with the Awunga.
Reciprocal verbal affix ngazor / ngazek.
comprehension_questions: What is the role of the Hangva in village governance?
How is the position of Awunga inherited?

chapters.title: Traditional Laws, Land Tenure & Feasts of Merit
chapters.summary: Maran (Feasts of Merit), Tarung monuments, and terraced land rights.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Maran kashak hi Tangkhul ngashanli khamataiya otsak akhana. Tarung thingrei vakhang eina shimli shona. Seichang kala hok kachung khami eina ramnaoli shongza kashak saikora ngashitna. Lungto kala lungchan shoda awo-ayiwui machut saikora chimiksho chitheiya.
chapters.english_translation: The Feasts of Merit (Maran) represent the summit of customary social achievement. The celebrant earns the right to erect the carved Tarung monument post before his house. Mithuns and cattle are slaughtered to feast the entire community, and megalithic stone platforms are built.
grammar_points: Instrumental clitic -eina in monument dragging chants.
Nominal compounds combining animal terms and festive rites.
comprehension_questions: What privileges does a celebrant gain by performing Maran?
Describe the physical appearance and cultural meaning of the Tarung.

chapters.title: Tangkhul Folktales: Origin of the Species & Animals
chapters.summary: Mythological origin legends and the ancient brotherhood of hill and valley.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Awo-ayiwui khararchanli: 'Avah Samsokli tungthuiya, Makungana ili phungtung.' Chinaoni khani: kakhara a kaphungli leiyi, kakhanao a ngaleili vaipama. Meitei eina Tangkhul chinaoni thada kum kachida Mera Hou Chongba phanitli leikashi chithei ngaroka.
chapters.english_translation: Tangkhul mythology traces common origins from Samsok in the eastern hills. Tradition holds that two brothers parted ways: the elder brother settled in the misty Tangkhul heights, while the younger brother cultivated the fertile valley, establishing a bond renewed at the annual Mera festival.
grammar_points: Comparative conjunction thada (like, in the manner of).
Ablative suffix -eina in origin narratives.
comprehension_questions: What does the Samsok migration legend signify?
How is the kinship between Meiteis and Tangkhuls celebrated traditionally?

chapters.title: Traditional Tangkhul Ballads & Folk Poetry
chapters.summary: The epic ballad of Shimreishang and Maitonphi, and heroic martial poetry.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Shimreishang eina Maitonphiwui leikashiyi Tangkhul thotchanli kaphapamei laana. 'Avayo avayo, makhamalu Maitonphili rasha saka; sakhangaiye Maitonphi kharam thuihaowa.' Kazeiramli anili ngazipda kumching kumching leikashi ngazipsera.
chapters.english_translation: The tragic romance of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most famous epic ballad of the Tangkhuls. Forced apart by parental opposition and village taboos, their spirits are finally united in Kazeiram, the tranquil land of the departed where true lovers dwell forever.
grammar_points: Antiphonal dialogue structure in romantic verse.
Poetic vocabulary substitutions in folk metrics.
comprehension_questions: Why is the story of Shimreishang and Maitonphi significant in Tangkhul literature?
What is Kazeiram in traditional Tangkhul eschatology?

Systematic sound shifts across regional varieties.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 1: Habitat, Geography & Tribal Divisions
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul miyur hi Manipur wui kaphung zanshorli pamda kaphung khangacheo eina ngashitna. Ayur khani eina mati leiyi: Raphei (Northern Tangkhuls), Kathur (Central Tangkhuls around Ukhrul), Kamo (Southern Tangkhuls bordering Maring territory), and Kharao (Western Tangkhuls facing the valley). Ukhrul kaphung hi phungreitang sada kaphung khangateiwui tui ngazekpam thada leiyi.
excerpts.translation_en: The Tangkhuls occupy the mountain tracts east of the valley of Manipur. They are grouped into four main territorial sections: Raphei in the north, Kathur in the centre around Ukhrul and Hungpung, Kamo in the south, and Kharao in the west. Ukhrul serves as the recognized linguistic standard among all regional dialects.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 2: Tangkhul Linguistic Classification & Dialects
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Tangkhul language exhibits agglutinative morphology with dominant prefix ka- forming adjectives and infinitives. Case relationships are indicated by postpositional affixes: -na (agentive), -li (dative/locative), -wui (genitive). Vowel length contrasts: 'sa' (to do) vs 'sā' (animal/flesh); 'mik' (eye) vs 'mei' (fire).
excerpts.translation_en: Linguistic features of Tangkhul: Extensive use of prefixes and suffixes. Nominal and adjectival derivation through prefix ka-. Case markers function as postpositional clitics. Phonemic vowel length distinguishes essential vocabulary pairs.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 3: Village Organization & The Awunga (Headman)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Khaung kachida Awunga akha leiyi; Awunga hi shimkhurwui mathun eina ngashitna. Hangva council eina ngasoda ram shiyan kashak saikora ngazekseri. Shangnao kachida paman kathana mi akhakhana hangvali zangda khaungwui ot ngazeka.
excerpts.translation_en: Every Tangkhul village is an autonomous democratic unit under a hereditary chief called the Awunga. The Awunga rules in consultation with the village council (Hangva), comprised of representatives from each clan (Shangnao), managing village land, disputes, and seasonal festivals.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 4: Traditional Laws, Land Tenure & Feasts of Merit
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Maran kashak hi Tangkhul ngashanli khamataiya otsak akhana. Tarung thingrei vakhang eina shimli shona. Seichang kala hok kachung khami eina ramnaoli shongza kashak saikora ngashitna. Lungto kala lungchan shoda awo-ayiwui machut saikora chimiksho chitheiya.
excerpts.translation_en: The Feasts of Merit (Maran) represent the summit of customary social achievement. The celebrant earns the right to erect the carved Tarung monument post before his house. Mithuns and cattle are slaughtered to feast the entire community, and megalithic stone platforms are built.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 5: Tangkhul Folktales: Origin of the Species & Animals
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Awo-ayiwui khararchanli: 'Avah Samsokli tungthuiya, Makungana ili phungtung.' Chinaoni khani: kakhara a kaphungli leiyi, kakhanao a ngaleili vaipama. Meitei eina Tangkhul chinaoni thada kum kachida Mera Hou Chongba phanitli leikashi chithei ngaroka.
excerpts.translation_en: Tangkhul mythology traces common origins from Samsok in the eastern hills. Tradition holds that two brothers parted ways: the elder brother settled in the misty Tangkhul heights, while the younger brother cultivated the fertile valley, establishing a bond renewed at the annual Mera festival.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 6: Traditional Tangkhul Ballads & Folk Poetry
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Shimreishang eina Maitonphiwui leikashiyi Tangkhul thotchanli kaphapamei laana. 'Avayo avayo, makhamalu Maitonphili rasha saka; sakhangaiye Maitonphi kharam thuihaowa.' Kazeiramli anili ngazipda kumching kumching leikashi ngazipsera.
excerpts.translation_en: The tragic romance of Shimreishang and Maitonphi is the most famous epic ballad of the Tangkhuls. Forced apart by parental opposition and village taboos, their spirits are finally united in Kazeiram, the tranquil land of the departed where true lovers dwell forever.

chapters.title: Creation, Origins & Ancestral Migration Songs
chapters.summary: The emergence from Wahukong (Hwang-Ho) and migration from Samsok to Hunphun.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Oh! hauri haura kachida haulu? Oh! hauri haura wahukongda haowa, Oh! wahukongda tunga. O Kachili Tunglo Awa Samshokli Tunga, O Makungana ili phunga, O Makunganao ili pangthan, Lungshang makang ana safasing sing, Mala mangli Hunphun Ava kharar. O Ram wungaphei, Shokvaoli wungho maya; Mei wungayar Hunphun wunga kharara.
chapters.english_translation: From what far valley did our ancestors emerge? From the river of Wahukong they journeyed. From Samsok in the east our lineage migrated, guided by the staves of Makungana. In Hunphun the ancestral fathers settled and lit the permanent council fires.
grammar_points: Vocative interjections 'Oh!', 'O!'.
Alliterative couplets in oral metrics.
comprehension_questions: Where did Tangkhuls trace their ancient migration from?
What village was established as the mother-settlement?

chapters.title: Agricultural Cycles: Jhumming, Planting & Harvest
chapters.summary: Terrace work, transplantation songs (Luisom), and harvest celebration (Mahat).
chapters.tangkhul_text: Kongrei mathei kongrei, kongrei shailo marei salo; Matei kachui manoye, Mala ifu heinao naoye. Ithanvara iram leisaye, Isu luisa khinasa, ima lera khinasa; Maleira souralo, isa luisa lung haorana. Zingkum leiyao leiyameirano, chungmeida kharshokrano, phungshon phungthaigei.
chapters.english_translation: The terrace waters ripple, transplant the green shoots with joyous songs! Sweet is the labor on our ancestral hills; who will share my buffalo meat and drink my rice beer? May our granaries be filled to the rafters and the year bring peace and plenty.
grammar_points: Imperative exhortation in communal work songs.
Agricultural seasonal idioms.
comprehension_questions: What food and drink are shared during terrace work?
What does 'leiyameirano' mean?

chapters.title: Village Morung (Longra) & Dormitory Life Songs
chapters.summary: Longra drinking songs, companionship around the hearth, and youth solidarity.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Leader: I longnao (I Longra) ... ho...o...o! Members: Rapamlu ... ho...o...o! Machapralu ... ho...o...o! Sairam samjiya, sairam samjiya! Oh longra makazangwo, nawui shimli khisapamlo? Thakta razanglo, thakta razanglo!
chapters.english_translation: Leader: O comrades of the Longra! Members: Assemble, join the circle! Weep no more! The hunting grounds await our youth! Why linger solitary at home? Come swiftly into the warm circle of the dormitory hearth!
grammar_points: Leader-chorus call-and-response patterning.
Imperative markers -lu and -lo.
comprehension_questions: What social role did the Longra play in Tangkhul villages?
Describe the call-and-response structure of Song 38.

chapters.title: Historical Ballads: World War I & Regional Conflicts
chapters.summary: The 1917-18 France Labour Corps ballad and the 1919 Kuki War songs.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Rai ramli khava, rai ramli khava yaronpa, Yaronpa nakhi vasalo? Iya mavangai, sayisa sayi na tanti sahaowa. Franceshi ram khava, Franceli raikhavai; Makuiye makuiye, pham kata hiyo; Wungasam chap ngacha, rai ram khavayo. Ah khongjai rai khava yaronpa yaronva, Sangna ram penga yaronva; Kuiwung kuivaya suphung mei.
chapters.english_translation: Valiant young men journeying across distant seas to the battlefields of France in 1917; Putting on the soldier's uniform and marching into the unknown while elders lamented. In foreign lands they upheld the fearless reputation and honor of their ancestral hills.
grammar_points: Historical event dating embedded in oral songs.
Repetition of key lyrical phrases.
comprehension_questions: What historical event is memorialized in Song 21?
How did Tangkhul communities respond to the 1917 call?

chapters.title: Romance, Courtship & Love Songs (Leishat Laa)
chapters.summary: Courtship dialogues, fishing expeditions, and declarations of enduring fidelity.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Nana Kanta singloo, Ina Khailan singda, Kongli alei shonsa yahoo! Oh iwui sakhangai aluinao, kathuili oja saleiya aluinao; Mayo kachang tarn rahaira aluinao. Oh ini lungchang malai haosa, phaningda makhui aluinao leishiya; Kazingli samphangluinaosa aluinao.
chapters.english_translation: Take up your net and I will carry the line; together we shall cross the mountain stream! Beloved maiden, your smile brightens the terrace fields like springtime blossoms. Though our hands are parted here on earth, our souls are entwined forever in the sky.
grammar_points: First-person dual association in courtship songs.
Optative future in -luinaosa.
comprehension_questions: What stream-fishing metaphor is used in courting?
How is fidelity expressed beyond mortality?

chapters.title: Festival Dances & Virgin Songs (Laa Khanganui)
chapters.summary: The sacred Luira dance performed by young maidens and festival elegance.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Luira sangai uwa, hoksa sangai uwa; Awungo Awunga shangrei rukchang ura, Yarui rukthang Kazing mathang ngaiyijile. Zingkam won wonluiya, ngalanao mawonluipaiya; Ngalanaowa mawon luipaiya, nathanram khavasangmeiya. Phaoli chan ma-ungkhararyo, haoriva haorava leiretnasaya.
chapters.english_translation: The Luira festival arrives, the feast of pork is spread! The Awunga and elders assemble in regal attire. Wildflowers bloom upon the slopes every spring, but human youth blossoms only once; Dance with joy in the courtyard while youth shines bright and the festival drums resound.
grammar_points: Metaphor of fleeting youth compared with floral seasons.
Temporal conditional in festival chants.
comprehension_questions: When is the Laa Khanganui performed?
What philosophical truth is contained in the floral metaphor?

chapters.title: Laments, Funerary Memorials & Philosophy
chapters.summary: Mourning over departed family and classical philosophical aphorisms.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Ili vaiphumlakha, Oh Ava khi mang shimanlo? Avayo khi mang shimanlo? Lengshongthei shimanna, Mayarnao mangna. Khamathan longli yurkathan masaralu, Ngaleizingli kapam sangmeiya (kazeiram); Khamna longli khangkaser masaralu, Ngaleizingli khyip sangmeiya.
chapters.english_translation: When grief engulfed me, what bright dream was lost? The pride of the lineage was cut down in youth. Boast not of wealth and pedigree on this mortal earth; beneath the ground in Kazeiram all sleep equally. Live in humility and kindness, for mortal life vanishes like morning mist on the ridges.
grammar_points: Prohibitive negative imperative -ralu in philosophical wisdom.
Poetic parallelisms.
comprehension_questions: What moral counsel is given regarding wealth in Chapter 7?
What is the meaning of 'Ngaleizingli'?

chapters.title: Patriotic Anthems & Tribal Identity
chapters.summary: Celebration of the Tangkhul homeland, Longpi pottery, and the Shirui Lily.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Ngashan yanglo hey, Tangkhul ngalei hi! Kaphung kapha kongrei kongra hey, Khipana phashok Tangkhul ram? Varewui sokkhami ramna. Oh Tangkhul avaram, Tangkhul sinaram! Khangayam machining Irong sampunram, Ham kasa ram chiya Longpi ram na saya; Khamakang shim savai Hungpungram cement, Shirui ram lily mavatma nanaobing! Ringpha meiranu, mahomeiranu!
chapters.english_translation: Behold our glorious homeland! Mountains and crystal rivers bestowed by God. Beloved Tangkhul motherland! Longpi crafting timeless black stone-pottery, Hungpung building solid foundations, and Shirui Kashung blooming with the rare Shirui Lily! May prosperity and honor abide in our land forever!
grammar_points: Patriotic exclamations with 'Ringpha meiranu!'.
Toponymic cataloguing of craft villages.
comprehension_questions: Which village is celebrated for its pottery tradition?
What famous flower is native to Shirui Kashung?

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 1: Creation, Origins & Ancestral Migration Songs
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Oh! hauri haura kachida haulu? Oh! hauri haura wahukongda haowa, Oh! wahukongda tunga. O Kachili Tunglo Awa Samshokli Tunga, O Makungana ili phunga, O Makunganao ili pangthan, Lungshang makang ana safasing sing, Mala mangli Hunphun Ava kharar. O Ram wungaphei, Shokvaoli wungho maya; Mei wungayar Hunphun wunga kharara.
excerpts.translation_en: From what far valley did our ancestors emerge? From the river of Wahukong they journeyed. From Samsok in the east our lineage migrated, guided by the staves of Makungana. In Hunphun the ancestral fathers settled and lit the permanent council fires.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 2: Agricultural Cycles: Jhumming, Planting & Harvest
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Kongrei mathei kongrei, kongrei shailo marei salo; Matei kachui manoye, Mala ifu heinao naoye. Ithanvara iram leisaye, Isu luisa khinasa, ima lera khinasa; Maleira souralo, isa luisa lung haorana. Zingkum leiyao leiyameirano, chungmeida kharshokrano, phungshon phungthaigei.
excerpts.translation_en: The terrace waters ripple, transplant the green shoots with joyous songs! Sweet is the labor on our ancestral hills; who will share my buffalo meat and drink my rice beer? May our granaries be filled to the rafters and the year bring peace and plenty.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 3: Village Morung (Longra) & Dormitory Life Songs
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Leader: I longnao (I Longra) ... ho...o...o! Members: Rapamlu ... ho...o...o! Machapralu ... ho...o...o! Sairam samjiya, sairam samjiya! Oh longra makazangwo, nawui shimli khisapamlo? Thakta razanglo, thakta razanglo!
excerpts.translation_en: Leader: O comrades of the Longra! Members: Assemble, join the circle! Weep no more! The hunting grounds await our youth! Why linger solitary at home? Come swiftly into the warm circle of the dormitory hearth!

chapters.title: Invocations & Spring Songs (Zingkum Hao Kaphok)
chapters.summary: Hokharai war-cry and spring arrival songs heralded by Sampheirok and Koktui.
chapters.tangkhul_text: AE-HE! Phamei yameisa HE... HE. O--O-HU-O! Ilongnao laa sa usa, Kashishoklu, kaphazanglu--O--Hui-O-hui! O, kazingkum ura, o, kazingkum ura, o, hungnaovayo luithuimihaolu; Mamanaomara, hungnaovayo luithuimashunga; Sampheirokna riri rakhonga, koktui vana zingkum phungraya!
chapters.english_translation: Hokharai invocation: May the better be ours! Let us sing, may evil depart and divine goodness enter! O, spring has begun! Your highness, sow the seeds for the year; royal venture is just and timely; The Sampheirok sings melodiously and the cuckoo heralds the arrival of the fruitful year!
grammar_points: Ritual invocation phonetics.
Reduplication in bird call onomatopoeia ('riri rakhonga').
comprehension_questions: What is Hokharai and when is it performed?
Which birds announce the arrival of spring?

chapters.title: Tarung Carrying & Monument Construction Songs
chapters.summary: Dragging the monumental Tarung tree from the forest and erecting megaliths.
chapters.tangkhul_text: O, yarso thingrei vakhang, thingpitang tak ungrall yaronnao, thingreiva ungreilu! Seichang kharaei hangmi phalungra, phanora vashatta chaklen meikan naona kacheka, lumlao sakda vakhuiphalungra. O, Kashongta phung-o, maranla saya; ilangkaso machilo, I wui luiyi kaya lhuiito, I wui chumrei hjorphiya!
chapters.english_translation: O young men, lift the mighty tree! The twigs bend, pull together with sturdy cane ropes; The sacrificial mithun is provided, the augury bird Chaklen gave favorable omens; carry home the Tarung! I built this house from humble beginnings; my terrace fields are fertile and granary full!
grammar_points: Collective working rhythm in dragging chants.
Augury interpretation terminology.
comprehension_questions: What bird's call determines the auspiciousness of monument hauling?
What animal is sacrificed for the Tarung?

chapters.title: Ceremonial Dance & Hornbill Movements (Pheishon Laa)
chapters.summary: Dance steps modeled on the flight and wingbeats of the great Indian hornbill.
chapters.tangkhul_text: O, iram hongreili, Mafathing kasui kharipna; Ngachamching arang shangkaya, arangchi khili kachanlo? Mafathei channa, arangkho arangkhon ngashing leishiya; Thuingashing, kashung shanghaowa.
chapters.english_translation: In our ancient forests, the majestic Mafathing trees spread their wide canopy; Upon their boughs perch the great hornbills; why have they gathered in numbers? For the ripe Mafa fruits they have flown; with rhythmic wingbeats they soar towards the mountain peaks!
grammar_points: Choreographic terminology encoded in song lyrics.
Rhythmic meter imitating animal locomotion.
comprehension_questions: What bird inspires the choreography of Pheishon?
Why is the hornbill culturally sacred to Tangkhuls?

chapters.title: Maiden Dances & Youth Festivals (Yarra Laa)
chapters.summary: Laa Khanganui maiden dances and the Yarra spring festival of the youth.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Kazingkum huimailo aria, shivanaoli khina sale? Kha shingnai rao vasaya, he ring khaya zak matheiya. Kongrali theo theo, ilongnaova khithing kaphato? Ilongnaova longthing kaphana, meishum kapamnao zangyo!
chapters.english_translation: Let the seasons turn in gentleness! Maidens dance in the village square in graceful innocence. What merry voices echo by the stream? The youth gather firewood for the annual Yarra celebration!
grammar_points: Youth-group terminology.
Onomatopoeic stream sounds 'theo theo'.
comprehension_questions: In which months is the Yarra festival celebrated?
What activity do the youth undertake during Yarra?

chapters.title: Agriculture, Terrace Labor & Cowherd Songs
chapters.summary: Luisom paddy planting chants and Sei Hom cowherd ballads of solitary orphans.
chapters.tangkhul_text: O, I siluisa, I siluisa khinashai? I makreira khina mang, makreira sangralu; Shama maran saluira. Ava khaho malei, aya kaho malei, seihom langphaizaya; Shok reo rangpamshona, silui shur khani chi kachui laga yaronnao chara horlama.
chapters.english_translation: Who will feast on my buffalo meat, who will drink my aged rice beer? Pour generously for the laborers! No parents call my name; upon the high grassy slopes I herd buffalos alone from dawn till dusk, Tending the herds while silent tears trace lines upon my face.
grammar_points: Rhetorical questions in festive work songs.
Poignant elegiac tone in pastoral chants.
comprehension_questions: What contrast is drawn between festive terrace planting and cowherd life?
What is 'siluisa'?

chapters.title: Martial Ballads & Head-hunting Epics (Ral Laa)
chapters.summary: Ancient heroic victory chants and warrior prowess of Lunghar and Ringui.
chapters.tangkhul_text: O, atung shangla rai sakashiyavo, Lunghar yaron ni chiya! Azing takha rai sakashiyavo, Ringui yaron ni chiya! Shangching Shangshak na ili khachitna chiya, shimin kayang ra mahon shok! Kharing sing singa, ili mangakatshelu!
chapters.english_translation: Behold in the northern heights the gallant warriors of Lunghar stand ready! In the southern ranges the brave youths of Ringui guard the mountain passes; They fear me as the tiger of the forest; challenge me not, for our victory shout resounds!
grammar_points: Vocative and boastful declamatory syntax.
Geographical identifiers of warrior clans.
comprehension_questions: Which two villages are celebrated as warrior centres?
What does 'kharing sing' mean?

chapters.title: Traditional Love Romances (Shimreishang & Maitonphi)
chapters.summary: The immortal romance of Shimreishang and Maitonphi in antiphonal dialogue.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Avayo avayo, makhamalu, Maitonphili rasha saka; sakhangaiye Maitonphi kharam thuihaowa. Laishikhavai chi lunamlizang ngaroksa; Coi marongthei reola khuisingda lung ringa. Ameishang Ameishang, Ira kachangli thuiulu; Maitonphi, pangthui haosa, ini lungchan malaihaosa.
chapters.english_translation: Elders, do not forbid! For sweet Maitonphi alone does my heart beat in devotion; Though adverse circumstances part us in this earthly life, our love remains green like the mountain pine. Beloved Ameishang, farewell on this mortal shore; in the spirit realm beyond, we shall part no more.
grammar_points: Antiphonal romantic dialogue.
Symbolism of botanical endurance.
comprehension_questions: What plant symbolizes unyielding love in the ballad?
How does the story conclude in traditional belief?

chapters.title: Weaving Songs, Festive Banquets & Bedtime Chants
chapters.summary: Back-strap loom weaving (Themsak), traditional shawls, and evening chants (Pet Laa).
chapters.tangkhul_text: O Tangkhul ngalanao yanglu yanglu, sak kasa kathemma themma; Haora chi yaron kachonna, Phangyai rah Tangkhul kashanna! Phungcham vana ratha apamva rarona, phanishida tarikhana vaotun; Nali ungthuilo, sami ngachiya, i ram kashamshiraro.
chapters.english_translation: Behold the skilled Tangkhul maidens weaving traditional textiles with masterly artistry! The black-and-red Haora shawl is for valiant young men, and the Phangyai skirt for graceful women. Evening settles over the ridges of Phungcham; put aside your tools and find peaceful sleep.
grammar_points: Textile terminology and designators.
Evening benedictory phrasing.
comprehension_questions: What is Haora and who wears it?
What is Phangyai and what colors define it?

O young men, lift the mighty tree! The twigs bend, pull together with

from humble beginnings; my terrace fields are fertile and granary full!

canopy; Upon their boughs perch the great hornbills; why have they
gathered in numbers? For the ripe Mafa fruits they have flown; with
rhythmic wingbeats they soar towards the mountain peaks!

lines: CHAPTER 4: MAIDEN DANCES & YOUTH FESTIVALS (YARRA LAA)
Summary: Laa Khanganui maiden dances and the Yarra spring festival of the youth.
Kazingkum huimailo aria, shivanaoli khina sale? Kha shingnai rao vasaya,
he ring khaya zak matheiya. Kongrali theo theo, ilongnaova khithing
kaphato? Ilongnaova longthing kaphana, meishum kapamnao zangyo!
Let the seasons turn in gentleness! Maidens dance in the village square
in graceful innocence. What merry voices echo by the stream? The youth
gather firewood for the annual Yarra celebration!

lines: CHAPTER 5: AGRICULTURE, TERRACE LABOR & COWHERD SONGS
Summary: Luisom paddy planting chants and Sei Hom cowherd ballads of solitary orphans.
O, I siluisa, I siluisa khinashai? I makreira khina mang, makreira
sangralu; Shama maran saluira. Ava khaho malei, aya kaho malei, seihom
langphaizaya; Shok reo rangpamshona, silui shur khani chi kachui laga
Who will feast on my buffalo meat, who will drink my aged rice beer?
Pour generously for the laborers! No parents call my name; upon the high
grassy slopes I herd buffalos alone from dawn till dusk, Tending the
herds while silent tears trace lines upon my face.

lines: CHAPTER 6: MARTIAL BALLADS & HEAD-HUNTING EPICS (RAL LAA)
Summary: Ancient heroic victory chants and warrior prowess of Lunghar and Ringui.

Behold in the northern heights the gallant warriors of Lunghar stand
ready! In the southern ranges the brave youths of Ringui guard the

pages.title: Chapter 7: Traditional Love Romances (Shimreishang & Maitonphi)
lines: Summary: The immortal romance of Shimreishang and Maitonphi in antiphonal dialogue.
Avayo avayo, makhamalu, Maitonphili rasha saka; sakhangaiye Maitonphi
kharam thuihaowa. Laishikhavai chi lunamlizang ngaroksa; Coi marongthei
reola khuisingda lung ringa. Ameishang Ameishang, Ira kachangli thuiulu;
Maitonphi, pangthui haosa, ini lungchan malaihaosa.
Elders, do not forbid! For sweet Maitonphi alone does my heart beat in
devotion; Though adverse circumstances part us in this earthly life, our
love remains green like the mountain pine. Beloved Ameishang, farewell
on this mortal shore; in the spirit realm beyond, we shall part no more.

chapters.title: The Legend of Hundung & The White Cow
chapters.summary: Founding of Hundung village guided by the sacred pregnant cow.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Awo-ayiwui thotchanli: Seiva kachang akha leilaga apha kapha apamli vatuda seinao phanung tharanli Hundung khaung phokna. Kaphung kaphali zatlaga seiva china apam kaphā akha theilaga pamshona; chili seinao phada awo-ayina 'Hundung' (Hungpung) da hoya.
chapters.english_translation: Ancestral lore recounts that the village founders followed a sacred white cow across the hills. Wherever the cow rested upon the fertile plateau, there she gave birth to her calf, and upon that blessed ground the ancient mother-village of Hundung was founded.
grammar_points: Founding legend narrative formula.
Temporal clause marker tharanli.
comprehension_questions: What animal guided the founders of Hundung?
What does this legend symbolize in Tangkhul pastoralism?

chapters.title: The Two Brothers & Migration to the Hills
chapters.summary: The covenant between elder brother (hills) and younger brother (valley).
chapters.tangkhul_text: Chinaoni khani wui tui: kakhara a kaphungli pamda kakhanao a ngaleili vaipama. Anili khangaran shiyan leiyi: kakhara na kaphungwui theishak kala khuira chili ngaleili phungmiya; kakhanao na ngaleiwui machi kala kachon chili kaphungli phungmiya.
chapters.english_translation: The legend of the two brothers: the elder brother chose the high mountain ridges, while the younger brother cultivated the valley plains. They established a covenant: the elder sent mountain forest produce and honey to the plain, and the younger returned salt and woven cloth.
grammar_points: Reciprocal trade terminology in oral covenants.
Contrastive particle na.
comprehension_questions: What goods did the two brothers exchange?
How does this folktale reflect historical trade between hills and valley?

chapters.title: Animal Fables: The Tiger and the Clever Toad
chapters.summary: Wit triumphs over brute force in the forest.

pages.header: Chapter 1: The Legend of Hundung & The White Cow (Page 4)
pages.title: Chapter 1: The Legend of Hundung & The White Cow
lines: CHAPTER 1: THE LEGEND OF HUNDUNG & THE WHITE COW
Summary: Founding of Hundung village guided by the sacred pregnant cow.
Awo-ayiwui thotchanli: Seiva kachang akha leilaga apha kapha apamli
vatuda seinao phanung tharanli Hundung khaung phokna. Kaphung kaphali
zatlaga seiva china apam kaphā akha theilaga pamshona; chili seinao
Ancestral lore recounts that the village founders followed a sacred
white cow across the hills. Wherever the cow rested upon the fertile
plateau, there she gave birth to her calf, and upon that blessed ground
the ancient mother-village of Hundung was founded.
pages.tangkhul_content: Awo-ayiwui thotchanli: Seiva kachang akha leilaga apha kapha apamli vatuda seinao phanung tharanli Hundung khaung phokna. Kaphung kaphali zatlaga seiva china apam kaphā akha theilaga pamshona; chili seinao phada awo-ayina 'Hundung' (Hungpung) da hoya.
pages.english_translation: Ancestral lore recounts that the village founders followed a sacred white cow across the hills. Wherever the cow rested upon the fertile plateau, there she gave birth to her calf, and upon that blessed ground the ancient mother-village of Hundung was founded.

lines: CHAPTER 2: THE TWO BROTHERS & MIGRATION TO THE HILLS
Summary: The covenant between elder brother (hills) and younger brother (valley).
Chinaoni khani wui tui: kakhara a kaphungli pamda kakhanao a ngaleili
vaipama. Anili khangaran shiyan leiyi: kakhara na kaphungwui theishak
kala khuira chili ngaleili phungmiya; kakhanao na ngaleiwui machi kala
The legend of the two brothers: the elder brother chose the high
mountain ridges, while the younger brother cultivated the valley plains.
They established a covenant: the elder sent mountain forest produce and
honey to the plain, and the younger returned salt and woven cloth.
pages.tangkhul_content: Chinaoni khani wui tui: kakhara a kaphungli pamda kakhanao a ngaleili vaipama. Anili khangaran shiyan leiyi: kakhara na kaphungwui theishak kala khuira chili ngaleili phungmiya; kakhanao na ngaleiwui machi kala kachon chili kaphungli phungmiya.
pages.english_translation: The legend of the two brothers: the elder brother chose the high mountain ridges, while the younger brother cultivated the valley plains. excerpts.chapter: Chapter 1: Phonological Structure & Lexicographical Conventions
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Lexicographical Format: Headword [Part of Speech] English Definition / Hindi Equivalent. Minimal vowel length contrasts: 'sa' [v] to do / करना vs 'sā' [n] animal, meat / पशु, माँस. 'sha' [v] to hear / सुनना vs 'shā' [num] hundred / सौ. Infinitive prefix ka- precedes verbal roots: ka-sa, ka-thei, ka-shak.
excerpts.translation_en: Conventions: Headwords are alphabetized according to Roman script order. Phonemic vowel length (macron) is strictly distinguished. Trilingual definitions provide immediate cross-linguistic equivalents in English and Hindi.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 2: Nominal Vocabulary: Body Parts, Kinship & Nature
excerpts.tangkhul_text: akui [n] head / सिर | mik [n] eye / आँख | khana [n] ear / कान | khamasung [n] nose / नाक | khamor [n] mouth / मुँह | ha [n] tooth / दाँत | pang [n] hand / हाथ | phei [n] foot / पैर | ava [n] father / पिता | aza [n] mother / माता | zingsho [n] sun / सूर्य | kachang [n] moon / चंद्रमा | tara [n] water / जल | mei [n] fire / अग्नि.
excerpts.translation_en: Nominal lexical inventory covering human anatomy with obligatory prefix a-, kinship relationships, and primary elemental entities of the physical environment.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 3: Verbal Lexicon: Motion, Action & Cognition
excerpts.tangkhul_text: kasa [v] to do / करना | kathei [v] to see / देखना | kashā [v] to hear / सुनना | kazat [v] to walk / चलना | kapam [v] to sit / बैठना | kapi [v] to sleep / सोना | kashak [v] to eat / खाना | kapāng [v] to drink / पीना | kacham [v] to speak / बोलना. Tenses: Present -ei/-i | Past -ser/-da | Future -ra | Imperative -lu.
excerpts.translation_en: Primary verbal roots organized with infinitive prefix ka-. Tense inflection paradigms demonstrated with Subject pronouns (i, na, a).

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 4: Adjectives, Color Terms & Spatial Qualifiers
excerpts.tangkhul_text: kaphā [adj] good / अच्छा | kashi [adj] bad / बुरा | kahak [adj] big / बड़ा | kateo [adj] small / छोटा | kachon [adj] white / सफेद | muk [adj] black / काला | ngaching [adj] green / हरा | khangayei [adj] brave / वीर. Degrees of comparison: kaphā (good), kaphāmei (better), pamei (best).
excerpts.translation_en: Adjectives derived through prefixation of ka- to qualitative verbal roots. Color terminology and morphological degrees of comparison using suffix -mei.
