Time: aja [today] / आज | ngalap [tomorrow] / कल | ningla [yesterday] / बीता कल.
excerpts.translation_en: Base-10 cardinal numeral system and calendar markers for day, night, month, and year.

front_matter.preface: Pa o Kamata Isha mai Jesu Christawui Khararchan: John Kahona Kasa (The Gospel According to St. John in Tangkhul Naga), translated from the original Greek by Rev. William Pettigrew. Published in London by the British and Foreign Bible Society in 1904; printed at the Baptist Mission Press, Calcutta. This landmark volume represents the first printed continuous scripture portion in the Tangkhul Naga language in the Ukhrul dialect.

chapters.title: Kaphung-kachungwui Tui (The Word in the Beginning)
chapters.summary: The prologue to St. John: The Word was with God, life, light, and the testimony of John the Baptist.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Kaphung-kachungwui thotli Tui li-li-sai, kala Tuichi Varivarali lei, kala Tuichi Varivarasai. Chiya kaphung-kachungli Varivarawui kachungli leisai. Ali vangteina ot kathata pamei sakahaisai; Awui chungli haring kasawui maram leisai; kala haring chi miwungwui khanganaso thotsai. Kala Tuichi miwung thot sakahaida i-wui ngachaili pamsai; kala i-thumna Awui mashunkashak theisai.
chapters.english_translation: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. The same was in the beginning with God. All things were made by Him. In Him was life, and the life was the light of men. And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, and we beheld His glory, full of grace and truth.
chapters.grammar_notes: The copula clitic '-sai' signifies remote past narrative, while '-na' marks divine nominative agency.

exercises.question: How did Pettigrew translate 'the Word' (Logos) in Tangkhul?
Explain the semantic adaptation of 'Varivara' for the Supreme Deity.

chapters.title: Cana Ramli Phankahai Thot (The Marriage in Cana)
chapters.summary: The first sign in Cana of Galilee: turning water into wine and the cleansing of the Temple in Jerusalem.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Thot thumana phungli Galilee ramwui Cana shongli phankahai thotli amina pamsai; Jesu kala Awui ngashunbingli chili ho-ngarursai. Jesuna athumli hosa: Tuisin hili tara kaping zang-chihailu. Kala athumna ngathumda kaping zangsai. Phankahai wui pamshim-khararna tara chi khamarao kasada theiphun chitharan, kashak maram mathangsa mana. Kala Varivarawui shimli A se-bing kala tangka kakhalimbingi theida shim katharawui pammali khor-khaleisai.
chapters.english_translation: On the third day there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee. Jesus and His disciples were invited. Jesus said unto them: Fill the waterpots with water. And they filled them to the brim. When the ruler of the feast tasted the water that was made wine, he knew not whence it was. And in the temple He found those that sold oxen and sheep, and drove them out of the holy place.

vocabulary.meaning: governor of the feast, master of ceremonies

chapters.grammar_notes: Prefix 'ka-' with stative stem '-ping' (full) forms the participial modifier 'kaping' (completely full).

exercises.question: Where did the first miracle take place in Tangkhul?
What Tangkhul phrase translates 'filled to the brim'?

chapters.title: Nicodemusli Tui Kaphung (Discourse with Nicodemus)
chapters.summary: Discourse on spiritual rebirth from above, the work of the Spirit, and the love of God for the world.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Phariseebingwui ngachaili Nicodemus kahona mi akhat pamsai, aya Judea miwungwui khararsai. Jesuna ngahanda hosa: Kaphung-kachangli Ina nali hosa, mi akhatna thot katharada mazat-khalakha Varivarawui kazingram theikhami mathailak mana. Kha Varivarana ngalei hiwui miwungli kongashi-kasa thotna, Amani Makaza Mayarwui khali ngashir-khami, chiya Ali kachithek phungmei khikha masiman-lakla, kashak thotwui haring kazang pamsai.
chapters.english_translation: There was a man of the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews. Jesus answered: Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God. For God so loved the world, that He gave His only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in Him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

vocabulary.meaning: new birth, born again, regenerated life
to love tenderly, divine agape love

chapters.grammar_notes: Conditional suffix '-khalakha' (unless / except) governs the subjunctive negative verbal stem 'mazat-'.

exercises.question: Translate John 3:16 from Tangkhul into English.
Identify the theological terms used for 'heaven' and 'everlasting life'.

chapters.title: Samaria Shanawui Tui (The Samaritan Woman at the Well)
chapters.summary: Jesus at Jacob's well in Sychar of Samaria: living water and worshipping God in spirit and truth.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Jesu zattangda Jacobwui tuikhor ngalenli pamsai. Samaria shanawui akhatna tara khaphungli rasai; Jesuna ali hosa: Ili tara mangkhami khalu. Ina khami tara khamang chi thangmatharada khangaraophung mapamlik mana; kha Ina khami tara chi awui chungli kashak thotwui haring kaphanwui tuikhor thot salikha. Varivaraya Mangan thotsai; kala Ali khangamorbingna Mangan kala Kashungli khangamor kashungsa.
chapters.english_translation: Jesus sat thus on the well of Jacob. There cometh a woman of Samaria to draw water: Jesus saith unto her, Give me to drink. Whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life. God is a Spirit: and they that worship Him must worship Him in spirit and in truth.
chapters.grammar_notes: The dual case postposition 'kala' pairs 'Mangan' (Spirit) and 'Kashung' (Truth) as twin coordinates.

exercises.question: Where was the well located according to the text?
What is the requirement for true worshippers stated in John 4:24?

chapters.title: Bethesda Tuikhorli Thotkhamatei (Healing at Bethesda)
chapters.summary: Healing of the infirm man of thirty-eight years at Bethesda on the Sabbath and discourse on divine authority.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Jerusalemli sayat kachung khami gate wui pammali Bethesda kahona tuikhor pamsai. Chili kum thumchitaruk kachang kazat akhatna pamsai; Jesuna ali theida hosa: Nana kaphara phasasholakha? Jesuna ali hosa: Ngakaranglu, nawui khamathali phunglu kala zatlu! Kaphung-kachangli Ina nithumli hosa, Iwui tui kakhangasho kala Ili kasobingli kachithekna kashak thotwui haring leisai, kala thikahaiwui ngachaili haringli kaphan theisai.
chapters.english_translation: Now there is at Jerusalem by the sheep market a pool called Bethesda. A certain man was there, which had an infirmity thirty and eight years. Jesus saith unto him, Wilt thou be made whole? Rise, take up thy bed, and walk! Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and is passed from death unto life.
chapters.grammar_notes: Imperative suffix '-lu' forms strong commands: 'ngakaranglu' (arise!), 'phunglu' (take up!), 'zatlu' (walk!).

exercises.question: For how many years was the man infirm at Bethesda?
What three commands did Jesus give the healed man?

chapters.title: Raruikatha Kachiwui Paothem (The Bread of Life)
chapters.summary: Feeding of the multitudes and declaration: I am the living bread that came down from heaven.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Jesuna athumli hosa: Ina haringwui raruikatha thotsai; Iwui kachungli khara chi thangmatharada kharashok mapamlik mana; kala Ili kachithek chi thangmatharada khangaraophung mapamlik mana. Simon Peterna ngahanda hosa: O Mapao, ithumna khipalishong zatta katha? Nawui kachungli kashak thotwui tui pamsai. Kala ithumna chitheksai kala theisai Nana Varivarawui Kathara chi thotsai.
chapters.english_translation: And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst. Simon Peter answered Him, Lord, to whom shall we go? Thou hast the words of eternal life. And we believe and are sure that thou art that Christ, the Son of the living God.
chapters.grammar_notes: Double negative particle 'mapamlik mana' emphasizes categorical impossibility: shall never ever hunger.

exercises.question: What title did Simon Peter confess in John 6:69?
Explain the metaphor of 'haringwui raruikatha'.

chapters.title: Haring Tara Kong (Rivers of Living Water)
chapters.summary: The proclamation at the Feast of Tabernacles: rivers of living water flowing from within.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Phanitwui thang kashung chili Jesu ngakarangda kaho: Mi akhatna khangaraokhalakha Iwui kachungli rada manglu. Ili kachithekna, tui katharali kakashitheithata, awui malungli haring tara kong shokkasa pamsai. Kha Aya Manganwui maram hosa, chiya Ali kachithekna khapan kashung thotsai.
chapters.english_translation: In the last day, that great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink. He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water. But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him should receive.

vocabulary.meaning: flowing forth, welling up from within
unto, toward, into the presence of

chapters.grammar_notes: The compound noun 'tara kong' combines 'tara' (water) and 'kong' (river/stream) denoting an abundant torrent.

exercises.question: What promise is given to believers in John 7:38?
What does 'malung' symbolize in Tangkhul psychology?

pages.title: Chapter 3: Nicodemusli Tui Kaphung (Discourse with Nicodemus)
lines: CHAPTER 3: NICODEMUSLI TUI KAPHUNG (DISCOURSE WITH NICODEMUS)
Summary: Discourse on spiritual rebirth from above, the work of the Spirit, and the love of God for the world.

kasa thotna, Amani Makaza Mayarwui khali ngashir-khami, chiya Ali
kachithek phungmei khikha masiman-lakla, kashak thotwui haring kazang

should not perish, but have everlasting life.

pages.header: Chapter 4: Samaria Shanawui Tui (The Samaritan Woman at the Well) (Page 13)
pages.title: Chapter 4: Samaria Shanawui Tui (The Samaritan Woman at the Well)
lines: CHAPTER 4: SAMARIA SHANAWUI TUI (THE SAMARITAN WOMAN AT THE WELL)
Summary: Jesus at Jacob's well in Sychar of Samaria: living water and worshipping God in spirit and truth.
Jesu zattangda Jacobwui tuikhor ngalenli pamsai. Samaria shanawui
akhatna tara khaphungli rasai; Jesuna ali hosa: Ili tara mangkhami
khalu. Ina khami tara khamang chi thangmatharada khangaraophung mapamlik
mana; kha Ina khami tara chi awui chungli kashak thotwui haring
kaphanwui tuikhor thot salikha. Varivaraya Mangan thotsai; kala Ali
khangamorbingna Mangan kala Kashungli khangamor kashungsa.
Jesus sat thus on the well of Jacob. There cometh a woman of Samaria to
draw water: Jesus saith unto her, Give me to drink. Whosoever drinketh
of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water
that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into
everlasting life. God is a Spirit: and they that worship Him must
worship Him in spirit and in truth.

lines: CHAPTER 5: BETHESDA TUIKHORLI THOTKHAMATEI (HEALING AT BETHESDA)

pamsai. Chili kum thumchitaruk kachang kazat akhatna pamsai; Jesuna ali
theida hosa: Nana kaphara phasasholakha? Jesuna ali hosa: Ngakaranglu,
nawui khamathali phunglu kala zatlu! Kaphung-kachangli Ina nithumli
hosa, Iwui tui kakhangasho kala Ili kasobingli kachithekna kashak

certain man was there, which had an infirmity thirty and eight years.
Jesus saith unto him, Wilt thou be made whole? Rise, take up thy bed,
and walk! Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that heareth my word, and
believeth on him that sent me, hath everlasting life, and is passed from
pages.tangkhul_content: Jerusalemli sayat kachung khami gate wui pammali Bethesda kahona tuikhor pamsai. pages.title: Chapter 6: Raruikatha Kachiwui Paothem (The Bread of Life)
lines: CHAPTER 6: RARUIKATHA KACHIWUI PAOTHEM (THE BREAD OF LIFE)
Summary: Feeding of the multitudes and declaration: I am the living bread that came down from heaven.
Jesuna athumli hosa: Ina haringwui raruikatha thotsai; Iwui kachungli
khara chi thangmatharada kharashok mapamlik mana; kala Ili kachithek chi
thangmatharada khangaraophung mapamlik mana. Simon Peterna ngahanda
hosa: O Mapao, ithumna khipalishong zatta katha? Nawui kachungli kashak
thotwui tui pamsai. Kala ithumna chitheksai kala theisai Nana
And Jesus said unto them, I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me
shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst.
Simon Peter answered Him, Lord, to whom shall we go? Thou hast the words
of eternal life. And we believe and are sure that thou art that Christ,
the Son of the living God.

pages.title: Chapter 7: Haring Tara Kong (Rivers of Living Water)
lines: CHAPTER 7: HARING TARA KONG (RIVERS OF LIVING WATER)
Summary: The proclamation at the Feast of Tabernacles: rivers of living water flowing from within.

khangaraokhalakha Iwui kachungli rada manglu. Ili kachithekna, tui
katharali kakashitheithata, awui malungli haring tara kong shokkasa
pamsai. Kha Aya Manganwui maram hosa, chiya Ali kachithekna khapan

saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink. He that
believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow
rivers of living water. But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that
pages.tangkhul_content: Phanitwui thang kashung chili Jesu ngakarangda kaho: Mi akhatna khangaraokhalakha Iwui kachungli rada manglu. Ili kachithekna, tui katharali kakashitheithata, awui malungli haring tara kong shokkasa pamsai. Kha Aya Manganwui maram hosa, chiya Ali kachithekna khapan kashung thotsai.
pages.english_translation: In the last day, that great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink. He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water. But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him should receive.

Ili kachithekna, tui katharali kakashitheithata, awui malungli haring tara kong shokkasa pamsai. Kha Aya Manganwui maram hosa, chiya Ali kachithekna khapan kashung thotsai.
excerpts.translation_en: In the last day, that great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried, saying, If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink. He that believeth on me, as the scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water. But this spake he of the Spirit, which they that believe on him should receive.

chapters.title: Theophilusli Kakhayao kala Marywui La (Preface and Magnificat)
chapters.summary: Dedication to Theophilus, the annunciation by Gabriel to Zacharias and Mary, and Mary's song of praise.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Theophilus mathilakha, Ina maram kachiva kaphung-kachungli theikasomda nawui vang kaphika mathaikha theisai. Kachisona hosa: Zacharias, macharanlu; nawui khangamor chi khanashosai, kala nawui shanao Elisabethna mayar akhat zatlikha. Maryna hosa: Iwui malungna Mapaoli mathan-kashei salikha, kala iwui manganna iwui Haring Kashei Varivarali kaphung phungsai. Pangmashan phungna iwui vang ot kaphung kasada, Awui min Katharasai.
chapters.english_translation: It seemed good to me also, most excellent Theophilus, to write unto thee in order. The angel said: Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son. And Mary said, My soul doth magnify the Lord, and my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. For he that is mighty hath done to me great things; and holy is his name.

vocabulary.meaning: He that is mighty, the Almighty One

chapters.grammar_notes: The negative imperative prefix 'ma-' combined with verbal stem '-charan' forms 'macharanlu' (do not fear).

exercises.question: To whom did Luke address his Gospel in Tangkhul?
Translate Mary's opening verse of the Magnificat into English.

chapters.title: Jesuwui Phankahai Bethlehem Shongli (The Nativity)
chapters.summary: The decree of Caesar Augustus, the birth in Bethlehem, and the angelic message to the shepherds.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Zingkum chiwui thotli Caesar Augustus-wui tuingashit kaphung ngalei pamkhapeida min khangashan shoksai. Josephna Davidwui shim kala kachung thotsada Galilee ram Nazarethwui Judea ram Bethlehem shongli zangsai. Chili pammali shit kashikbingna thot khangaso ngasophun sayatli ngayon-kasa pamsai. Kachisona hosa: Macharanlu; Ina nithumli miwung kachivawui kaphung kachang pao kaphung phungsai! Tangkham chili Davidwui ramli Haring Kashei Christa Mapao phankahaisai.
chapters.english_translation: And it came to pass in those days, that there went out a decree from Caesar Augustus that all the world should be taxed. And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judaea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem. And there were in the same country shepherds abiding in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night. And the angel said: Unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.
chapters.grammar_notes: Temporal adverbial clause 'Zingkum chiwui thotli' marks historical framing (in those days).

exercises.question: What Roman ruler issued the census decree?
How did the angels address the shepherds in Tangkhul?

chapters.title: Jordan Kongli Baptisma (Baptism at Jordan)
chapters.summary: John the Baptist's preaching of repentance in the wilderness and the baptism of Jesus at the river Jordan.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Johnna Jordan kongwui pammali rada kasha-kashan kazangwui baptisma khangayei pao phungsai. Johnna ngahanda hosa: Ina tarana baptisma khayao thotsai; kha Iwui saphunga pangmashan phung akhat raranglikha; Aya Mangan Kathara kala meina baptisma salikha. Mi kachivana baptisma khayaoli Jesu-kha baptisma sayaosai; kala A khangamorli kazing phangshoksai, kala kazingwui tui shoksai: Nana Iwui Mayar Kongashi thotsai.
chapters.english_translation: John came into all the country about Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins. John answered, saying unto them all, I indeed baptize you with water; but one mightier than I cometh: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost and with fire. Now when all the people were baptized, it came to pass, that Jesus also being baptized, and praying, the heaven was opened, and a voice came from heaven, which said, Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased.

vocabulary.meaning: to baptize with water, ritual immersion
fire, flame of judgment and purification

chapters.grammar_notes: Instrumental postposition '-na' appears in 'tarana' (with water) and 'meina' (with fire).

exercises.question: What two elements of baptism did John contrast?
What words were spoken from heaven at Jesus' baptism?

chapters.title: Nazarethli Kashung Ot (The Ministry in Nazareth)
chapters.summary: The reading of the Isaiah scroll in the synagogue at Nazareth and preaching deliverance to the captives.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Kala A Nazareth shongli zangsai, chili A kashung pamsai; Sabbath thangli synagogue shimli zangda tui kaphika phashoksai: Mapaowui Mangan Iwui kachungli leisai, maramchilu Aya ningzanbingli pao kaphung kaphan chitheikahai thotsai; A Ili kachiso kazatbingli thotkhamatei kala khararkashanbingli haring khami vangna. Kala A Capernaum shongli zangsai, kala Sabbath thangli athumli tuitam chitheisai; Awui tui pangmashan phungsai.
chapters.english_translation: And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up: and, as his custom was, he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up for to read. The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives. And he came down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and taught them on the sabbath days. And they were astonished at his doctrine: for his word was with power.

vocabulary.meaning: house of prayer, Jewish meeting hall
the poor, the humble and afflicted

chapters.grammar_notes: Postposition '-wui vangna' denotes teleological purpose: 'haring khami vangna' (for the purpose of granting life).

exercises.question: What passage of scripture did Jesus read in Nazareth?
Identify the four groups blessed in the Nazareth manifesto.

chapters.title: Samaria Miwung Phakazang (The Good Samaritan)
chapters.summary: The parable of the man who fell among thieves on the Jericho road and the compassionate Samaritan stranger.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Jesuna hosa: Mi akhat Jerusalem shongwui Jericho shongli vangasai; kala aya rari-kapangbingwui pangli kaphan theisai. Athumna awui kachon khangashan kala thotkhamatei kasada ali marikha-thida vangasai. Pung-kashang akhat shongfa chili vangasai; aya theida shong kacheili vangasai. Kha Samaria mi akhatna zatli aya ali rasai; kala aya ali theida ning-kongashi phungsai. Aya rada awui khazatli thao kala khamarao teikahai, kala pangkaso phungda hotel shimli phung-zangsai. Hiwui thum chili khipana rari-kapangbingwui pangli kaphanchiwui ngacham-mi thotsa naningkha? Aya hosa: Ali kongashi kachithei chi. Jesuna hosa: Zattu, nankha chithata salu!
chapters.english_translation: A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him, and departed, leaving him half dead. And by chance there came down a certain priest that way: and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side. But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was: and when he saw him, he had compassion on him, and went to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him. Which now of these three was neighbour unto him? He that shewed mercy on him. Then said Jesus unto him, Go, and do thou likewise.
chapters.grammar_notes: The compound idiomatic phrase 'ning-kongashi' signifies visceral heart compassion (malungwui kongashi).

exercises.question: What two travelers passed by the wounded man before the Samaritan?
How did Jesus define 'ngacham-mi' (neighbour) in this parable?

chapters.title: Mayar Kashingashimanwui Wari (The Prodigal Son)
chapters.summary: The parable of the lost younger son, his journey to a far country, repentance, and the father's joyous feast.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Kala A hosa: Mi akhatli mayar khikakhana leisai. Ngachonchi avana hosa: Ava, nawui lungli iwui share phunkami khalu. Thang khakhanali ngachonchi kachiva phungda ram kachang akhatli vangasai, chili aya awui kashak kachiva shiman-hailsai. Aya ning khangasholi hosa: Iwui ava-wui shimli ot-kashabing kachiva raruikatha kaping leisai, kha ina hili ngaraoda thilikha! Ina ngakarangda iwui ava shongli zanglikha kala ali holikha: Ava, ina kazingram kala nawui phungli kakhama sakahaisai. Kha aya kachangli leisalilha avana theida ning-kongashi phungda katda chikhurli phumsai.
chapters.english_translation: A certain man had two sons. And the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me. And he divided unto them his living. And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living. And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger! I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee. And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

vocabulary.meaning: two sons, pair of male siblings
embraced upon the neck, kissed warmly

chapters.grammar_notes: Temporal correlative 'leisalilha' (while still being far off) expresses anticipatory parental vigil.

exercises.question: What request did the younger son make of his father?
What phrase translates 'when he came to himself' in Tangkhul?

chapters.title: Emmaus Shongwui Zatkatha (The Road to Emmaus)
chapters.summary: The risen Christ walking unrecognized with two disciples on the Emmaus road and revealing Himself in the breaking of bread.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Thang chili athum ngachaiwui khani Jerusalem shongwui Emmaus kahona ramli zattangsai. Kala athumna hiwui maram kachiva ngatei-tui kasai. Athum tui ngateili Jesu amana athumli phakazangda ngasoda vangasai. Kala A athum ngasoda pamsai; A raruikatha phungda mathankashakda kashai chitharan athum theiphunsai! Kala athumna hosa: Shongfali A ithumli tui hoda scripture chitheikahai thotli ithumwui malung mei katha kazang masasakha?
chapters.english_translation: And, behold, two of them went that same day to a village called Emmaus, which was from Jerusalem about threescore furlongs. And they talked together of all these things which had happened. And it came to pass, that, while they communed together and reasoned, Jesus himself drew near, and went with them. And it came to pass, as he sat at meat with them, he took bread, and blessed it, and brake, and gave to them. And their eyes were opened, and they knew him. And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?

vocabulary.meaning: to discuss, converse mutually on deep matters
burning like fire, inflamed with conviction

chapters.grammar_notes: The rhetorical interrogative suffix '-sakha' poses the reflective question: 'masasakha?' (did it not burn?).

exercises.question: At what exact moment did the disciples recognize Jesus at Emmaus?
How did the disciples describe their hearts burning within them?

pages.title: Chapter 3: Jordan Kongli Baptisma (Baptism at Jordan)
lines: CHAPTER 3: JORDAN KONGLI BAPTISMA (BAPTISM AT JORDAN)
Summary: John the Baptist's preaching of repentance in the wilderness and the baptism of Jesus at the river Jordan.
Johnna Jordan kongwui pammali rada kasha-kashan kazangwui baptisma
khangayei pao phungsai. Johnna ngahanda hosa: Ina tarana baptisma khayao
thotsai; kha Iwui saphunga pangmashan phung akhat raranglikha; Aya
Mangan Kathara kala meina baptisma salikha. Mi kachivana baptisma
khayaoli Jesu-kha baptisma sayaosai; kala A khangamorli kazing
phangshoksai, kala kazingwui tui shoksai: Nana Iwui Mayar Kongashi
John came into all the country about Jordan, preaching the baptism of
repentance for the remission of sins. John answered, saying unto them
all, I indeed baptize you with water; but one mightier than I cometh: he
shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost and with fire. Now when all the
people were baptized, it came to pass, that Jesus also being baptized,
and praying, the heaven was opened, and a voice came from heaven, which
said, Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased.
pages.tangkhul_content: Johnna Jordan kongwui pammali rada kasha-kashan kazangwui baptisma khangayei pao phungsai. Johnna ngahanda hosa: Ina tarana baptisma khayao thotsai; kha Iwui saphunga pangmashan phung akhat raranglikha; Aya Mangan Kathara kala meina baptisma salikha. Mi kachivana baptisma khayaoli Jesu-kha baptisma sayaosai; kala A khangamorli kazing phangshoksai, kala kazingwui tui shoksai: Nana Iwui Mayar Kongashi thotsai.
pages.english_translation: John came into all the country about Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins. John answered, saying unto them all, I indeed baptize you with water; but one mightier than I cometh: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost and with fire. Now when all the people were baptized, it came to pass, that Jesus also being baptized, and praying, the heaven was opened, and a voice came from heaven, which said, Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased.

pages.header: Chapter 4: Nazarethli Kashung Ot (The Ministry in Nazareth) (Page 12)
pages.title: Chapter 4: Nazarethli Kashung Ot (The Ministry in Nazareth)
lines: CHAPTER 4: NAZARETHLI KASHUNG OT (THE MINISTRY IN NAZARETH)
Summary: The reading of the Isaiah scroll in the synagogue at Nazareth and preaching deliverance to the captives.
Kala A Nazareth shongli zangsai, chili A kashung pamsai; Sabbath thangli
synagogue shimli zangda tui kaphika phashoksai: Mapaowui Mangan Iwui
kachungli leisai, maramchilu Aya ningzanbingli pao kaphung kaphan
chitheikahai thotsai; A Ili kachiso kazatbingli thotkhamatei kala
khararkashanbingli haring khami vangna. Kala A Capernaum shongli
zangsai, kala Sabbath thangli athumli tuitam chitheisai; Awui tui
And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up: and, as his
custom was, he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up
for to read. The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed
me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the
brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives. And he came down
to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and taught them on the sabbath days.
And they were astonished at his doctrine: for his word was with power.
pages.tangkhul_content: Kala A Nazareth shongli zangsai, chili A kashung pamsai; Sabbath thangli synagogue shimli zangda tui kaphika phashoksai: Mapaowui Mangan Iwui kachungli leisai, maramchilu Aya ningzanbingli pao kaphung kaphan chitheikahai thotsai; A Ili kachiso kazatbingli thotkhamatei kala khararkashanbingli haring khami vangna. Kala A Capernaum shongli zangsai, kala Sabbath thangli athumli tuitam chitheisai; Awui tui pangmashan phungsai.
pages.english_translation: And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up: and, as his custom was, he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up for to read. The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives. And he came down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and taught them on the sabbath days. And they were astonished at his doctrine: for his word was with power.

pages.header: Chapter 5: Samaria Miwung Phakazang (The Good Samaritan) (Page 14)
pages.title: Chapter 5: Samaria Miwung Phakazang (The Good Samaritan)
lines: CHAPTER 5: SAMARIA MIWUNG PHAKAZANG (THE GOOD SAMARITAN)
Summary: The parable of the man who fell among thieves on the Jericho road and the compassionate Samaritan stranger.
Jesuna hosa: Mi akhat Jerusalem shongwui Jericho shongli vangasai; kala
aya rari-kapangbingwui pangli kaphan theisai. Athumna awui kachon
khangashan kala thotkhamatei kasada ali marikha-thida vangasai. Pung-
kashang akhat shongfa chili vangasai; aya theida shong kacheili
vangasai. Kha Samaria mi akhatna zatli aya ali rasai; kala aya ali
theida ning-kongashi phungsai. Aya rada awui khazatli thao kala khamarao
teikahai, kala pangkaso phungda hotel shimli phung-zangsai. Hiwui thum
chili khipana rari-kapangbingwui pangli kaphanchiwui ngacham-mi thotsa
naningkha? Aya hosa: Ali kongashi kachithei chi. Jesuna hosa: Zattu,
A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among
thieves, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him, and
departed, leaving him half dead. And by chance there came down a certain
priest that way: and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.
But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was: and when he
saw him, he had compassion on him, and went to him, and bound up his
wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and brought him to an inn, and took
care of him. Which now of these three was neighbour unto him? He that
shewed mercy on him. Then said Jesus unto him, Go, and do thou likewise.
pages.tangkhul_content: Jesuna hosa: Mi akhat Jerusalem shongwui Jericho shongli vangasai; kala aya rari-kapangbingwui pangli kaphan theisai. pages.header: Chapter 6: Mayar Kashingashimanwui Wari (The Prodigal Son) (Page 17)
pages.title: Chapter 6: Mayar Kashingashimanwui Wari (The Prodigal Son)
lines: CHAPTER 6: MAYAR KASHINGASHIMANWUI WARI (THE PRODIGAL SON)
Summary: The parable of the lost younger son, his journey to a far country, repentance, and the father's joyous feast.
Kala A hosa: Mi akhatli mayar khikakhana leisai. Ngachonchi avana hosa:
Ava, nawui lungli iwui share phunkami khalu. Thang khakhanali ngachonchi
kachiva phungda ram kachang akhatli vangasai, chili aya awui kashak
kachiva shiman-hailsai. Aya ning khangasholi hosa: Iwui ava-wui shimli
ot-kashabing kachiva raruikatha kaping leisai, kha ina hili ngaraoda
thilikha! Ina ngakarangda iwui ava shongli zanglikha kala ali holikha:
Ava, ina kazingram kala nawui phungli kakhama sakahaisai. Kha aya
kachangli leisalilha avana theida ning-kongashi phungda katda chikhurli
A certain man had two sons. And the younger of them said to his father,
Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me. And he divided
unto them his living. And not many days after the younger son gathered
all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted
his substance with riotous living. And when he came to himself, he said,
How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare,
and I perish with hunger! I will arise and go to my father, and will say
unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee. And he
arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his
father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and
pages.tangkhul_content: Kala A hosa: Mi akhatli mayar khikakhana leisai. Ngachonchi avana hosa: Ava, nawui lungli iwui share phunkami khalu. Aya ning khangasholi hosa: Iwui ava-wui shimli ot-kashabing kachiva raruikatha kaping leisai, kha ina hili ngaraoda thilikha! Kha aya kachangli leisalilha avana theida ning-kongashi phungda katda chikhurli phumsai.
pages.english_translation: A certain man had two sons. And the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me. And he divided unto them his living. And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living. And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger! I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee. And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

pages.header: Chapter 7: Emmaus Shongwui Zatkatha (The Road to Emmaus) (Page 19)
pages.title: Chapter 7: Emmaus Shongwui Zatkatha (The Road to Emmaus)
lines: CHAPTER 7: EMMAUS SHONGWUI ZATKATHA (THE ROAD TO EMMAUS)
Summary: The risen Christ walking unrecognized with two disciples on the Emmaus road and revealing Himself in the breaking of bread.
Thang chili athum ngachaiwui khani Jerusalem shongwui Emmaus kahona
ramli zattangsai. Kala athumna hiwui maram kachiva ngatei-tui kasai.
Athum tui ngateili Jesu amana athumli phakazangda ngasoda vangasai. Kala
A athum ngasoda pamsai; A raruikatha phungda mathankashakda kashai
chitharan athum theiphunsai! Kala athumna hosa: Shongfali A ithumli tui
hoda scripture chitheikahai thotli ithumwui malung mei katha kazang
And, behold, two of them went that same day to a village called Emmaus,
which was from Jerusalem about threescore furlongs. And they talked
together of all these things which had happened. And it came to pass,
that, while they communed together and reasoned, Jesus himself drew
near, and went with them. And it came to pass, as he sat at meat with
them, he took bread, and blessed it, and brake, and gave to them. And
their eyes were opened, and they knew him. And they said one to another,
Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way,
and while he opened to us the scriptures?
pages.tangkhul_content: Thang chili athum ngachaiwui khani Jerusalem shongwui Emmaus kahona ramli zattangsai. Kala athumna hiwui maram kachiva ngatei-tui kasai. Athum tui ngateili Jesu amana athumli phakazangda ngasoda vangasai. Kala A athum ngasoda pamsai; A raruikatha phungda mathankashakda kashai chitharan athum theiphunsai! Kala athumna hosa: Shongfali A ithumli tui hoda scripture chitheikahai thotli ithumwui malung mei katha kazang masasakha?
pages.english_translation: And, behold, two of them went that same day to a village called Emmaus, which was from Jerusalem about threescore furlongs. And they talked together of all these things which had happened. And it came to pass, that, while they communed together and reasoned, Jesus himself drew near, and went with them. And it came to pass, as he sat at meat with them, he took bread, and blessed it, and brake, and gave to them. And their eyes were opened, and they knew him. And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 1: Theophilusli Kakhayao kala Marywui La (Preface and Magnificat)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Theophilus mathilakha, Ina maram kachiva kaphung-kachungli theikasomda nawui vang kaphika mathaikha theisai. Kachisona hosa: Zacharias, macharanlu; nawui khangamor chi khanashosai, kala nawui shanao Elisabethna mayar akhat zatlikha. Maryna hosa: Iwui malungna Mapaoli mathan-kashei salikha, kala iwui manganna iwui Haring Kashei Varivarali kaphung phungsai. Pangmashan phungna iwui vang ot kaphung kasada, Awui min Katharasai.
excerpts.translation_en: It seemed good to me also, most excellent Theophilus, to write unto thee in order. The angel said: Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son. And Mary said, My soul doth magnify the Lord, and my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. For he that is mighty hath done to me great things; and holy is his name.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 2: Jesuwui Phankahai Bethlehem Shongli (The Nativity)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Zingkum chiwui thotli Caesar Augustus-wui tuingashit kaphung ngalei pamkhapeida min khangashan shoksai. Josephna Davidwui shim kala kachung thotsada Galilee ram Nazarethwui Judea ram Bethlehem shongli zangsai. Chili pammali shit kashikbingna thot khangaso ngasophun sayatli ngayon-kasa pamsai. Kachisona hosa: Macharanlu; Ina nithumli miwung kachivawui kaphung kachang pao kaphung phungsai! Tangkham chili Davidwui ramli Haring Kashei Christa Mapao phankahaisai.
excerpts.translation_en: And it came to pass in those days, that there went out a decree from Caesar Augustus that all the world should be taxed. And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judaea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem. And there were in the same country shepherds abiding in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night. And the angel said: Unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 3: Jordan Kongli Baptisma (Baptism at Jordan)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Johnna Jordan kongwui pammali rada kasha-kashan kazangwui baptisma khangayei pao phungsai. Johnna ngahanda hosa: Ina tarana baptisma khayao thotsai; kha Iwui saphunga pangmashan phung akhat raranglikha; Aya Mangan Kathara kala meina baptisma salikha. Mi kachivana baptisma khayaoli Jesu-kha baptisma sayaosai; kala A khangamorli kazing phangshoksai, kala kazingwui tui shoksai: Nana Iwui Mayar Kongashi thotsai.
excerpts.translation_en: John came into all the country about Jordan, preaching the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins. John answered, saying unto them all, I indeed baptize you with water; but one mightier than I cometh: he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost and with fire. Now when all the people were baptized, it came to pass, that Jesus also being baptized, and praying, the heaven was opened, and a voice came from heaven, which said, Thou art my beloved Son; in thee I am well pleased.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 4: Nazarethli Kashung Ot (The Ministry in Nazareth)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Kala A Nazareth shongli zangsai, chili A kashung pamsai; Sabbath thangli synagogue shimli zangda tui kaphika phashoksai: Mapaowui Mangan Iwui kachungli leisai, maramchilu Aya ningzanbingli pao kaphung kaphan chitheikahai thotsai; A Ili kachiso kazatbingli thotkhamatei kala khararkashanbingli haring khami vangna. Kala A Capernaum shongli zangsai, kala Sabbath thangli athumli tuitam chitheisai; Awui tui pangmashan phungsai.
excerpts.translation_en: And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up: and, as his custom was, he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up for to read. The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives. And he came down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and taught them on the sabbath days. And they were astonished at his doctrine: for his word was with power.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 5: Samaria Miwung Phakazang (The Good Samaritan)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Jesuna hosa: Mi akhat Jerusalem shongwui Jericho shongli vangasai; kala aya rari-kapangbingwui pangli kaphan theisai. Athumna awui kachon khangashan kala thotkhamatei kasada ali marikha-thida vangasai. Pung-kashang akhat shongfa chili vangasai; aya theida shong kacheili vangasai. Kha Samaria mi akhatna zatli aya ali rasai; kala aya ali theida ning-kongashi phungsai. Aya rada awui khazatli thao kala khamarao teikahai, kala pangkaso phungda hotel shimli phung-zangsai. Hiwui thum chili khipana rari-kapangbingwui pangli kaphanchiwui ngacham-mi thotsa naningkha? Aya hosa: Ali kongashi kachithei chi. Jesuna hosa: Zattu, nankha chithata salu!
excerpts.translation_en: A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him, and departed, leaving him half dead. And by chance there came down a certain priest that way: and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side. But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was: and when he saw him, he had compassion on him, and went to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him. Which now of these three was neighbour unto him? He that shewed mercy on him. Then said Jesus unto him, Go, and do thou likewise.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 6: Mayar Kashingashimanwui Wari (The Prodigal Son)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Kala A hosa: Mi akhatli mayar khikakhana leisai. Ngachonchi avana hosa: Ava, nawui lungli iwui share phunkami khalu. Thang khakhanali ngachonchi kachiva phungda ram kachang akhatli vangasai, chili aya awui kashak kachiva shiman-hailsai. Aya ning khangasholi hosa: Iwui ava-wui shimli ot-kashabing kachiva raruikatha kaping leisai, kha ina hili ngaraoda thilikha! Ina ngakarangda iwui ava shongli zanglikha kala ali holikha: Ava, ina kazingram kala nawui phungli kakhama sakahaisai. Kha aya kachangli leisalilha avana theida ning-kongashi phungda katda chikhurli phumsai.
excerpts.translation_en: A certain man had two sons. And the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me. And he divided unto them his living. And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living. And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father's have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger! I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee. And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

excerpts.chapter: Chapter 7: Emmaus Shongwui Zatkatha (The Road to Emmaus)
excerpts.tangkhul_text: Thang chili athum ngachaiwui khani Jerusalem shongwui Emmaus kahona ramli zattangsai. Kala athumna hiwui maram kachiva ngatei-tui kasai. Athum tui ngateili Jesu amana athumli phakazangda ngasoda vangasai. Kala A athum ngasoda pamsai; A raruikatha phungda mathankashakda kashai chitharan athum theiphunsai! Kala athumna hosa: Shongfali A ithumli tui hoda scripture chitheikahai thotli ithumwui malung mei katha kazang masasakha?
excerpts.translation_en: And, behold, two of them went that same day to a village called Emmaus, which was from Jerusalem about threescore furlongs. And they talked together of all these things which had happened. And it came to pass, that, while they communed together and reasoned, Jesus himself drew near, and went with them. And it came to pass, as he sat at meat with them, he took bread, and blessed it, and brake, and gave to them. And their eyes were opened, and they knew him. And they said one to another, Did not our heart burn within us, while he talked with us by the way, and while he opened to us the scriptures?

front_matter.preface: Pa o Kachatbingna Kasa wui Khararchan: The Acts of the Apostles in Tangkhul Naga, translated by Rev. William Pettigrew. Published in London by the British and Foreign Bible Society, 1905; printed at the Baptist Mission Press, Calcutta. Details the day of Pentecost, Peter's defense before the Sanhedrin, Stephen's martyrdom, and Paul's speech at the Areopagus in Athens.

chapters.title: Kazingli Kaphan kala Kachatbing (Ascension and Commission)
chapters.summary: The ascension of Christ from the Mount of Olives and the gathering of the apostles in Jerusalem.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Theophilus-li kaphung kakhanin: Jesu-na khararchanli ot kasawui maram kaphung-kachungli kaphika thotsai. Awui thikahaiwui saphunga A haringkasa theichithei kachiva thotna athumli thang taracham kachithei Varivarawui kazingramwui tui hosa. Mangan Kathara nithumwui kachungli raranglikha nithum pangmashan phunglikha; kala Jerusalemli, Judea kala Samaria ram kachivali, kala ngalei pammai kashung kachivali Iwui sakhibing salikha. Athumna theishak phashokda Matthiasli rasai, kala aya kachatbing tarakhatli ngasohailsai.
chapters.english_translation: The former treatise have I made, O Theophilus, of all that Jesus began both to do and teach. To whom also he shewed himself alive after his passion by many infallible proofs, being seen of them forty days. But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth. And they gave forth their lots; and the lot fell upon Matthias; and he was numbered with the eleven apostles.
chapters.grammar_notes: Tangkhul uses the indigenous legal term 'sakhibing' (witnesses) for those testifying under solemn oath.

exercises.question: How long was Jesus seen by the apostles after His passion?
Who was chosen to take the place of Judas among the twelve?

chapters.title: Pentecost Thangli Mangan Kathara (Day of Pentecost)
chapters.summary: The descent of the Holy Spirit like rushing wind and tongues of fire, and Peter's first sermon.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Pentecost kumshang phungphatli nithum pam akhangli zikahai pamsai. Kazingwui huchiphung majung katha khara rasai, kala athum pamsahai shim kachivali kapingsai. Kala meiwui malei katha khangayeida athum kachivawui kachungli rasai. Kala athum kachiva Mangan Katharana kapingda ngatei tui khangayei hosa! Peterna ngakarangda hosa: Israel miwung, tui hi ngashonlu: Nazarethwui Jesu hili Varivarana thikahaiwui ngachaili thingkashangsai; chiwui maramli ithum kachiva sakhibing thotsai. Ningzan ngashunlu, kala nithum kachiva Jesu Christawui minli baptisma sayanlu!
chapters.english_translation: And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place. And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting. And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them. And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues. Then Peter stood up and said, Ye men of Israel, hear these words; This Jesus hath God raised up, whereof we all are witnesses. Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ.

vocabulary.meaning: to repent, rectify the mind and heart

chapters.grammar_notes: The verbal phrase 'ningzan ngashunlu' fuses 'ningzan' (heart-contrition) with 'ngashun' (to make straight).

exercises.question: Describe the signs that accompanied the descent of the Holy Spirit at Pentecost.
What did Peter urge the crowd to do at the conclusion of his sermon?

chapters.title: Temple Gate wui Pamli Thotkhamatei (Lame Man at the Beautiful Gate)
chapters.summary: Healing of the lame man by Peter and John at the Beautiful Gate of the Temple.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Peter kala John thangkhamir pung chiko khangamor thangli Templeli zangvangasai. Phaphuk khazat akhat, awui phankahaiwui thotli theisai, aya Templewui Mathan Gate kahowali pamsai; aya Peter kala Johnli theida seisan khamor khanasai. Peterna hosa: Rupa kala sona iwui chungli mathai mana; kha ina phungli nali khamlikha: Nazarethwui Jesu Christawui minli ngakarangda zatlu! Kala ayana awui pangkasho pangda thingkasangsai; chitharan awui phakhur kala pharu pangmashan phungsai! Aya ngachor-da ngakarangsai kala zat-zangsai, Templeli zangda khangachor kala Varivarali mathankashei sasai.
chapters.english_translation: Now Peter and John went up together into the temple at the hour of prayer, being the ninth hour. And a certain man lame from his mother's womb was carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the temple which is called Beautiful, to ask alms of them that entered into the temple. Then Peter said, Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk. And he took him by the right hand, and lifted him up: and immediately his feet and ankle bones received strength. And he leaping up stood, and walked, and entered with them into the temple, walking, and leaping, and praising God.

vocabulary.meaning: lame from birth, crippled in the feet

chapters.grammar_notes: The paired coordinate 'rupa kala sona' uses standard Loan-Assamese roots fully naturalized in colonial Tangkhul.

exercises.question: At what hour did Peter and John go up to the Temple?
What memorable response did Peter give when asked for alms?

chapters.title: Councilwui Phungli Sakhi Chitheikahai (Before the Sanhedrin)
chapters.summary: Peter and John arrested and questioned before the rulers, elders, and scribes of the Council.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Athumna Peter kala Johnli ngachaili pamsahai hosa: Khipawui pangmashan kala minli nithumna hi sakha? Peterna Mangan Katharana kapingda hosa: Miwungwui khararbing kala Israelwui Hangvabing, ngatei khipawui chunglikha haring kaphan mathailak mana; maramchilu kazing kaphungli miwungli khami ngatei min khikha mathai mana! Kha athumna Peter kala Johnna ngahanda hosa: Nithumwui tui ngashon-katha Varivarawui tui ngashon-katha khipana mashungkha nithum shanshilu! Maramchilu ithumna theikahai kala ngashokahai tui masasa pamtang mathailak mana.
chapters.english_translation: And when they had set them in the midst, they asked, By what power, or by what name, have ye done this? Then Peter, filled with the Holy Ghost, said unto them, Ye rulers of the people, and elders of Israel, Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved. But Peter and John answered and said unto them, Whether it be right in the sight of God to hearken unto you more than unto God, judge ye. For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard.

vocabulary.meaning: council of elders, senators, Sanhedrin magistrates
under heaven, beneath the celestial dome
to hearken, obey, submit to authority

chapters.grammar_notes: Pettigrew uses the indigenous administrative title 'Hangvabing' (village elder bench) for the Sanhedrin rulers.

exercises.question: How did Peter respond to the council's prohibition against preaching?
Explain the cultural borrowing of 'Hangva' in early Tangkhul scriptural translation.

chapters.title: Stephenwui Pao kala Kashung Thot (The Martyrdom of Stephen)
chapters.summary: Stephen's defense before the council, vision of the Son of Man, and stoning as the first Christian martyr.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Stephenna ning-kachang kala pangmashan phungda miwungwui ngachaili theichithei kaphung sasai. Council shimli pambing kachivana ali theida awui mai kazingram kachisowui mai katha theisai. Kha aya Mangan Katharana kapingda kazingli theida Varivarawui mathankashak theisai. Kala athumna lungna chidatli Stephenna khon-kaphung: O Mapao Jesu, iwui mangankhali khaphanlu! Kala aya phakhur phumda kaho: O Mapao, kakhama hi athumwui chungli machonlu! Hi hoda aya thikahaisai. Saulna awui thikahaili ningkachang phungsai.
chapters.english_translation: And Stephen, full of faith and power, did great wonders and miracles among the people. And all that sat in the council, looking stedfastly on him, saw his face as it had been the face of an angel. But he, being full of the Holy Ghost, looked up stedfastly into heaven, and saw the glory of God. And they stoned Stephen, calling upon God, and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep. And Saul was consenting unto his death.

vocabulary.meaning: calling out with loud voice, invoking
lay not to charge, impute not
kneeled down, fell on knees in prayer

chapters.grammar_notes: Instrumental postposition '-na' on 'lungna' marks the lethal physical instrument: by means of stones.

exercises.question: What two prayers did Stephen utter before his death?
Who was recorded as consenting to Stephen's death?

chapters.title: Corneliusli Pao Kazang (Conversion of Cornelius)
chapters.summary: Peter's vision of the clean and unclean animals, journey to Caesarea, and the gospel opened to the Gentiles.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Caesarea ramli Cornelius kahona Italian cohortwui centurion akhat pamsai. Aya Varivarali kacharan, awui shim kachiva ngasoda, miwungli dori khami kala Varivarali thang kachiva khangamor. Peterna Caesareali rada hosa: Kaphung-kachangli ina theisai Varivarana mi akhatli kaching mei mana; kha ram kachivali Ali kacharan kala mashungkasa chi Awui ningkachang phungsai. Peterna tui hi holikha Mangan Katharana tui ngashonbing kachivawui chungli rasai!
chapters.english_translation: There was a certain man in Caesarea called Cornelius, a centurion of the band called the Italian band, A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway. Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him. While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word.

vocabulary.meaning: does not show partiality, no respecter of persons
alms, charitable offerings to the needy

chapters.grammar_notes: The negative comparative 'kaching mei mana' (literally: does not exceed in biased viewing) translates impartial justice.

exercises.question: What was the occupation of Cornelius in Caesarea?
What theological breakthrough did Peter announce in Acts 10:34-35?

chapters.title: Athens Ramli Paulna Tui Chitheikahai (Paul at the Areopagus)
chapters.summary: Paul's sermon at Mars Hill in Athens concerning the Unknown God, repentance, and resurrection.
chapters.tangkhul_text: Paulna Areopagus (Mars Hill) ngachaili ngakarangda hosa: Athens miwung, ina theisai nithum thang kachiva kameo khangamor phungsai; maramchilu ina zatli nithumwui altar akhatli kaphika theisai: MATHIKAHAI VARIVARALI. Nithumna matheila khangamor hili ina chitheikhami! Kazing kala ngalei kala chili leisatha kachiva sakahai Varivara chili kazing kala ngaleiwui Mapaosai, Aya mina sakahai templeli mapam mana; maramchilu Awui chungli ithum haring, zatta, kala pamsai; nithumwui la-kashabingna hokatha: 'Ithumya Awui kachung thotsai.'
chapters.english_translation: Then Paul stood in the midst of Mars' hill, and said, Ye men of Athens, I perceive that in all things ye are too superstitious. For as I passed by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription, TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I unto you. God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands; For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.

vocabulary.meaning: traditional nature spirits, idols, lesser deities
offspring, lineage, children of the divine

chapters.grammar_notes: Pettigrew contrasts indigenous 'Kameo' (animistic spirits) with the sovereign 'Varivara' (Creator of heaven and earth).

exercises.question: What inscription did Paul encounter in Athens?
How did Paul quote the Greek poets in Tangkhul?

pages.header: Chapter 2: Pentecost Thangli Mangan Kathara (Day of Pentecost) (Page 7)
pages.title: Chapter 2: Pentecost Thangli Mangan Kathara (Day of Pentecost)
lines: CHAPTER 2: PENTECOST THANGLI MANGAN KATHARA (DAY OF PENTECOST)
Summary: The descent of the Holy Spirit like rushing wind and tongues of fire, and Peter's first sermon.
Pentecost kumshang phungphatli nithum pam akhangli zikahai pamsai.
Kazingwui huchiphung majung katha khara rasai, kala athum pamsahai shim
kachivali kapingsai. Kala meiwui malei katha khangayeida athum
kachivawui kachungli rasai. Kala athum kachiva Mangan Katharana kapingda
ngatei tui khangayei hosa! Peterna ngakarangda hosa: Israel miwung, tui
hi ngashonlu: Nazarethwui Jesu hili Varivarana thikahaiwui ngachaili
thingkashangsai; chiwui maramli ithum kachiva sakhibing thotsai. Ningzan
ngashunlu, kala nithum kachiva Jesu Christawui minli baptisma sayanlu!
And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one
accord in one place. And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a
rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were
sitting. And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire,
and it sat upon each of them. And they were all filled with the Holy
Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues. Then Peter stood up and
said, Ye men of Israel, hear these words; This Jesus hath God raised up,
whereof we all are witnesses. Repent, and be baptized every one of you
in the name of Jesus Christ.

pages.title: Chapter 2 Exercises & Vocabulary
lines: * Huchiphung (noun): rushing mighty wind, storm force
* Ngatei tui (noun phrase): other languages, diverse tongues
* Ningzan ngashun (verb phrase): to repent, rectify the mind and heart
- The verbal phrase 'ningzan ngashunlu' fuses 'ningzan' (heart-contrition) with 'ngashun' (to make straight).

pages.header: Chapter 3: Temple Gate wui Pamli Thotkhamatei (Lame Man at the Beautiful Gate) (Page 10)
pages.title: Chapter 3: Temple Gate wui Pamli Thotkhamatei (Lame Man at the Beautiful Gate)
lines: CHAPTER 3: TEMPLE GATE WUI PAMLI THOTKHAMATEI (LAME MAN AT THE BEAUTIFUL GATE)
Summary: Healing of the lame man by Peter and John at the Beautiful Gate of the Temple.
Peter kala John thangkhamir pung chiko khangamor thangli Templeli
zangvangasai. Phaphuk khazat akhat, awui phankahaiwui thotli theisai,
aya Templewui Mathan Gate kahowali pamsai; aya Peter kala Johnli theida
seisan khamor khanasai. Peterna hosa: Rupa kala sona iwui chungli mathai
mana; kha ina phungli nali khamlikha: Nazarethwui Jesu Christawui minli
ngakarangda zatlu! Kala ayana awui pangkasho pangda thingkasangsai;
chitharan awui phakhur kala pharu pangmashan phungsai! Aya ngachor-da
ngakarangsai kala zat-zangsai, Templeli zangda khangachor kala
Now Peter and John went up together into the temple at the hour of
prayer, being the ninth hour. And a certain man lame from his mother's
womb was carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the temple which
is called Beautiful, to ask alms of them that entered into the temple.
Then Peter said, Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I
thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk. And he
took him by the right hand, and lifted him up: and immediately his feet
and ankle bones received strength. And he leaping up stood, and walked,
and entered with them into the temple, walking, and leaping, and
pages.tangkhul_content: Peter kala John thangkhamir pung chiko khangamor thangli Templeli zangvangasai. Phaphuk khazat akhat, awui phankahaiwui thotli theisai, aya Templewui Mathan Gate kahowali pamsai; aya Peter kala Johnli theida seisan khamor khanasai. Peterna hosa: Rupa kala sona iwui chungli mathai mana; kha ina phungli nali khamlikha: Nazarethwui Jesu Christawui minli ngakarangda zatlu! Kala ayana awui pangkasho pangda thingkasangsai; chitharan awui phakhur kala pharu pangmashan phungsai! Aya ngachor-da ngakarangsai kala zat-zangsai, Templeli zangda khangachor kala Varivarali mathankashei sasai.
pages.english_translation: Now Peter and John went up together into the temple at the hour of prayer, being the ninth hour. And a certain man lame from his mother's womb was carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the temple which is called Beautiful, to ask alms of them that entered into the temple. Then Peter said, Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk. And he took him by the right hand, and lifted him up: and immediately his feet and ankle bones received strength. And he leaping up stood, and walked, and entered with them into the temple, walking, and leaping, and praising God.

lines: * Phaphuk khazat (noun phrase): lame from birth, crippled in the feet

* Khangachor (verb participle): leaping, dancing with joyous vigor

pages.header: Chapter 4: Councilwui Phungli Sakhi Chitheikahai (Before the Sanhedrin) (Page 12)
pages.title: Chapter 4: Councilwui Phungli Sakhi Chitheikahai (Before the Sanhedrin)
lines: CHAPTER 4: COUNCILWUI PHUNGLI SAKHI CHITHEIKAHAI (BEFORE THE SANHEDRIN)
Summary: Peter and John arrested and questioned before the rulers, elders, and scribes of the Council.
Athumna Peter kala Johnli ngachaili pamsahai hosa: Khipawui pangmashan
kala minli nithumna hi sakha? Peterna Mangan Katharana kapingda hosa:
Miwungwui khararbing kala Israelwui Hangvabing, ngatei khipawui
chunglikha haring kaphan mathailak mana; maramchilu kazing kaphungli
miwungli khami ngatei min khikha mathai mana! Kha athumna Peter kala
Johnna ngahanda hosa: Nithumwui tui ngashon-katha Varivarawui tui
ngashon-katha khipana mashungkha nithum shanshilu! Maramchilu ithumna
theikahai kala ngashokahai tui masasa pamtang mathailak mana.
And when they had set them in the midst, they asked, By what power, or
by what name, have ye done this? Then Peter, filled with the Holy Ghost,
said unto them, Ye rulers of the people, and elders of Israel, Neither
is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under
heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved. But Peter and John
answered and said unto them, Whether it be right in the sight of God to
hearken unto you more than unto God, judge ye. For we cannot but speak
the things which we have seen and heard.
pages.tangkhul_content: Athumna Peter kala Johnli ngachaili pamsahai hosa: Khipawui pangmashan kala minli nithumna hi sakha? Peterna Mangan Katharana kapingda hosa: Miwungwui khararbing kala Israelwui Hangvabing, ngatei khipawui chunglikha haring kaphan mathailak mana; maramchilu kazing kaphungli miwungli khami ngatei min khikha mathai mana! Kha athumna Peter kala Johnna ngahanda hosa: Nithumwui tui ngashon-katha Varivarawui tui ngashon-katha khipana mashungkha nithum shanshilu! Maramchilu ithumna theikahai kala ngashokahai tui masasa pamtang mathailak mana.
pages.english_translation: And when they had set them in the midst, they asked, By what power, or by what name, have ye done this? Then Peter, filled with the Holy Ghost, said unto them, Ye rulers of the people, and elders of Israel, Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved. But Peter and John answered and said unto them, Whether it be right in the sight of God to hearken unto you more than unto God, judge ye. For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard.

pages.title: Chapter 4 Exercises & Vocabulary
lines: * Hangvabing (noun plural): council of elders, senators, Sanhedrin magistrates
* Kazing kaphungli (prepositional phrase): under heaven, beneath the celestial dome
* Ngashon-katha (verb phrase): to hearken, obey, submit to authority
* Shanshilu (imperative verb): judge ye, weigh and determine
- Pettigrew uses the indigenous administrative title 'Hangvabing' (village elder bench) for the Sanhedrin rulers.

pages.header: Chapter 5: Stephenwui Pao kala Kashung Thot (The Martyrdom of Stephen) (Page 14)
pages.title: Chapter 5: Stephenwui Pao kala Kashung Thot (The Martyrdom of Stephen)
lines: CHAPTER 5: STEPHENWUI PAO KALA KASHUNG THOT (THE MARTYRDOM OF STEPHEN)
Summary: Stephen's defense before the council, vision of the Son of Man, and stoning as the first Christian martyr.
Stephenna ning-kachang kala pangmashan phungda miwungwui ngachaili
theichithei kaphung sasai. Council shimli pambing kachivana ali theida
awui mai kazingram kachisowui mai katha theisai. Kha aya Mangan
Katharana kapingda kazingli theida Varivarawui mathankashak theisai.
Kala athumna lungna chidatli Stephenna khon-kaphung: O Mapao Jesu, iwui
mangankhali khaphanlu! Kala aya phakhur phumda kaho: O Mapao, kakhama hi
athumwui chungli machonlu! Hi hoda aya thikahaisai. Saulna awui
And Stephen, full of faith and power, did great wonders and miracles
among the people. And all that sat in the council, looking stedfastly on
him, saw his face as it had been the face of an angel. But he, being
full of the Holy Ghost, looked up stedfastly into heaven, and saw the
glory of God. And they stoned Stephen, calling upon God, and saying,
Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. And he kneeled down, and cried with a
loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said
this, he fell asleep. And Saul was consenting unto his death.
pages.tangkhul_content: Stephenna ning-kachang kala pangmashan phungda miwungwui ngachaili theichithei kaphung sasai. Council shimli pambing kachivana ali theida awui mai kazingram kachisowui mai katha theisai. Kha aya Mangan Katharana kapingda kazingli theida Varivarawui mathankashak theisai. Kala athumna lungna chidatli Stephenna khon-kaphung: O Mapao Jesu, iwui mangankhali khaphanlu! Kala aya phakhur phumda kaho: O Mapao, kakhama hi athumwui chungli machonlu! Hi hoda aya thikahaisai. Saulna awui thikahaili ningkachang phungsai.
pages.english_translation: And Stephen, full of faith and power, did great wonders and miracles among the people. And all that sat in the council, looking stedfastly on him, saw his face as it had been the face of an angel. But he, being full of the Holy Ghost, looked up stedfastly into heaven, and saw the glory of God. And they stoned Stephen, calling upon God, and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep. And Saul was consenting unto his death.

pages.title: Chapter 5 Exercises & Vocabulary
lines: * Lungna chidat (verb phrase): cast stones, stoned with rocks
* Khon-kaphung (verb participle): calling out with loud voice, invoking
* Machonlu (imperative negative): lay not to charge, impute not
* Phakhur phum (verb phrase): kneeled down, fell on knees in prayer
- Instrumental postposition '-na' on 'lungna' marks the lethal physical instrument: by means of stones.

? Who was recorded as consenting to Stephen's death?

Khon-kaphung: calling out with loud voice, invoking
Machonlu: lay not to charge, impute not
Phakhur phum: kneeled down, fell on knees in prayer
pages.english_translation: Instrumental postposition '-na' on 'lungna' marks the lethal physical instrument: by means of stones.

pages.header: Chapter 6: Corneliusli Pao Kazang (Conversion of Cornelius) (Page 16)
pages.title: Chapter 6: Corneliusli Pao Kazang (Conversion of Cornelius)
lines: CHAPTER 6: CORNELIUSLI PAO KAZANG (CONVERSION OF CORNELIUS)
Summary: Peter's vision of the clean and unclean animals, journey to Caesarea, and the gospel opened to the Gentiles.
Caesarea ramli Cornelius kahona Italian cohortwui centurion akhat
pamsai. Aya Varivarali kacharan, awui shim kachiva ngasoda, miwungli
dori khami kala Varivarali thang kachiva khangamor. Peterna Caesareali
rada hosa: Kaphung-kachangli ina theisai Varivarana mi akhatli kaching
mei mana; kha ram kachivali Ali kacharan kala mashungkasa chi Awui
ningkachang phungsai. Peterna tui hi holikha Mangan Katharana tui
There was a certain man in Caesarea called Cornelius, a centurion of the
band called the Italian band, A devout man, and one that feared God with
all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God
alway. Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that
God is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him,
and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him. While Peter yet spake
these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word.
pages.tangkhul_content: Caesarea ramli Cornelius kahona Italian cohortwui centurion akhat pamsai. Aya Varivarali kacharan, awui shim kachiva ngasoda, miwungli dori khami kala Varivarali thang kachiva khangamor. Peterna Caesareali rada hosa: Kaphung-kachangli ina theisai Varivarana mi akhatli kaching mei mana; kha ram kachivali Ali kacharan kala mashungkasa chi Awui ningkachang phungsai. Peterna tui hi holikha Mangan Katharana tui ngashonbing kachivawui chungli rasai!
pages.english_translation: There was a certain man in Caesarea called Cornelius, a centurion of the band called the Italian band, A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway. Then Peter opened his mouth, and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is no respecter of persons: But in every nation he that feareth him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with him. While Peter yet spake these words, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the word.

pages.title: Chapter 6 Exercises & Vocabulary
lines: * Kaching mei mana (idiomatic clause): does not show partiality, no respecter of persons
* Dori (noun): alms, charitable offerings to the needy
- The negative comparative 'kaching mei mana' (literally: does not exceed in biased viewing) translates impartial justice.
? What was the occupation of Cornelius in Caesarea?
? What theological breakthrough did Peter announce in Acts 10:34-35?
pages.tangkhul_content:
Kaching mei mana: does not show partiality, no respecter of persons
Kacharan: reverent, God-fearing, devout
Dori: alms, charitable offerings to the needy
Ningkachang: favor, delight, divine acceptance
pages.english_translation: The negative comparative 'kaching mei mana' (literally: does not exceed in biased viewing) translates impartial justice.

pages.header: Chapter 7: Athens Ramli Paulna Tui Chitheikahai (Paul at the Areopagus) (Page 18)
pages.title: Chapter 7: Athens Ramli Paulna Tui Chitheikahai (Paul at the Areopagus)
lines: CHAPTER 7: ATHENS RAMLI PAULNA TUI CHITHEIKAHAI (PAUL AT THE AREOPAGUS)
Summary: Paul's sermon at Mars Hill in Athens concerning the Unknown God, repentance, and resurrection.
Paulna Areopagus (Mars Hill) ngachaili ngakarangda hosa: Athens miwung,
ina theisai nithum thang kachiva kameo khangamor phungsai; maramchilu
ina zatli nithumwui altar akhatli kaphika theisai: MATHIKAHAI
VARIVARALI. Nithumna matheila khangamor hili ina chitheikhami! Kazing
kala ngalei kala chili leisatha kachiva sakahai Varivara chili kazing
kala ngaleiwui Mapaosai, Aya mina sakahai templeli mapam mana;
maramchilu Awui chungli ithum haring, zatta, kala pamsai; nithumwui la-
Then Paul stood in the midst of Mars' hill, and said, Ye men of Athens,
I perceive that in all things ye are too superstitious. For as I passed
by, and beheld your devotions, I found an altar with this inscription,
TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Whom therefore ye ignorantly worship, him declare I
unto you. God that made the world and all things therein, seeing that he
is Lord of heaven and earth, dwelleth not in temples made with hands;
For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of
your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.
pages.tangkhul_content: Paulna Areopagus (Mars Hill) ngachaili ngakarangda hosa: Athens miwung, ina theisai nithum thang kachiva kameo khangamor phungsai; maramchilu ina zatli nithumwui altar akhatli kaphika theisai: MATHIKAHAI VARIVARALI. Nithumna matheila khangamor hili ina chitheikhami! Kazing kala ngalei kala chili leisatha kachiva sakahai Varivara chili kazing kala ngaleiwui Mapaosai, Aya mina sakahai templeli mapam mana; maramchilu Awui chungli ithum haring, zatta, kala pamsai; nithumwui la-kashabingna hokatha: 'Ithumya Awui kachung thotsai.'

pages.title: Chapter 7 Exercises & Vocabulary
lines: * Mathikahai Varivara (noun phrase): Unknown God, the unrevealed Creator
* Kameo (noun): traditional nature spirits, idols, lesser deities
* La-kashabing (noun plural): poets, ballad makers, lyricists
* Kachung (noun): offspring, lineage, children of the divine
- Pettigrew contrasts indigenous 'Kameo' (animistic spirits) with the sovereign 'Varivara' (Creator of heaven and earth).
? What inscription did Paul encounter in Athens?
? How did Paul quote the Greek poets in Tangkhul?
